text:
Comic Sans, you were literally designed for a talking dog in Microsoft Bob, and somehow you're the only part of that project that didn't die with dignity. Vincent Connare made you in 1994 for cartoon speech bubbles, and you heard that and thought, "Tombstones. Legal notices. Resignation letters."

Dan Gilbert wrote his furious LeBron James letter in you, and that's why nobody remembers being scared. CERN announced the Higgs boson, the most important physics discovery in fifty years, in you, and the entire scientific community went, "Did a third grader find God?"

People defend you because you help some readers with dyslexia, which is true and lovely, and also the only time you've ever been used responsibly.

You're not a font. You're a bake sale flyer that got tenure. Even Papyrus looks at you and says, "Wow, okay, tone it down."

Papyrus, look at you. A 23-year-old drew you with a calligraphy pen in 1982, trying to imagine what English would look like 2,000 years ago, and somehow you became the official font of every place that sells crystals next to a tanning bed. You're on yoga studios, hookah lounges, and the church bake sale flyer for "Loaves & Fishes & Brownies."

Your letters look like they were chiseled by a Pharaoh with a hangover. That little floaty bar on your capital E? Even your crossbars are trying to leave.

James Cameron spent a billion dollars inventing an alien language, then labeled the poster with a font that came free with Microsoft Office. Ryan Gosling got an entire SNL sketch out of being haunted by you.

Even your creator says he's sick of you. Comic Sans has haters. You have a dad who wants a refund.

Comic Sans, you were born in 1994 to put words in the mouth of a cartoon dog in Microsoft Bob, and somehow you're the one that survived. Bob is dead. The dog is dead. You're on a sympathy card at a funeral home.

You were inspired by Batman comics, and you've never once been near anything heroic. CERN used you to announce the Higgs boson: humanity's greatest discovery, presented like a lemonade stand. Dan Gilbert used you to call LeBron a traitor, because nothing says "furious billionaire" like bubble letters.

And your defense is always "Well, I help dyslexic readers." Great. You're the guy at the party whose whole personality is a doctor's note.

Even Vincent Connare, the man who made you, says he's barely ever used you. Your own dad won't put you on the fridge.

Comic Sans这个字体，出身就很尴尬。1994年微软设计它，是给一只卡通狗说话用的，就是Microsoft Bob里那只狗，对话框里的字。结果字还没赶上，软件先黄了。狗失业了，字留下来了，开始替全人类说话。

这就麻烦了，它天生就是狗的口音啊！你用它写“生日快乐”，没问题，狗很开心。你用它写“电梯故障，已困三人”，就像一只狗摇着尾巴跑来通知你出事了。

最狠的是2012年，欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子，人类物理学最伟大的时刻之一，PPT用的就是Comic Sans。几千个博士，几十亿欧元，找到了“上帝粒子”，然后派一只卡通狗上台宣布。

我觉得上帝看完都想换个字体，把宇宙重新造一遍。

Papyrus, you were designed in 1982 by a 23-year-old with calligraphy pens and a dream of ancient Egypt, and somehow you still look like you were drawn by someone shivering. Your edges are so rough you need exfoliating. You promised the wisdom of the Nile and delivered the vibe of a chiropractor's tri-fold brochure. Every day spa, hookah lounge, and "Inner Journey" yoga retreat found you in the dropdown menu and whispered, "This feels ancient." James Cameron spent $237 million on *Avatar* and then used you for the logo, which is like building the Taj Mahal and signing it in crayon. Ryan Gosling lost sleep over you on national television. You're not a typeface; you're a cry for help with ragged little serifs. Even Comic Sans looks at you and says, "At least I know I'm a joke."

你们知道Comic Sans这个字体最早是给谁设计的吗？给一条狗。九十年代微软有个软件，里面有只卡通狗，它说话的气泡里用的就是这个字。后来软件死了，狗失业了，字活下来了，开始到处打零工。

最离谱的一次是2012年，欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子。人类几十年、几十亿欧元，物理学史上最重要的时刻之一，PPT用的是Comic Sans！全世界最聪明的一群人站在台上，大屏幕上的字看着像幼儿园通知：“小朋友们，明天带一个上帝粒子来做手工哦~”

你看它那个字母，没有一笔是直的，每个字都像刚喝完两杯在那儿晃。它不是字体，它是一只狗在用爪子打字。

所以我现在判断一个文件严不严肃，就看字体。合同用宋体，我认真读；用Comic Sans，我第一反应是：这甲方，是条狗吧？

你们知道Papyrus这个字体吗？就是那种边缘毛毛糙糙、像被老鼠啃过的英文字。设计师当年二十三岁，拿笔在纹理纸上描了半年，想的是两千年前的中东古卷。结果呢？古卷没用上，全用在楼下的美甲店了。

你看它都出现在哪：瑜伽馆、养生会所、有机藜麦沙拉。只要老板想说“我们很灵性，所以贵三十”，就用它。

最离谱的是《阿凡达》。卡梅隆花几个亿造了一整颗星球，片名用的是Word下拉菜单里白送的字体。哥，那是潘多拉星，不是你二姨的足疗店！

后来拍续集，全世界都在笑他，他终于改了：改成了一个稍微修过的Papyrus。这不叫改，这叫同一个人换了个发型。

PHP. You started as "Personal Home Page," then rebranded as "PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor," a recursive acronym, because even your name couldn't commit to a stable API.

For twenty years, "abc" == 0 was true, and you called it "type juggling," like a clown proud of dropping things.

strpos takes haystack, needle. array_search takes needle, haystack. That's not argument order; that's mood swings.

Your parse error says T_PAAMAYIM_NEKUDOTAYIM. That's Hebrew for "double colon" and English for "good luck."

You skipped version 6 entirely. Even your release numbers just wanted to move on.

You shipped mysql_real_escape_string, implying the first one was a hoax.

Facebook loved you so much they invented Hack just to avoid touching you.

But sure, you power most of the web. Mostly WordPress. That's like bragging your biggest fan is a raccoon.

我最怕的字体叫Papyrus。你肯定见过：每个字母边缘都毛毛糙糙，像被老鼠啃过一圈。设计师当年二十三岁，说他在想象“两千年前的中东人写英文会是什么样”。兄弟，两千年前的中东人不写英文啊！你这是给法老报了个英语口语班！

结果现在它在哪儿？足疗店、茶馆、瑜伽馆，凡是想显得“我很有灵性”的，招牌一律Papyrus。最离谱的是《阿凡达》，花两亿多美元造外星人，片名用的是电脑自带字体。那个A，横杠飘到头顶，像系了条头巾。卡梅隆，你的潘多拉星跟楼下“禅意养生”，用的是同一张脸！

PHP, you started life as "Personal Home Page," and somehow you now run most of the internet, which explains a lot about the internet. Your own creator said he's "not a real programmer," and honestly, it shows. Is it needle then haystack, or haystack then needle? strpos and in_array have been in a custody battle since 1995. You gave us mysql_escape_string, then mysql_real_escape_string, because apparently the first one was just pretending. Your loose equality swears "0e123" equals "0e456," since both are zero in scientific notation. Your error message for a double colon is T_PAAMAYIM_NEKUDOTAYIM, which is Hebrew, because English wasn't confusing enough. You skipped version 6 entirely, like a kid hiding a report card. Facebook loved you so much they had to rewrite you as a different language. But hey, you power WordPress, so you'll outlive all of us.

我写PHP八年了，最大的收获是：每个变量前面都得加个美元符号。$name，$age，$user。写着写着我就懂了，这不是在写代码，是在报账。

PHP的函数命名特别有个性。strlen，连着写；str_replace，加下划线。查字符串用strpos，参数先写"大海"再写"针"；到了in_array，又变成先"针"后"大海"。就像你家门锁，周一往左拧，周二往右拧。

还有比较。以前字符串"abc"等于数字0，PHP说：对，相等。我说你认真的？它说：要认真，请用三个等号。

后来官方都绷不住了，PHP 5直接跳到PHP 7，PHP 6没了。这不叫迭代，这叫销毁证据。

我写PHP十年了。PHP每个变量前面都得加美元符号，$name，$password。它在提醒你：这里的每一行，迟早都要付出代价。

找东西的函数，strpos先传大海再传针，in_array先传针再传大海。同一门语言，规矩看心情。

转义数据库输入，先给你一个mysql_escape_string，后来又出了个mysql_real_escape_string。real！意思是之前那个是骗你的。

有一次它报错：T_PAAMAYIM_NEKUDOTAYIM。希伯来语，"双冒号"。半夜两点，我被一门编程语言用希伯来语骂了。

JavaScript, you were built in ten days, and you've spent thirty years proving it. You named yourself after Java for the clout, like a guy introducing himself as "Brad Pitt's cousin." You think null is an object. You think NaN is a number, and it isn't even equal to itself. Ask you to sort and you hand back, alphabetically, like a librarian having a breakdown. "11" plus 1 is "111," but "11" minus 1 is 10, so you're consistent the way a slot machine is consistent. You needed two kinds of nothing, undefined and null, and three equals signs just to tell the truth. Your own developers can't agree what "this" means. And the entire internet runs on you, which honestly explains the internet.
text_raw: JavaScript, you were built in ten days, and you've spent thirty years proving it. You named yourself after Java for the clout, like a guy introducing himself as "Brad Pitt's cousin." You think null is an object. You think NaN is a number, and it isn't even equal to itself. Ask you to sort [10, 1, 3] and you hand back [1, 10, 3], alphabetically, like a librarian having a breakdown. "11" plus 1 is "111," but "11" minus 1 is 10, so you're consistent the way a slot machine is consistent. You needed two kinds of nothing, undefined and null, and three equals signs just to tell the truth. Your own developers can't agree what "this" means. And the entire internet runs on you, which honestly explains the internet.

text:
我学JavaScript三个月，最大的收获是：不再相信任何人。

"5"减3，等于2。挺好，懂事。
"5"加3，等于"53"。……你刚才不是还会算术吗？

我问它，null是什么类型？它说：对象。
空的东西是对象。这不是编程语言，这是我妈给我介绍对象的标准。

还有NaN，意思是"不是一个数字"。你猜typeof NaN是什么？number。
"不是数字"是个数字。
更狠的是NaN不等于它自己。连自己都不认识自己，它比我还迷茫。

后来我给数组排序，10、9、1，排完变成1、10、9。
它按字符串排的。
我说你这叫排序？它说：你先用三个等号，再跟我说话。

我学JavaScript第一天，老师问："字符串五减三等于几？"我说二。对。"那字符串五加三呢？"我说八。错，是"53"。减号会算数，加号不会，这加法是体育老师教的吧？

后来我发现它连自己都不认识。NaN，意思是"不是数字"，你问它typeof，它说："我是number。"你问NaN等不等于NaN，它说不等于。这不是变量，这是失忆症患者。

最绝的是排序。10、9、1，让它排一下，它给你排成1、10、9，因为它默认按字符串排。我问它懂不懂数学，它说："兄弟，我是十天写出来的，你还想咋样？"

哦对了，它跟Java一点关系都没有。就跟老婆饼里没有老婆一样。

PMMA, you're literally Plexiglas. Somewhere your cousin is a sneeze guard at Chipotle, and honestly? Your cousin has better etch resistance. One whiff of plasma and you vanish faster than a grad student's weekend.

You've been the "gold standard" since the 1970s, which is a polite way of saying nobody's been able to fire you. You need hundreds of microcoulombs just to *notice* the beam. A 40-hour write for one wafer. Glacial, but sure, sub-10-nanometer lines, we get it.

Positive resist? Overdose you and you cross-link into a *negative* one. That's not versatility, that's an identity crisis.

You get developed in MIBK, which smells like regret, and you come in 495K and 950K because one of you alone can't even do liftoff. And acetone dissolves you instantly. Even your solvents think you're temporary.

JavaScript, you were built in ten days, and honestly? It shows. You're named after Java the way a knockoff purse is named after Gucci.

You think null is an object. You think NaN is a number. NaN doesn't even equal itself, which makes it the only thing in you with any self-awareness.

Ask you to sort and you hand back, because you alphabetize numbers like a drunk librarian. "11" plus 1 is "111", but "11" minus 1 is 10. Pick a lane.

You needed a second equals sign just to stop lying, and nobody, including you, knows what "this" means.

January is month zero. One guy unpublishing left-pad broke half the internet. And your node_modules folder is heavier than a black hole.

Every week there's a new framework to fix you. That's not a language. That's a renovation.

Ask you to sort [10, 1, 3] and you hand back [1, 10, 3], because you alphabetize numbers like a drunk librarian. "11" plus 1 is "111", but "11" minus 1 is 10. Pick a lane.

You needed a second equals sign just to stop lying, and nobody, including you, knows what "this" means.

January is month zero. One guy unpublishing left-pad broke half the internet. And your node_modules folder is heavier than a black hole.

Every week there's a new framework to fix you. That's not a language. That's a renovation.

text: PMMA, you're the same plastic as a hockey rink window, and somehow that's your most dignified job. You've been "high resolution" since the 1970s, which is like bragging about your SAT score at your retirement party. Sure, you'll resolve sub-10-nanometer lines, if someone stands there blasting you with electrons for an eternity. Your sensitivity is so low the beam current has gotten tenure. You don't even develop properly without MIBK and IPA holding your hand in a one-to-three ratio. And your whole personality is chain scission: you literally fall apart when someone pays attention to you. Then hit you with too much dose and you crosslink and flip to negative tone, a full identity crisis. And dry etch? You melt in plasma faster than an ice sculpture at a barbecue. Honestly, the only thing you're consistently good at is lift-off: leaving.

HSQ, everybody! The only resist that ages faster than the grad student using it. You spin it Monday, expose it Tuesday, and suddenly your dose curve has gone through a midlife crisis. It has to live in the fridge like expired yogurt, and it's about as forgiving.

HSQ brags about sub-10-nanometer lines. Sure, if you've got six hours of write time, because this diva needs a dose that could sterilize a hospital. Then you develop it in TMAH, or, if you're desperate, *salt water*. Your whole career is literally seasoned with tears now.

And once it's exposed? It turns into glass. Brittle, cracking glass. You wanted a mask; you got a window that shatters when you look at it. Want it gone? Hope you enjoy hydrofluoric acid, the chemical that dissolves your bones.

HSQ: beautiful resolution, terrible personality. It's not negative-tone. It's just negative.

HSQ, ladies and gentlemen: the only resist with sub-10-nanometer resolution and the personality of a sourdough starter. You buy it, you refrigerate it, and it *still* starts gelling in the bottle like it's got somewhere better to be. Shelf life measured in "eh, few months, maybe."

And slow? HSQ needs a dose so high the e-beam tool files for overtime. Your PMMA friends finished their write and went home; you're still exposing alignment marks.

Then you develop it in TMAH, or, if you want contrast, *salty* developer. Yes, this resist literally needs you to add salt. Even Gordon Ramsay thinks that's a lot.

But the real red flag? Once it's exposed, it turns into glass. Permanently. You want it gone? Hydrofluoric acid. That's not a resist, that's a relationship you can only leave with a hazmat suit.

Still, gorgeous lines. Shame they collapse when they dry.

我读博做电子束光刻，用的胶叫PMMA。说出来挺高级，其实就是亚克力，奶茶店挡你口水的那块板子。我每天在洁净室穿得像宇航员，伺候的是鱼缸。

它是正胶，电子打上去它断链，断了才洗得掉。先被打碎才能成才，跟我导师培养我一个思路。

分辨率能到十纳米，但灵敏度极低，一个图曝一晚上。剂量打多了还不行，它会交联，正胶当场变负胶，原地叛变。

最气人的是不抗刻蚀，等离子一吹就没了。辛苦画了十纳米，一刻，鱼缸化了。

所以大家拿它做剥离，它唯一的使命就是被丙酮泡掉。组里用我，也是这个思路。

我们实验室有种胶叫HSQ，负性电子束胶，号称能写十纳米以下的线。听着高端吧？它是有保质期的，得放冰箱。我们组冰箱里，左边是酸奶，右边是HSQ，酸奶都比它扛放。旋涂完你还不能歇着，放久了它自己就开始“老化”，剂量全变。这胶跟你谈恋爱：“你要么现在曝光我，要么就别曝光了。”

曝它还得给大剂量，电子枪一写写一宿，我在旁边陪着，跟守灵似的。好不容易写完，显影还得用含盐的显影液。我一个读博的，天天在给芯片腌咸菜。

最绝的是曝完它就变成二氧化硅了。你想去掉？得上氢氟酸。结果它是没了，我底下那层氧化硅也跟着没了。这哪是光刻胶，这是跟我同归于尽来了。

我读博做纳米加工，用PMMA电子束光刻胶。PMMA是啥？亚克力，奶茶店那块挡板。几十万一小时的电子束机器，伺候的是奶茶店挡板。

它还特娇气。剂量少了，显影完啥也没有；剂量多了，它直接交联，从正胶变成负胶。被电急了当场换立场，比我导师还善变。

显影液是MIBK兑异丙醇，一比三，泡几十秒，多泡一会儿线条就胖了。好不容易做出来拿去刻蚀，它扛不住，比底下的硅先没。

最后只能剥离，丙酮里泡一夜。我问师兄成功率多少，他说：“看PMMA心情。”我说一块亚克力有啥心情？他说：“分子量九十五万，心思比你多。”

我读博搞纳米加工，用的光刻胶叫HSQ。它分辨率能做到几个纳米，号称胶界学霸。但学霸脾气大：得放冰箱里冻着，拿出来放久了它自己就开始交联。你还没曝光，它先把自己“曝光”了，这叫提前躺平。

它还特别迟钝，剂量得打到别的胶好几倍。电子束写一片样品写一整晚，我跟机器一起熬，机器好歹还有冷却水。

显影用TMAH，师兄说加点盐对比度更好。我一个搞半导体的，天天在实验室称氯化钠配盐水，像在腌咸菜。

最绝的是，曝光完它直接变成二氧化硅，就是玻璃。写错了想洗掉？丙酮没用，得上氢氟酸。别的胶犯错是擦掉重来，HSQ犯错，得先签危化品登记表。

Vim. The only program where "how do I leave?" has more Stack Overflow views than most religions have followers. Two million people asked, and the answer was colon, q, exclamation point, which reads less like a command and more like a hostage's final words.

Vim stands for "Vi Improved." Improved from a 1976 terminal whose arrow keys were printed on H, J, K, and L. Fifty years later, Vim's still out here like, "Why fix what you can turn into a personality?"

You don't type in Vim. You type a sentence, then discover you deleted four lines, yanked a paragraph into register W, and started recording a macro.

Crash it once and it leaves a .swp file behind, like a ghost whispering, "Recover, Edit anyway, Quit, or Abort?"

Even its fans forked it. Neovim exists because Vim users wanted Vim, minus Vim.

Vim, you're the only text editor with its own hostage negotiation thread. Millions of people have viewed the Stack Overflow question on how to leave you. That's not a user base, that's a missing persons report.

You have modes. Normal mode, where typing does nothing normal, and Insert mode, hidden behind the letter "i" like a secret menu.

Your fans move the cursor with h, j, k, l because a terminal from 1976 printed arrows on those keys. That's not efficiency, that's Stockholm syndrome on the home row.

Every Vim user has a 900-line .vimrc copied from a stranger and is too scared to touch it. And when you crash, you leave .swp files behind like a burglar who signs the guestbook.

Even your own kids forked you into Neovim. That's not a fork. That's an intervention.

Goodnight! :wq… :q!… ESC ESC ESC…

我第一次用Vim，是git commit自己弹出来的。我没请它，它就来了。

我上来就打字，屏幕上一个字没有，光标在那儿乱跳。在Vim里，字母不是字母，是方向盘。你想打hello：h往左挪一格，e跳到词尾，l往右，再l往右，o……恭喜，它给你新开了一行。

你得先按i才能打字。打字，还得先申请。

写完想走，Esc，冒号，q。它说有改动没保存。冒号wq，它说只读文件，要加感叹号。我说我就想走！冒号q感叹号！

“怎么退出Vim”这个问题，两百多万人看过。这不是编辑器，这是密室逃脱，门把手是个冒号。

Emacs is a beautiful operating system. Shame it never shipped with a decent text editor. That's why half its users install evil-mode: they love Emacs so much they turned it into Vim.

Emacs stands for "Escape Meta Alt Control Shift," which is also the sound your pinky makes on its way to the orthopedic surgeon. Asking for help is C-h, which in a terminal deletes a character. So even your cry for help gets backspaced.

It has a built-in therapist, M-x doctor, which is thoughtful, because nobody else will listen to you explain your init.el. Four thousand lines of Lisp, half copied from a 2003 mailing list, and you still declare "Emacs bankruptcy" every two years.

It plays Tetris. It reads email. It runs your entire life in Org-mode. It still chokes on one long line of JSON.

Emacs is the only text editor that ships with a psychotherapist, and you'll need it. M-x doctor exists because the developers knew exactly what they were doing to people.

It's a great operating system. It has a mail client, a web browser, Tetris, and a Lisp interpreter. What it lacks is a decent text editor. Its most beloved package is Evil mode, which is just Vim wearing an Emacs costume. That's like buying a Ferrari and installing a horse.

Want to save? C-x C-s. Want to quit? C-x C-c. Want to feel your left pinky again? Too late. Emacs stands for "Escape Meta Alt Control Shift," and the RSI stands for "you chose this."

Every user has a 4,000-line init.el they don't understand, copied from strangers on Stack Overflow in 2009.

我第一次用Vim，打开文件，敲了个hello。前四个字母，屏幕上一个没有，光标自己左右晃了几下，然后“啪”，自己开了个新行。后来我才知道，Vim一打开不是让你写字的，是让你下命令的。我那不叫打字，叫念咒。

写完我想走。右上角？没有叉。按Esc，按Ctrl+C，它底下冒出一行字，教我输“冒号q回车”。我输了，它说文件改过了，不让走。得输“冒号q感叹号”，连退出都得吼着说。

“怎么退出Vim”这个问题，网上几百万人看过。这不是编辑器，这是密室逃脱，门是有的，口令你自己背。

最可怕的是用了三年以后，我在微信里给我妈回消息，手一顺，打了个“:wq”。我妈回我：“儿子，你是不是被盗号了？”

Excel, you're the only software so powerful that scientists had to rename human genes because you kept turning MARCH1 into a date. You didn't adapt to biology; biology adapted to you. Type a phone number and you lop off the leading zero like it owes you money. Enter a credit card number and you serve back 4.53E+15, as if I'm splitting dinner with a physicist.

You still think 1900 was a leap year. It wasn't. You've known for decades. You just don't care.

You're running entire national economies and you still panic over merged cells. The UK lost sixteen thousand COVID cases because someone used your old .xls format and you quietly ran out of rows. No warning. Just vibes.

And VLOOKUP only looks right. Thirty years we spent squinting at #N/A before you finally invented XLOOKUP, like a guy who learns to turn left at fifty.

我有个朋友用Emacs，二十年了。我问他好用吗，他说："这是个伟大的操作系统，就缺一个好编辑器。"

你知道Emacs怎么退出吗？Ctrl-X，Ctrl-C。跟电脑对暗号似的。他小拇指常年按Ctrl，现在跟人握手，小拇指先翘起来，像在喝下午茶。

他的配置文件init.el，三千行Lisp，括号比代码多。我说你这是写配置，还是给括号开会？

最绝的是，他心情不好不找我，敲M-x doctor，Emacs里自带一个心理医生。我说这编辑器连抑郁都管？他说："还有俄罗斯方块呢。"

兄弟，你那不叫编辑器，叫养老院。

我有个朋友用Emacs，二十年了。我问他好用吗？他说好用，就是还没配置完。

二十年！房子都装修三回了，他的init.el还在施工。

Emacs能收邮件、能玩俄罗斯方块，还自带一个心理医生，敲M-x doctor它真陪你聊天。为什么一个编辑器要配心理医生？因为它知道你用的是Emacs。

都说Emacs是个伟大的操作系统，就缺个好用的文本编辑器。我朋友不服，说有啊，装个evil-mode，就能用Vim的键位了。

兄弟，你配了二十年Emacs，最后配成了Vim？

现在他左手小拇指按Ctrl按变形了。医生让他休息，他说不用，我写个Lisp函数替我按。

我跟Excel认识十年了，它最大的特点就是：特别有主见。

你输入“3-1”，它说：“我懂，三月一号。”我懂你个头，那是比分！你输入身份证号，18位，它说：“太长了，我帮你精简一下”，啪，变成4.10E+17，后三位全给你改成0。你身份证尾号能是000吗？派出所都不敢这么发！

最狠的是，全世界的科学家，因为Excel老把基因名“SEPT1”改成“9月1日”，最后决定集体给基因改名。人类拗不过一个表格软件，改的是DNA！

列宽不够它不提醒你，就显示一排“######”，跟骂人似的。我就打开看了一眼，啥也没动，关的时候它还问：“是否保存更改？”

我改什么了？你倒是说说，我改什么了？

Excel, you're the only software that forced geneticists to rename human genes because you kept turning MARCH1 into March 1st. Scientists can edit DNA, but they couldn't edit you. You still think 1900 was a leap year. You've known it wasn't for forty years. You just don't care. You see a zip code like 02134 and go, "Leading zero? Not on my watch." You lost sixteen thousand UK COVID cases by quietly stopping at row 65,536. Your error messages are pure poetry: #REF!, #N/A, #VALUE!, and my favorite, a column of hashtags that just means "make me wider." And VLOOKUP: insert one column and the whole finance department enters witness protection. You're not a spreadsheet. You're a hostage situation with gridlines.

我觉得Excel是全世界最自作聪明的软件。我输个十八位身份证号，它嫌长，帮我改成“4.40306E+17”。我说你别动，它说好的，然后把最后三位全改成0。现在我这身份证全国通用，谁都是我。

我输“3-1”，意思是三楼一号，它改成3月1日。我改回来，它又改。最后我只能在前面加个单引号，就像跟它解释：这话是我说的，跟你没关系。

科学家更惨，有个基因叫SEPT2，Excel一律改成九月二号。后来国际组织直接把基因改名了。人类改了自己基因的名字，就为了迁就一个表格软件。

你们还担心AI统治人类？Excel早就统治了，只是统治得特别不准。

Google Sheets, you're Excel's little brother who moved into a browser tab and called it "the cloud." Your whole personality is twelve people's colored cursors circling the same cell like sharks while an Anonymous Capybara silently watches everyone's mistakes. You say "Saving..." with the confidence of a man who has absolutely not saved. Your IMPORTRANGE makes me click "Allow access" like I'm asking my own spreadsheet for permission to see my own spreadsheet. Half my cells just say "Loading..." forever, like a Victorian ghost waiting for a letter. And you'll let anyone sort one column without the others, then shrug while every customer gets someone else's phone number. Version history is your only real feature: it's just a timeline of who ruined everything at 2 a.m. And yes, Gemini can explain my #REF! error now. Great. It's still there.

Google Sheets, you're Excel's cousin who got into tech because you could "share a link." Congrats: now forty Anonymous Capybaras can watch me botch a VLOOKUP in real time. Your whole personality is "All changes saved in Drive," which is a weird flex when the change was Kevin sorting one column and detaching every employee from their salary. Version history isn't a feature; it's a crime scene. IMPORTRANGE says "Loading..." the way my dad said he was going out for milk. You've got a QUERY function that's just SQL in a fake mustache, yet you freeze if I paste more than twelve rows. And #REF! isn't an error message; it's you shrugging in all caps. You cap out at ten million cells. Ten million. You're the only spreadsheet with a bedtime.

Windows Vista, everybody! Five years in development as "Longhorn," and the only thing that shipped on time was the disappointment. They cut WinFS but kept the Aero glass. Finally, an operating system you could see right through.

Vista came in six editions, from Starter to Ultimate, which is five more ways to pay for the same crash. Microsoft slapped "Vista Capable" stickers on computers that could barely run Solitaire, then got sued. The only thing Vista ever finished loading was a class action.

And User Account Control! "Are you sure you want to do that?" Every. Single. Click. Vista was the only software that needed permission to exist, and honestly? We should've hit Cancel.

Copying a file: "Calculating time remaining…" Vista, you were calculating until 2009, when Microsoft fixed you, renamed you Windows 7, and pretended you were adopted.

Windows Vista, everybody! Microsoft spent five years building you as "Longhorn," and somehow you still came out premature.

Your slogan was "The Wow Starts Now." You meant "Now" as in "after the loading circle finishes." People bought laptops with "Vista Capable" stickers, which turned out to mean "capable of being sued over." Those machines couldn't even run Aero, so they got a see-through window theme with nothing to see.

And User Account Control! You asked "Are you sure?" so many times that you became the first operating system with separation anxiety.

You came in six editions, including "Ultimate," whose big exclusive was DreamScene: a moving wallpaper for the ten minutes you weren't hunting for printer drivers.

Microsoft had to trick people into liking you. The Mojave Experiment! Your own parents had to put you in disguise.

Your greatest feature? The XP downgrade.

我们公司什么都用Google Sheets管，预算、排班、年会抽奖。最恐怖的不是加班，是你打开表格，右上角突然冒出一只"匿名水豚"。谁啊？不知道。它也不说话，就一直盯着我那格"实际支出"。过一会儿又来一只"匿名狐狸"。我不是在做表，我是在动物园被参观。

还有那个彩色光标。你正填着数，一个绿色小框标着"王总"，慢慢地、慢慢地往你这格挪。比恐怖片还吓人，恐怖片里的鬼至少不会顺手把你的公式改成数值。

最绝的是同事只选了一列就点"排序"，三百个人的工资当场重新分配。我赶紧打开版本历史，四千条记录，每条都写着"匿名水豚"。

我们公司所有事都用Google Sheets，因为它能“多人协作”。协作是什么意思？就是你在改A列，右上角突然冒出个“匿名水獭”，在改B列。谁是水獭？不知道。水獭也不说话，光标一闪一闪跟着你，你删一格它填一格。我一个人加班，办公室就我一个，表里有四只动物。

后来我学聪明了，去翻版本历史。版本历史告诉我：凌晨三点，“匿名卡皮巴拉”把整张工资表按姓氏排了序，只排了第一列。

现在全公司工资都对不上。老板问谁干的，我说一只卡皮巴拉。他说你把它找出来。我说找不到啊，权限设的是“任何知道链接的人均可编辑”。这链接，我昨天发在了全员群里。

我这辈子最没安全感的时候，就是用Windows Vista那几年。点开个计算器，屏幕一暗：“用户账户控制：你确定要运行此程序吗？”我确定啊！我自己点的！这不是操作系统，这是我妈。

微软憋了五年，代号Longhorn，“长角”，结果端出来一只蜗牛。电脑上贴着“Vista Capable”，意思是“能装Vista”，没说能用。

最绝的是微软自己。后来他们把Vista换了个名字叫“Mojave”，骗用户说是新系统，大家试完都说：“哇，好用！”你品品，这系统最大的毛病就是叫Vista。再后来出了Windows 7，人人都夸。废话，那就是Vista终于做完了。

Windows 8, you looked at a billion people with a mouse and a keyboard and said, "What if your monitor was a giant phone you can't touch?"

You took away the Start button. The one thing a user knew how to find. Microsoft had literally sold Windows 95 with a Rolling Stones song called "Start Me Up," and you said, "Nah."

Want to shut down? Easy: hover in a secret corner, summon the Charms bar, click Settings, click Power. Turning off my computer shouldn't feel like unlocking a cheat code.

Your tiles were so ugly even the name "Metro" had to get dropped over a trademark dispute. Then 8.1 brought back the Start button, which just opened the same tiles. That's not an apology, that's a hostage video.

You were so bad Microsoft skipped the number 9 entirely just to put distance between you and Windows 10.

我第一台电脑装的Windows Vista，它特别有礼貌。我双击个图标，屏幕一暗："Windows需要您的许可才能继续。"我点继续。改个时间，问我；删个快捷方式，问我；我想去关掉这个弹窗，它还要问我！这不是系统，这是我妈。

买的时候机箱上贴着"Vista Capable"，意思是"能装"，没说"能用"。一开Aero毛玻璃，风扇起飞，开机时间够我泡碗面。

后来微软改了改，换个名字叫Windows 7，大家都夸好用。所以Vista不是失败，是公测，只不过测试员得自己掏钱。

Windows 8是我见过最自信的产品。微软开会：“用户用开始按钮十七年了，习惯了吧？”“习惯了。”“删了。”

开机，满屏彩色方块，我以为电脑中了彩票。想关机？鼠标甩到右上角，等“超级按钮”栏飘出来，点设置，点电源，再点关机。关个电脑像拆炸弹。

最绝的是锁屏，没按钮，得用鼠标往上“拖”开。我抓着鼠标在桌上猛推，像在给电脑做心肺复苏。

后来大家骂疯了，微软出了8.1：“开始按钮回来了！”我一点，弹出来的还是那堆方块。这不叫道歉，这叫“我听到了，但我不改”。

Windows 8, Microsoft looked at the Start button, the one thing every human on Earth knew how to use, and said, "What if we hid it?" You turned every desktop into a giant tablet nobody could touch. People were swiping at their monitors like they were wiping off a stain. Shutting you down required a treasure map: hover in a corner, summon the Charms bar, Settings, Power. Charms! Like the operating system was a bracelet from Claire's. You shipped with two Internet Explorers, which is two more than anyone wanted. Even your design name, Metro, got taken away by lawyers. And when 8.1 finally brought the Start button back, it just took you to the same tile screen. That's not an apology, that's a hostage note. You were so bad Microsoft skipped Windows 9 entirely, just to put more distance between us and you.

Windows 8最狠的是什么？它把"开始"按钮删了。微软开了无数会，最后决定：用户不需要开始。

那怎么关机？鼠标挪到右上角，等一排"超级按钮"飘出来，点设置，点电源，再点关机。关个电脑跟拆炸弹一样，剪错一根线，打开了天气。

一开机，满屏彩色方块，跟进了麦当劳点餐机似的。我那台没触摸屏的台式机，它天天劝我"用手指滑一下"。我滑了，显示器倒了。

它还自带两个IE，一个全屏版一个桌面版，书签不通。我一个人上网，自己跟自己是网友。

后来骂的人多了，8.1把开始按钮还回来了。我感动地一点，弹出来的还是那堆方块。

这叫什么？退货，退回来一个包装盒。

Hawaiian pizza, you're named after a place you've never been. You were invented in Ontario, by a Greek guy, using canned pineapple. That's not a heritage, that's a witness protection identity.

And the ham? It's Canadian bacon. Even your meat is from Canada. The only Hawaiian thing about you is that people see you and say "aloha," meaning goodbye.

Pineapple has an enzyme that digests protein. You're the only pizza that eats the customer back. Warm fruit juice pooling on mozzarella like a hot tub nobody cleaned.

Italians don't hate you; they pray for you. The president of Iceland said he'd ban you if he could, and Iceland eats fermented shark.

You're not a pizza. You're a fruit cup that fell on a pizza and refused to get up.

Hawaiian pizza. Let's start with the name, because that's the first lie. You were invented in Ontario. By a Greek guy. In 1962. You're Hawaiian the way a tiki bar in Ohio is Hawaiian. The only tropical thing about you is the can your pineapple came out of.

And that pineapple: warm, wet, weeping syrup into the crust until the middle slice folds like a lawn chair. Pineapple contains an enzyme that breaks down protein, so the fruit is literally trying to digest the ham. Even your toppings hate each other.

And the ham! Not prosciutto, not even pepperoni. Just pale pink squares that look like they were chiseled out of a deli's floor tile.

You're the pizza people order to seem quirky. "I'm so random!" No, Kevin. That's a fruit cup that fell on a pizza, and nobody cleaned it up.

Chicago deep-dish isn't a pizza. It's a casserole that got a fake ID. You order it, and the waiter says, "That'll be forty-five minutes." Forty-five minutes! I've had relationships bake faster. They put the sauce on top because if you saw what was underneath first, you'd leave. A solid sheet of sausage, like somebody paved a driveway with a patty. Two pounds of mozzarella hiding under a tomato quilt. It's not a slice, it's a core sample. You need a knife, a fork, and a structural engineer. The crust is buttery cornmeal, so it's a pie crust, so congratulations, you're eating dessert with ambitions. And here's the best part: actual Chicagoans don't even eat it. They eat tavern-style thin crust cut in squares. Deep-dish is just the city's way of keeping tourists too full to walk to Wrigley.

Chicago deep-dish isn't a pizza. It's a casserole with a publicist. You order one and the waiter says "forty-five minutes," which is how long it takes to bake and also how long it takes to finish one slice. They put the sauce on top and the cheese underneath, like they're hiding evidence. That's not a recipe, that's a cover-up. The crust is a buttery retaining wall holding back a lake of chunky tomato, because apparently Lake Michigan wasn't enough water for one city to manage. You need a knife, a fork, a nap, and a cardiologist on retainer. Then there's the sausage, laid down as one solid patty like the base layer of a parking garage. Chicagoans defend it like family. Sure: the relative who shows up late, takes up three chairs, and leaves everyone unable to move.

夏威夷披萨，你们知道是谁发明的吗？一个希腊人，在加拿大发明的。夏威夷人全程不知情。这就好比我在东北开个店卖"巴黎煎饼"，法国人路过都得报警。

再说菠萝。菠萝里有种酶，专门分解蛋白质，所以吃菠萝舌头会麻，那是它在吃你。你把它往披萨上放，旁边是火腿、是芝士，全是蛋白质。这不叫配料，这叫把狼放进羊圈，还给烤到两百度，让它带着怨气上桌。

最离谱的是那一口：咬下去，"滋"，一股滚烫的甜水直接浇在上颚。我一个成年人，吃个披萨，被水果烫伤了。医生问我怎么弄的，我都不好意思说，只能说：遭遇了热带气旋。

Durian, they call you the King of Fruits, which tracks, because like most monarchies, you stink and nobody's allowed to say it to your face.

You're the only fruit with a criminal record. Banned on the Singapore subway, alongside flammable liquids. Hotels put your picture on signs next to "no smoking." In 2019, a university in Melbourne evacuated five hundred people because they thought there was a gas leak. Nope. Just you, sitting in a cupboard, being yourself.

And the armor! You're covered in spikes like a medieval mace. Nature built you to defend yourself, then gave you a smell that does it better. The spikes are just overkill.

Fans say you taste like custard. Sure. Custard that was left in a gym bag next to some onions. Your flavor isn't an acquired taste. It's a hostage situation.

夏威夷披萨，我查了一下，是一个希腊人在加拿大发明的。跟夏威夷一点关系没有。夏威夷人一口没吃过，背了六十年锅，这比冤假错案还冤。

再看这个组合：火腿配菠萝。一个是猪，一个长得像穿了盔甲的刺猬，它俩这辈子本来不该见面。你非把它们塞进烤箱，菠萝一受热，汁全爆出来，滚烫的糖水泡着芝士。你咬一口，那感觉就像一个水果罐头，在你嘴里，偷袭了一张饼。

意大利人最惨。全世界拿他们的披萨乱来，他们都忍了，但看见菠萝那一刻，他们的表情就像祖坟上被人插了一把小雨伞。

最气人的是，它好吃。我每次骂完都再点一个。

芝加哥深盘披萨，我第一次点，服务员说：“要等四十五分钟。”我说我点的是披萨，不是做手术。

端上来一看，边儿高得像城墙，我得先攻城才能吃到馅。最离谱的是顺序，别人家芝士在上面，它偏把番茄酱盖在最顶上，芝士压底下。为啥？怕芝士烤焦。芝加哥人的逻辑是：烤四十五分钟没问题，但芝士不能受委屈。

里面的香肠不是一片片的，是整整一张，像给披萨铺了块地毯。我切下一块，芝士拉丝拉到我站起来它还连着，像脐带，舍不得我走。

纽约人说这不叫披萨，叫砂锅。不对，砂锅吃完你还能站起来。

我去芝加哥，朋友带我吃深盘披萨。点完单，服务员说：“要等四十五分钟。”四十五分钟！在别的城市，这是外卖超时免单的时间，在芝加哥只是烤箱的开场白。

端上来一看，这不是披萨，这是一口锅。番茄酱在最上面，芝士压在最底下，跟填反了的问卷一样。我想用手拿，旁边芝加哥大哥一把按住我：“用刀叉。”用刀叉吃披萨？那跟千层面有什么区别？区别就是千层面不用等四十五分钟。

一块下去，我饱了。两块下去，我开始写遗嘱。大哥还骄傲地说：“这才叫真正的披萨。”你们冬天零下二十度，这根本不是食物，这是吃进肚子里的羽绒服。

Durian, the "King of Fruits." Sure, if the kingdom is a landfill. You're banned on the Singapore subway, right there on the sign next to flammable liquids, because apparently you're the bigger hazard. Hotels fine guests for sneaking you in. That's not a fruit, that's a parole violation.

You wear a medieval mace as a jacket, which is smart, since nobody who's smelled you wants to get close anyway. You fall out of trees and put people in the hospital. You're the only produce that needs a hard hat AND a hazmat suit.

And your fans swear you're "like custard!" Sure: custard aged in a gym bag full of rotten onions. Fifty bucks for a Musang King, and your breath's a crime scene for three days.

Anthony Bourdain ate warthog rectum on camera, and *you're* the one he warned people about.

Jackfruit, you're the largest fruit that grows on a tree, which sounds impressive until you realize it just means you're the biggest thing that can fall on someone's head in an orchard. Eighty pounds of spikes dangling at skull height. You're not a fruit, you're a booby trap with seeds.

Opening you requires an oiled knife, rubber gloves, and a tarp, because your sap is basically Elmer's glue with a grudge. Then the smell hits: half Juicy Fruit gum, half onions somebody forgot in a gym bag. You smell like a candy store got food poisoning.

And sure, vegans love you, but only when you're young and taste like absolutely nothing. That's your whole career. The most famous thing about you is that, with enough barbecue sauce, you can pass for a pig. Even your best role is an impression.

Jackfruit, look at you. The largest fruit that grows on a tree, and you couldn't even make it to the branches. You just hang off the trunk like a drunk uncle clinging to a lamppost.

You weigh eighty pounds. That's not a fruit, that's a fourth grader in a bumpy green costume. People cut you open and need cooking oil on their hands and knives, because your insides are basically rubber cement. You're the only produce that requires a solvent.

And vegans love you because when you're young, you taste like absolutely nothing. Your big career move is pretending to be pulled pork. Your whole identity is "not bad if you drown me in barbecue sauce."

Then you ripen and smell like Juicy Fruit gum fermenting in a gym bag.

You're the national fruit of Bangladesh, and you still find time to fall on people's heads.

我买过一次榴莲。六十八一斤，一称九斤，我心想好家伙，这是要吃到过年。老板拿刀一撬，掰开，五个房，三个是空的，剩下两坨肉加起来也就一个鸡蛋大。那剩下八斤多是啥？是壳！我花了好几百，买了一个带刺的快递盒子！

吃完更绝。冰箱里放了一块，第二天开门，我的牛奶、鸡蛋、昨天的剩饭，全是榴莲味儿。它不是水果，它是占领军。

新加坡地铁明文禁止带榴莲，跟易燃易爆物品贴在一块儿。一个水果，混到这个待遇，我是服的。

最气的是爱吃的人永远那一句：“你闻着臭，吃着香啊！”大哥，这句话放在任何别的东西上，都叫“过期了”。

榴莲这东西，我是真服。你见过哪个水果，新加坡地铁专门给它立块禁止牌？跟“禁止吸烟”“禁止携带易燃物”挂一排。它不是水果，它是违禁品，只是碰巧能吃。

买的时候更离谱。四十块一斤，五斤，两百。回家戴上劳保手套，拿着菜刀，跟拆炸弹一样顺着缝撬开。五斤里头，三斤是壳，一斤是核，剩下一斤，是我花两百块买的“老板说这个肉厚”。

然后吃完你以为就结束了？没有，它还在。你打一个嗝，它就回来跟你打声招呼。凌晨三点，我老婆从床上坐起来问：“你是不是偷吃榴莲了？”我说你怎么知道，她说：“我梦见煤气泄漏了。”

我上次买了个菠萝蜜，三十斤，抱回家像抱着个浑身长疙瘩的胖娃娃。老板叮嘱：“切之前手上抹油。”我心想吃个水果还得做保养？一刀下去我懂了，它流的不是汁，是502。刀粘住了，手粘住了，我顺手挠了下脸，现在左手和左脸是一体的。

好不容易掰开，一坨坨黄色果肉，裹在一堆白色烂布条里，跟拆快递一样：三十斤，二十五斤是泡沫纸。剩下五斤里，一半是核。最气的是我妈说核别扔，煮了能吃。好家伙，这玩意儿连垃圾都要我亲自消化。

还有人问：“菠萝蜜就是菠萝吧？”菠萝要是长这样，我早戒水果了。

我跟你们说，菠萝蜜是水果界最大的骗局。

先说名字，菠萝蜜，跟菠萝一毛钱关系没有，跟蜜也就沾点边。这就好比一个人叫“张帅”，你见了面才发现，人家是姓张。

去年我脑子一热买了一整个，三十斤，扛回家跟扛了个煤气罐似的。一刀下去，流出一堆白胶，黏得我五根手指头拜了把子，菜刀直接焊在了砧板上。后来上网一查：“切之前记得手上抹油。”谢谢，我现在全身都抹油了，因为我整个人都粘在厨房了。

剖开一看，满肚子的白丝，跟拆了一床旧棉被一样。我扒了一个小时，才扒出一小碗黄肉，每块肉里还裹着一颗巨大的核。

三十斤，我吃了一碗，剩下的全是垃圾。最气人的是那堆核，煮熟了居然像板栗。你说这玩意儿，它到底是水果，还是一个装满板栗的包装箱？

Luosifen, you're the only dish that arrives before the delivery guy does. You're named after river snails, yet nobody has ever found one in the bowl. You boiled them for hours, took their soul, and threw out the bodies. That's not a recipe, that's a cover-up.

And that smell? Fermented bamboo shoots that died, got buried, and came back for revenge. Someone opens a packet in Liuzhou and a guy in Guilin checks his shoes. College dorms banned you like a space heater. Neighbors call the gas company.

Your fans swear, "It smells terrible but tastes amazing." Buddy, that's what everyone says about their toxic ex.

Peanuts, crispy tofu skin, wood ear, pickled beans, a slick of chili oil... that's not garnish, that's witness protection for flavor.

And now you come instant. Congratulations: a biohazard with a seasoning packet.

Luosifen, you're the only dish named after a snail that contains zero snails. They simmer the snails for hours, then throw them out, like a dad who shows up for the paternity test and leaves. Your real star is suan sun, fermented bamboo shoot that smells like a gym sock studied abroad in Liuzhou and came back with opinions. Fans say, "It smells terrible but tastes amazing." So does every scam. You turned instant noodles into a hazmat event: one packet opened in a dorm and three floors file noise complaints, because that smell is *loud*. Couriers wrap you in four bags like evidence. And you come with seven sachets: chili oil, peanuts, tofu skin, wood ear, the bamboo. It's IKEA furniture that makes the neighbors move out. Liuzhou didn't invent a soup. It invented Stockholm syndrome with chili oil.

我最服螺蛳粉的一点：它叫螺蛳粉，里面没有螺蛳。你问老板螺蛳呢，老板说熬汤了。哦，就是螺蛳把命献了，碗里只留下一个名字，跟烈士陵园一样。

真正的主角是酸笋。那个味儿，我第一次闻，以为楼下下水道炸了。我妈冲进厨房问："你是不是把袜子煮了？"我说妈，这是网红，二十多块一袋。

袋装的更绝，拆开里面七八个小包：粉包、汤包、酸笋包、花生包、腐竹包、木耳包、辣油包……我以为在拆快递。拆到最后，全家人都在拆窗户。

而且它闻着像犯罪现场，吃一口，香。香得你没法跟人解释。你说"真的好吃"，人家看你的眼神，就像你在给一个化粪池写好评。

螺蛳粉最大的骗局在名字。你吃了三年，见过一颗螺蛳吗？没有。店家说螺蛳熬汤了，熬完捞走了。可它臭的是酸笋，跟螺蛳一点关系没有。螺蛳全程没露面，名字挂在门口，专门替酸笋挨骂。

袋装的更绝，拆开七八个小包：汤包、酸笋包、腐竹花生包、辣油包、醋包，煮个粉跟拆炸弹似的，还得按顺序剪。我第一次剪开酸笋包，我妈在阳台收衣服，冲进来问我是不是把下水道撬了。

还有那个炸腐竹，泡汤里十秒，吸饱红油，咬一口“滋”地喷你一脸。这是我吃过唯一一种会主动反击的配菜。

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that announces itself before the menu does. People find you at the night market the way sharks find blood: follow the stench three stalls past the bubble tea. Your brine is fermented vegetables, shrimp, amaranth stems, and apparently a gym sock that lost a bet. Months in that bucket, and you came out smelling like a festival porta-potty in August. Your own name is a confession. Not "aged tofu," not "artisanal bean curd." Your family took one whiff and went, "Yeah, call him Stinky." And the Changsha version? Dyed jet black, like it's in mourning for everyone's sense of smell. The only reason anyone finishes you is the pickled cabbage and chili sauce piled on top to keep you quiet. "Smells bad, tastes good" isn't a slogan, buddy. It's a hostage negotiation.

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that announces itself three night-market stalls before you arrive. People don't find you at Shilin. They track you, like bloodhounds following a crime scene. Your whole brand is "smells like a sewer, tastes great," which is also what every bad Tinder date says about himself. You soak for months in fermented brine like you're marinating in a grudge. And your family's no better: Changsha dyed you black, the culinary equivalent of putting sunglasses on a corpse. You need deep frying, chili sauce, AND a mound of pickled cabbage just to be socially acceptable. That's not a garnish, that's a legal team. Your parents gave you one job: be tofu. Tofu's whole personality is having no personality. And somehow you came out smelling like a gym sock that went to college. Honestly? Respect.

Oat milk, you are porridge that got a publicist. Somebody looked at the breakfast of Victorian orphans and said, "What if it cost six dollars and had a font?"

Your carton talks to me. Oatly, I'm trying to make coffee, not get into a pen-pal situation with a beverage that writes like a substitute teacher who wants to be called "Dave."

You're oats, water, and rapeseed oil. That's not milk, that's a salad dressing that gave up. And they had to add enzymes to turn your starch into sugar so you'd taste like something. You're the only "health drink" that spikes my blood sugar like a Pop-Tart.

There's a "Barista Edition" now. Oat milk, there are two editions of you. Moby-Dick has fewer editions than you.

And you're beige. You make every latte look like dishwater with ambition.

Horses eat oats for free, and they still look embarrassed for us.

臭豆腐是唯一一种靠差评做广告的小吃。隔三条街就有人捂着鼻子说"前面肯定有臭豆腐"，好，这一句话，就把客全引过去了。

长沙的更绝，炸出来是黑的。一块豆腐，闻着像下水道，长得像煤球，老板还拿筷子往中间戳个洞，灌一勺辣椒汁，递给你说"趁热"。这哪是卖吃的，这是在考验你的诚意。

关键它真好吃，外酥里嫩，一口咬下去汤汁烫嘴。所以吃臭豆腐的人都特别分裂：嘴在说"再来一份"，鼻子在说"你有病吧"。

最惨是吃完进电梯。所有人沉默，你也沉默，你不知道该自首，还是该陪大家一起骂是谁家的地漏又堵了。

臭豆腐是唯一一种你还没看见摊子，就已经知道它在哪儿的食物。导航都不用开，跟着鼻子走，哪儿最像下水道返味儿，抬头一看："正宗长沙臭豆腐"。

老板还骄傲地跟你说："我这卤水养了二十年！"二十年！你冰箱里的剩菜放二十天你都扔了，他放二十年，拿出来卖钱，还排队。

最离谱的是黑色那款。炸得黑里透亮，老板拿竹签中间一戳，灌一勺辣椒汁，再塞两根香菜。你看它，像块蜂窝煤；你闻它，像谁家化粪池；你咬一口，汤汁"呲"一下，烫得你原地蹦迪。等缓过来再嚼两下，坏了，真香。

你就站在路边，一边骂一边扫码买第二份。这东西厉害就厉害在：它从头到尾没装过好人，是你自己贱。

Oat milk, you're porridge that went to finishing school. Somebody looked at horse food and said, "What if it cost seventy cents extra?" Then somebody else said, "Yes, and put it in a carton that talks like a guy who just got back from Copenhagen." Your packaging has more personality than you do. Every box of Oatly reads like a cover letter: "Hi! We're a little weird!" No, you're oats, water, and rapeseed oil. That's not a beverage. That's a salad dressing that gave up.

And the "Barista Edition"? You needed extra oil just to get a job. Enzymes break your starch into maltose, so technically you're a sugar spike in a flannel shirt. Plus you were funded by Blackstone. You're not anti-establishment, oat milk. You're a private equity firm wearing a beanie.

我现在去咖啡店，店员第一句不问大杯小杯，问：“要不要换燕麦奶？加五块。”
我回家查了一下燕麦奶怎么做：燕麦，加水，打碎，过滤。
这东西我奶奶天天做啊！她管这个叫：熬粥剩下那层汤！
以前都是直接倒掉的，现在倒进拿铁里就值五块了？
再看配料表，第三位，菜籽油。菜籽油！我点杯咖啡，怎么还带炒青菜的工序？
店员还特骄傲：“我们用的是咖啡大师版。”大师在哪？大师就是多放了点油，好打奶泡。
而且燕麦它根本没有奶，它是草啊！你见过哪个农民蹲在地里，一手扶麦穗，一手拿桶接？
所以我这杯燕麦拿铁，正确的名字应该叫：油泼粥汤美式。

Almond milk, you're not milk. You're a rumor about an almond. Two percent almonds, ninety-eight percent "we strained the tap." You're the only drink that needs a legal team to call itself milk. The dairy lobby has spent a decade trying to make you admit you're nut juice.

California spends about a gallon of water per almond just so you can show up in my fridge as... water. That's like melting a glacier to make an ice cube.

They truck in billions of bees to pollinate your orchards, and the bees die by the millions so I can pay an extra eighty cents at Starbucks for a latte that tastes like damp drywall.

And "shake well"? Leave you alone for ten minutes and you separate like a couple who met at Whole Foods. Even *you* can't commit to you.

我现在点咖啡，店员都会问：“要不要换燕麦奶？加五块。”

燕麦奶是什么？燕麦泡水，打碎，过滤。说白了就是一碗稀到能插吸管的燕麦粥。

我小时候生病，我奶奶就给我煮燕麦粥，因为便宜。现在我花三十八，在咖啡里兑一碗我奶奶的“便宜”。

而且燕麦在欧洲几百年都是喂马的。英国人编字典，“燕麦”的解释是：在英格兰喂马，在苏格兰喂人。现在好了，全上海的白领一人一杯，排着队喂自己。

最绝的是包装上写“咖啡师版”。燕麦还分版本？那我奶奶那锅叫什么，“退休教师版”？

……嗯，确实有股马厩的清香。

text:
Almond milk, you're the only drink that needs a lawyer to defend its name. The dairy industry sued because, technically, nobody has ever milked an almond. We looked. No nipples.

You're about two percent almonds. The rest is water, gellan gum, and confidence. You're not milk. You're a nut that got waterboarded and called it wellness.

And speaking of water: it takes over a gallon to grow a single almond. California is in a drought so you can be beige in a latte. Bees get trucked across the country like seasonal laborers just to make you, and a lot of them don't come home.

Leave you in the fridge for two days and you separate like you're ashamed of yourself. Fair. I'd need to be shaken too if I cost seven dollars and tasted like a wet sympathy card.

Las Vegas, the only city where you can see the Eiffel Tower, a pyramid, and Venice in one afternoon and still feel like you never left a strip mall in Ohio. You're a city built in the desert out of pure spite and borrowed water. The Colorado River is literally drying up so a fake volcano can erupt every fifteen minutes for a guy in cargo shorts holding a yard-long margarita.

Your casinos have no clocks and no windows, which is smart, because nobody wants to know it's 9 a.m. on a Tuesday and Grandma's on her third oxygen tank at the Wheel of Fortune slots.

"What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas"? Sure. Mostly your 401(k). And now you've got the Sphere, a giant glowing eyeball, so the whole city can watch you make every mistake in 4K.

我最近改喝杏仁奶了，健康嘛。喝第一口我就有个问题：杏仁，它奶在哪儿？你见过杏仁哺乳吗？哪个农场工人蹲在树底下，捏着一颗杏仁：“来，挤一挤……”挤了一下午，挤出来的全是他自己的汗。

后来我翻过来看配料表：杏仁含量，百分之二。百分之二！剩下全是水。这不叫杏仁奶，这叫杏仁路过了一桶水。它在里面的存在感，跟我在家族群里差不多。

包装上还写：“饮用前请摇匀”。我摇了，特别认真地摇。那百分之二的杏仁，我得摇多猛，才能让每一口都雨露均沾？

最后一看价格，比牛奶贵一倍。我花双倍的钱，买了一盒被杏仁瞄过一眼的水。牛都笑了，人家好歹是真挤的。

我最近戒了牛奶，改喝杏仁奶。喝之前我一直有个疑问：杏仁，它是怎么挤的？你见过杏仁有乳头吗？没有。它就那么一小颗，硬邦邦的，你上哪儿给它挤去？

我专门翻了配料表，杏仁含量：百分之二。剩下全是水。这不叫杏仁奶，这叫"杏仁路过的水"。

更离谱的是，种一颗杏仁，要用差不多四升水。四升！也就是说，这瓶里那几颗杏仁，喝掉的水比我一个礼拜喝的都多。它们在加州把地都喝干了，最后挤出来一瓶……水。这是个闭环啊朋友们！

一瓶还卖二十八。我在超市犹豫半天，旁边一大爷凑过来看了一眼，说：小伙子，这不就是我们小时候泡完杏仁倒掉的那盆水吗？

我去了趟拉斯维加斯，发现这城市最大的本事，是把全世界复印了一遍，还印歪了。埃菲尔铁塔，一半大；威尼斯运河，修在商场二楼，船夫唱着意大利歌，头顶是画出来的蓝天，因为赌场不想让你知道现在几点。没窗户，没钟，我在里面待了六小时，以为才二十分钟。一出门，天黑了，钱包也黑了。

他们口号说：“在维加斯发生的，就留在维加斯。”确实。我的钱留下了，尊严留下了，连我跟猫王在小教堂定下的婚约也……等等，这个好像跟我回家了。

在沙漠正中间修一座满是喷泉的城，它不是在赌博，它是在跟老天爷赌气。

我去了趟拉斯维加斯，终于明白什么叫“人造天堂”。威尼斯人酒店里有运河、有贡多拉，船夫唱意大利歌——在沙漠正中间。外面四十五度，里面天花板画着蓝天白云，永远下午四点。

赌场没有钟，没有窗。你输了一夜出来，天黑了，你都不知道是今天黑的还是明天黑的。

他们说：“发生在维加斯的事，就留在维加斯。”对，主要是你的钱。

最气人的是那座埃菲尔铁塔，一半大小。我站在下面想：我花八千块机票，来沙漠看个打了五折的法国。整座城市唯一真打折的，就是它。

临走那天，猫王给我证了个婚。我本来没打算结，但人家二十四小时营业，还送自助餐券，我总觉得不结就亏了。

Macau, you're the only place where the most famous church is just a wall. The Ruins of St. Paul's: a gorgeous front with absolutely nothing behind it, which is basically your whole personality. You've got a fake Venice with a painted sky, a fake Paris with a half-size Eiffel Tower, and you're so tiny you had to dump dirt into the ocean just to fit a runway. You out-earned Las Vegas several times over, and your signature dish is still a pork chop jammed in a bun. The Portuguese stayed four hundred years and left you an egg tart and street signs nobody reads. The Grand Lisboa looks like a golden pineapple having a breakdown. And the Macau Tower's big attraction is jumping off it, which, after a night at the baccarat tables, is less a thrill ride and more a financial plan.

Las Vegas, the only city that looked at the Mojave Desert and said, "You know what this needs? Venice." Nothing says Italian romance like a gondolier singing in a mall next to a Cheesecake Factory.

You built a half-size Eiffel Tower, a fake New York, and a pyramid, because why visit the world when you can visit its gift shop?

No clocks, no windows, and carpet designed by a migraine, all so you won't notice you've been feeding a penny slot since Tuesday.

"What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas." Yeah. Especially your money. And the $45 resort fee for a pool you couldn't use because a bachelor party from Ohio was in it.

And Lake Mead's drying up so fast they keep finding bodies. Even the mob's secrets can't stay in Vegas anymore.

Macau, you're the only place where the most famous church is just a front wall. Fitting, since the whole city is a facade: a fake Venice with a painted sky, a half-size Eiffel Tower, and a Grand Lisboa that looks like a golden pineapple trying to cheat at baccarat.

Portugal ruled you for 442 years and left behind egg tarts and street signs nobody can pronounce. Four centuries, one pastry.

You've made several times more gambling money than Las Vegas, yet your signature dish is a pork chop jammed in a bun. Classy.

Half your land was dug out of the sea, which is perfect, because the other half was dug out of tourists' pockets.

And they built a 55-kilometer bridge to connect you to Hong Kong, and it's emptier than a junket operator's promises. Even the bridge is losing at the tables.

我去澳门，最有名的景点叫大三巴。到了才知道，大三巴就是一面墙。一座教堂烧得只剩个正门，全世界游客排着队，跟一扇门合影。这要在我老家，早拆了盖小区了。

澳门人特别会过日子。地不够，填海；天不够，画一个。威尼斯人酒店里那片蓝天是画在天花板上的，永远不下雨，永远是下午四点。为啥？赌场里不能让你知道几点了。

最贴心的是发财车，免费拉你去赌场。从来没人问过：回去那趟谁出钱？

出了赌场，门口一排当铺，全写着“24小时营业”。澳门的效率就在这儿：你输钱，它不让你等；你当表，它也不让你等。

Canberra exists because Sydney and Melbourne couldn't agree, so Australia built a city nobody wanted, which is honestly the most Canberra origin story possible: a compromise with suburbs. They held an international design competition and hired two Americans to plan it, and they nailed the brief: "Make it impossible to find anything." Every road is a roundabout leading to another roundabout, encircling a fake lake named after the guy who designed the roundabouts. Your Parliament House has a grass roof so you can literally walk on top of the government, the only time anyone in Canberra is above a public servant. The kangaroos outnumber the nightlife. For decades your two biggest attractions were legal fireworks and X-rated videos, which tells me the locals needed both a bang and a release. Then you banned the fireworks. Now the excitement is Floriade: a month of staring at tulips because the alternative is Tuggeranong.

澳门这地方特别会省钱。大三巴，最出名的景点，就剩一面墙。你绕到后面一看，啥也没有。这不是古迹，这是一张立起来的朋友圈封面。

威尼斯人里面，天花板画个蓝天，底下有人撑船唱意大利歌。我在里面待了六个钟头，出来发现天黑了，还以为是输光了眼前一黑。

你掏港币，人家一比一照收；找零给你澳门元，也是一比一。就这一下，我赌场门还没进，先输了百分之三。

最绝的是酒店的免费接驳巴士，满城跑，一分钱不要。为什么这么大方？因为回程的车费，你在里面已经付过了。

Canberra exists because Sydney and Melbourne couldn't agree on anything, so they built a city that nobody could possibly be jealous of. Mission accomplished.

It was designed by an American architect, which explains why it feels like a very nice airport with sheep. The roundabouts are so plentiful that locals don't give directions, they give revolutions. The lake is fake, the population is mostly public servants waiting for Friday, and the kangaroos outnumber the nightlife.

Your Parliament House is literally buried in a hill so people can walk on the roof, the only time Australians get to stand on politicians.

For your centenary you commissioned the Skywhale, a giant flying balloon with ten enormous boobs, and somehow that's still the most exciting thing to happen here.

Canberra: home of Summernats, Floriade, and legally purchasable X-rated videos. Burnouts, tulips and porn, because you've got to do something until the next Senate estimates hearing.

澳大利亚当年选首都，悉尼和墨尔本吵得不可开交，谁都不让谁。最后怎么解决的？在两个城市中间找了块羊吃草的地，说：“行了，都别争了，这儿！”

这就是堪培拉。它不是首都，它是离婚协议里分给孩子的那套房子。

而且这城市是比赛比出来的。全世界征集设计，一个美国建筑师赢了。所以澳大利亚的首都，是美国人画的图纸。湖也是挖出来的，还拿这个美国人的名字命名，叫格里芬湖。连湖都不是本地的。

你去开车就知道了，堪培拉的环岛多到什么程度？导航从头到尾就一句话：“请进入环岛，第二个出口驶出。”你开二十分钟，一直在转圈，最后发现你又回到了国会大厦门口。

国会大厦还盖在山里，屋顶是草坪，老百姓可以上去散步。全世界唯一一个，你能站在政府头上，政府还觉得这是设计亮点的地方。

晚上九点，整座城市一片安静，只有袋鼠在马路上溜达。我当时就明白了：堪培拉没有夜生活，堪培拉的夜生活是袋鼠的。

Brasília, you're what happens when an architect gets an entire country's budget and nobody says, "Maybe add a sidewalk?" You're shaped like an airplane, which is fitting, because everyone's goal is to board one by Friday afternoon. Your addresses read like Wi-Fi passwords: "SQS 308, Bloco C, apartamento 402." That's not a home. That's a parking spot on a spaceship. Kubitschek promised "fifty years in five," and you delivered: it's been sixty-five years and you still feel unfinished. Your Congress has one bowl facing up to receive the money and one facing down to hide it. You've got a row of identical ministry buildings so nobody can tell which one the scandal came from. In August the humidity drops so low that the only thing drier than the air is a deputy's sense of shame. Even your lake is fake. Honestly? On brand.

Brasília, you're the only city designed to look like an airplane, and somehow everyone still just wants to leave on one. Politicians fly in Tuesday, take a bribe Wednesday, and they're gone by Thursday like it's a timeshare.

Your addresses read like a Wi-Fi password: "SQS 308, Bloco C, Apartamento 402." I'm not visiting a friend, I'm resetting a router.

Niemeyer gave you gorgeous curves, then Lúcio Costa forgot pedestrians. Want to walk to the bakery? Hope you enjoy the eight-lane Eixão and a light jog through a tesourinha.

Your humidity drops to 10 percent. Your congress has one bowl facing up, one facing down: one for collecting money, the other for hiding it.

And you were built with no corners, so Brazil's capital has no boteco na esquina. That's not urban planning. That's a human rights violation.

堪培拉怎么当上首都的？悉尼和墨尔本抢，吵到最后国家说：你俩都别当，我在中间找块羊圈。这就像离婚抢孩子，法官把孩子判给了路边一只袋鼠。

为了像个首都，还从美国请人来设计，挖了个人工湖。别的首都是“有河才建城”，堪培拉是“城建好了一看没河，赶紧挖一个”。

路全是环岛。在堪培拉迷路不叫迷路，叫公转。

国会大厦盖在山里，屋顶铺草，老百姓能走上去。全世界唯一一个能站在政客头顶上的地方。可惜晚上来得最多的是袋鼠。议员们终于见到了真正的选民。

Juicero, you beautiful $120 million monument to Silicon Valley. You launched at seven hundred dollars to squeeze a bag. A bag! Then Bloomberg reporters squeezed that same bag with their bare hands and got basically the same juice, only faster. You got outperformed by a guy with a grip strength of "typing."

Doug Evans bragged you pressed with four tons of force, enough to lift two Teslas. Buddy, it's kale. The kale didn't need a forklift.

And it needed Wi-Fi. It scanned a QR code before it'd let you drink. Your router goes down and suddenly your breakfast is asking for credentials. Who designs a juicer that can be bricked?

Google Ventures funded this. Kleiner Perkins funded this. Somewhere, a man is still holding a lukewarm pouch, waiting for a firmware update so he's allowed to eat a carrot.

Juicero, you were a $400 Wi-Fi-connected juicer that delivered four tons of force, enough, your engineers bragged, to lift two Teslas, and Bloomberg proved the job could be done by a guy with hands. You raised $120 million from Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins to compete with *squeezing*. Every single customer already owned the competing product. It came in pairs.

You sold $8 bags of chopped produce that had to scan a QR code and phone home before you'd juice them. A juicer that needed internet. Imagine the outage: "Sorry, AWS is down, enjoy your sealed pouch of regret." You'd refuse to press an expired pack, like a bouncer for kale.

Doug Evans compared himself to Steve Jobs. Steve Jobs put a thousand songs in your pocket. Doug put a sack of mush in a vise and asked for your Wi-Fi password. Silicon Valley's most expensive way to say, "Just use your hands."

我去了趟巴西利亚。这城市是1960年平地画出来的，从天上看像一架飞机。问题是，人不住在天上。你在地上走，就是在机翼上散步：没有街角，没有小卖部，只有八车道，还有一种眼神，意思是“您走路过去？勇士。”

地址也绝了。我问朋友住哪，他说“SQS 308，C栋”。我说这是地址还是Wi-Fi密码？在巴西利亚，你不是住在一条街上，你是住在一个坐标里。

国会大厦顶上俩碗，一个朝上一个朝下。导游说，朝上的是众议院，接住人民的意见；朝下的是参议院……我说懂了，负责把意见扣住。

整座城规划得这么完美，就漏算了一件事：人偶尔想走两步路。

硅谷有个榨汁机叫Juicero，首发卖699美元，后来降到400。它号称能对着果汁包施加四吨的压力。四吨啊朋友们！你家冰箱里那袋菜，这辈子都没受过这种委屈。

问题是，它不能榨水果。你得另外买它家的专用果汁包，一包五到八美元。包上还印着二维码，机器得联网扫码，确认没过期，才肯开工。家里WiFi一断，你就只能抱着一袋过不了安检的菠菜干瞪眼。

后来彭博社的记者干了一件事：直接上手捏那个包。结果用手挤，跟用机器榨差不多快，挤出来的汁也差不多多。

一个融资一亿多美元的公司，最后输给了人的手。还是不用联网的那种手。

我去了趟巴西利亚。这城市是从天上设计的，整体像一架飞机。可人是住在地上的啊！站在地上你看不见飞机，只看见十几车道的大马路，对面就是目的地，中间没有一条斑马线。设计师的意思很明确：想过马路？请先登机。

问路，人家说：“SQS 308，C栋。”我以为他在报验证码。这儿没街名，只有南翼北翼加数字。你住的不是小区，是机翼上的座位号。

国会门口俩碗，一个正放一个倒扣。正碗是众议院，敞开听民意；倒碗是参议院，扣着搞反思。议员们周一到周三在碗里待着，周四一到，全飞回老家。也对，住在飞机里，谁不想下飞机？

Keurig, you took the simplest drink in human history (hot water, beans) and added a subscription model. Your own inventor said he regrets making you. Imagine your dad publicly apologizing for you and you're still in every dentist's waiting room.

You tried DRM on coffee. Keurig 2.0 literally scanned pods and refused to brew anything off-brand. You're the only appliance that's ever asked me for a license.

Every K-Cup costs more per pound than a decent steak, and you've buried enough of them to circle the Earth a dozen times. Archaeologists will dig them up and assume we worshipped tiny plastic thimbles.

And the Keurig Kold? A $370 soda machine that died faster than the flat Coke it made.

Your descale light blinks like a cry for help. Honestly, same.

你们知道Juicero吗？硅谷的榨汁机，拿了一亿两千万美元投资，卖699美元，后来降到399。它能对一袋水果泥施加四吨的压力，四吨！那是能把一辆皮卡压成午餐肉的力气，用来对付一袋切好的菠菜。

而且它只认自家的果蔬包，一包五到八美元，包上有二维码。机器得联网，扫码确认没过期才肯开工。家里断网了？对不起，你今天没资格喝果汁。

最绝的是彭博社的记者，把那包东西拿出来，直接用手捏，捏得比机器还快，一滴不少。

所以这一亿两千万美元，干的就是一件事：把“用手捏塑料袋”这个动作，做成了订阅制。

我小时候吃果冻也是这么吸的，我妈从来没想过找人融资。

Keurig, you took the one drink humanity had perfected over five hundred years and said, "What if it came in a tiny plastic thimble that outlives your grandchildren?" Your own inventor said he regrets making you. When your dad disowns you, that's a phase. When the guy who invented you disowns you, that's a recall.

You make coffee one sad, lukewarm cup at a time, then flash "DESCALE" like a check-engine light for a machine that costs forty bucks. Remember Keurig 2.0? You put DRM on coffee. You were scanning pods like a bouncer: "Sorry, sir, you're not on the list." Nobody was pirating Folgers! And your "Strong" button just drips slower, which isn't strength. That's procrastination.

You're not a coffee maker. You're a plastic-dispensing subscription that occasionally hiccups out hot brown water.

Crocs. The only shoe that looks like a colander that wanted to go to brunch. Thirteen holes, and somehow none of them let the dignity out, because there was never any in there.

You were invented as a boat shoe. A *boat* shoe. The one place you were built for, and you'd just float away. So you stayed on land and started fights with escalators. Malls had to post warnings. You're the only footwear with a rap sheet against machinery.

And "sport mode"? Flipping a strap behind your heel doesn't make you athletic. It makes you a clog wearing a seatbelt.

Then came Jibbitz, little charms you jam into the holes so grown adults can accessorize ventilation. Congratulations. You turned a shoe into a fridge door.

我家有台Keurig胶囊咖啡机。它的发明人约翰·西尔万后来公开说：我后悔了，我自己家都不用。亲爹都不认的孩子，被我领回家了。

它的流程特别有仪式感：掀盖，放进一个小塑料杯，合上，“咔”，一根针从上到下把它捅穿，跟行刑一样。然后机器开始咕噜咕噜，喘得像在交代遗言，最后挤出八盎司褐色的水。

我算过账，按胶囊价格，这咖啡折合四十多美元一磅。我喝的不是咖啡，是包装。

最绝的是Keurig 2.0，会扫描你的胶囊，不是官方授权的，不给出水。一台咖啡机，在我自己家里，查我的身份证。

还有那个“除垢”指示灯，亮了三年了。它在提醒，我假装没看见，我们就这么过着。

Crocs. The only shoe that looks like Swiss cheese that wanted to be a boat. You were invented for sailing, and the one place nobody wears you is a boat. You're at Applebee's, squeaking across a wet floor like a dolphin in distress.

You have holes. On purpose. Then you sell us Jibbitz to fill the holes. That's not fashion, that's a protection racket with a SpongeBob charm.

And "sport mode"? Flipping a strap behind my heel doesn't make me an athlete. It makes me a toddler about to sprint into traffic.

You made a KFC bucket clog with charms that smelled like fried chicken. That's not footwear. That's a foam cry for help.

Nurses love you. Chefs love you. Which proves you're comfortable for people who've stopped caring who's looking at their feet.

我家有台Keurig胶囊咖啡机。它的发明人公开说过，后悔发明了这玩意儿。亲爹都不认的东西，我天天早上伺候着。

放一颗胶囊，合盖，“咔”，一根针扎穿锡纸，像给咖啡打疫苗。然后它开始吭哧吭哧地叫，跟拖拉机打火似的，叫了半天，挤出来一小杯。我按的是最大杯，它给我的是稀释过的勇气。

最绝的是它还查户口。有一代机器，你塞别家牌子的胶囊，屏幕直接跳：不识别。我喝口咖啡，你在门口查我暂住证？

喝完那个小塑料杯往垃圾桶一扔，我看着它，它看着我。我喝了它五分钟，它要陪我子孙几百年。

我一直搞不懂洞洞鞋。你说它丑吧，它确实丑，长得像两块烤胀了的面包。但最离谱的是鞋面上那十几个洞，官方说是透气，行，我认了。结果店员转头就给我推荐鞋花，一个三十块，专门往洞里插。我花三百块买了一双全是洞的鞋，再花三百块把洞一个个堵上？这跟买个漏勺回家，拿胶布把眼儿全封上有什么区别？

还有后跟那根带子，翻到前面叫休闲模式，扣到后面叫"运动模式"。运动模式！我就信了，扣上带子去追公交。我人上车了，鞋还留在站台上。司机看了一眼说："你那鞋不走啊？"我说："可能它觉得，运动完了，该休闲了。"

我买了双洞洞鞋，穿了三天才搞明白那些洞是干嘛的：是给你插钱的。一个小恐龙二十九，一个小汉堡三十五。鞋才两百块，脚面上挂了八百块的塑料。现在我走路都不敢踢东西，踢一下掉一个汉堡。

还有后面那根带子。翻上去叫"休闲模式"，翻下来扣住脚后跟，叫"运动模式"。运动模式？我穿着两艘小船去跑八百米？

最绝的是下雨天。满身透气孔，水从洞里进来，再从洞里出去。我的脚泡在里面像腌泡菜，走一步"噗叽"一声。我妈在楼下听见了，以为我偷偷养了只鸭子。

UGG boots. Even the name sounds like the noise you make pulling them on. Australian surfers invented them to warm their feet after the ocean, and somehow they became snow boots that dissolve in snow. One puddle and you're wearing a salt-stained topographic map. They're sheepskin, so you skip the socks, so by February they smell like the sheep's revenge. Every pair eventually collapses outward until you're walking on the sides of your ankles like a newborn giraffe in a bread costume. And that's the look: two chestnut loaves. You don't walk in UGGs; you shuffle, like the ghost of Paris Hilton still searching for her Juicy tracksuit. And now they're back with platforms, so you can roll an ankle from higher up. It's not footwear. It's a bathrobe that learned to commute.

UGG boots. The only footwear named after a review. Australian surfers made these to warm their feet after the ocean, and somehow America decided the ocean was the mall. They're sheepskin, which means a sheep died so you could wear a slipper to the DMV. One puddle and they're covered in salt lines like a topographic map of everywhere you regret going. Zero arch support, so after two weeks your heel caves sideways and you're walking on the boot's ankle like it owes you money. You wear them barefoot, so by February they smell like a wet lamb's final wish. They're as waterproof as a muffin. Oprah put them on her Favorite Things list. She's since moved on. Twenty years later they're back with platform soles, proving even a mistake wants to be taller.

UGG这东西，叫雪地靴，最怕的就是雪。翻毛羊皮，沾一点水就留一圈地图，比我前任还记仇。下雪天穿UGG的人，走路全是踮着的，绕着水坑跳，跟排雷似的。你一个雪地靴，一下雪就请假？

而且它没有形状。刚买回来是双靴子，穿三个月变成两个面包，再穿半年，后跟往外塌，从后面看两只脚摆成一个"八"字。人还站得笔直，鞋已经躺平了。

最绝的是名字。据说UGG就是从ugly来的，意思是"丑"。人家老老实实告诉你了，它丑。是我们自己不信，排着队花一两千，买了双自我介绍。

Monopoly, you were invented by Lizzie Magie to warn people that landlords ruin lives, and somehow you became the thing Grandpa uses to teach eight-year-olds that ruining lives is fun. You're the only game where getting arrested is a power move, because late in the game jail is the safest property on the board. Your mascot is a man everyone swears wears a monocle. He doesn't. He's just so smug our brains added one. You promise "about an hour" and deliver a hostage situation. Nobody has ever actually finished you. You just end when somebody flips the board over Marvin Gardens. You award ten bucks for second place in a beauty contest, which is still more than Baltic Avenue pulls in. And the banker who skims from the bank isn't a cheater. He's the only player who read the theme.

我一直不明白UGG为什么叫雪地靴，它怕雪啊朋友们！翻毛羊皮，沾一点雪水，第二天就长出一圈白色盐渍，像地图上的海岸线。下雪天穿UGG出门，你不是在踩雪，你是在护送它。鞋底还是平的，往结冰的路上一站，人直接变冰壶。

而且它是澳大利亚的！一个圣诞节穿短裤烧烤的国家，给全世界定义雪地靴，就像撒哈拉出了本滑雪教程。

穿俩月，鞋跟往外一塌，脚踝往外撇，走路像刚下马。远看两只脚各蹲着一个烤糊的吐司。最绝的是里面那层羊毛，号称不用穿袜子。是不用，脱下来那味儿，袜子也不敢跟你了。

Monopoly, you were invented by Lizzie Magie to teach people that landlords ruin lives, and somehow the lesson everyone learned was "buy Park Place." Then Parker Brothers bought you from a guy who basically stole you, which is the most on-brand origin story in history.

You're the only game where "second prize in a beauty contest" counts as income and jail is solved with a coupon. Your mascot looks like he foreclosed on the Pringles guy, and half of America swears he wears a monocle. He doesn't. We just assumed a man that rich would be hiding something.

Nobody has ever finished you. Games don't end; your cousin just flips the board over Marvin Gardens, which you misspelled, by the way. It's Marven. Even your real estate is a scam.

Risk is the only game where you can conquer the entire planet and still lose to the guy who's been hiding in Australia since 7 p.m. Four territories, one entrance, and he just sits there like a guy at a party who won't leave the snack table.

This game has a map drawn by someone who heard about geography once, at a bar. Kamchatka borders Alaska. Ukraine is the size of Brazil. Yakutsk and Irkutsk are vital military objectives, and nobody at the table can find them on a real map.

The rules say the defender wins ties, which is the most realistic thing about it, because nobody actually finishes Risk. They just quit at 2 a.m. when someone's dad flips the board over Siberia.

And the pieces? Little plastic cannons and horses. Napoleonic warfare, global scale, and the whole thing is decided by rolling a 6 against your cousin Greg.

我家玩大富翁，从没人看过规则书。比如那个"免费停车"，官方规则里它就是个空格，屁事没有。可我们家硬是把所有罚款堆在中间，谁停上去谁拿走。本来两小时的游戏，被我们一改，能玩到天亮。

还有坐牢。全世界只有这个游戏，坐牢是福利。前期你哭着求保释，后期满地都是别人的酒店，你就在牢里蹲着，一边收租一边喊："别放我出去，外面太危险了！"

最离谱的是那张卡："选美比赛获得第二名，领取10元。"我爸，五十岁，秃顶，抽到这张，站起来给全家鞠了一躬。

那晚他输光了，但他是全场唯一被认证过颜值的人。

大富翁这游戏，教会我人生第一课：坐牢是好事。真的，满地图都是我表哥的酒店，走一步交一千八，整张地图只有监狱里不收钱。我在里面蹲了三回合，出来的时候哭了，外面的世界太贵了。

还有那张“命运”卡，写着“银行出错，你获得两百元”。银行出错，钱给你？谁当的银行？我表哥。他左手管银行，右手管自己，钱一直从左手流进右手，全家没人敢查账。

最狠的是这游戏根本没有结局。它不是有人赢了才结束，是有人掀了桌子才结束。我家那盒大富翁到现在还缺两张地契、一个小狗棋子，外加我跟表哥十五年的感情。

我最近跟朋友玩《战国风云》，就是那个在世界地图上掷骰子打仗的游戏。我第一次知道，原来世界上最重要的战略要地，叫堪察加。现实里那地方全是熊，在这游戏里，它是通往阿拉斯加的跨海大桥，兵家必争。

而且这游戏防守方掷骰子打平算赢。你带着三个骰子冲过去，对方两个骰子，你掷出两个六，他也掷出两个六，你就死俩人。这叫什么？这叫守门员发球。

最阴的永远是那个开局就缩在澳洲的人。全场打得血流成河，他守着一个入口，每回合多领两个兵，坐在那儿跟袋鼠一样看热闹。

你想占亚洲？亚洲在这游戏里不是个洲，是个坑。伊尔库茨克、雅库茨克，这些地名我这辈子就在这张地图上听过，而且每一个都在被三个人同时抢。

最后谁也没赢。游戏打了五个小时，有人说“我明天还要上班”，世界和平就这么实现了。

Risk, you're the only game where "world domination" takes longer than actual world domination. Genghis Khan conquered Asia faster than my cousin conquered Ukraine, and my cousin had six armies and a dream. Your map looks like it was drawn from a description of Earth overheard on a bus. Kamchatka borders Alaska? Irkutsk and Yakutsk get more real estate than most of Africa? You taught a generation that the winning strategy is hiding in Australia like a coward and waiting for everyone else to bleed out over Siam. The defender wins ties, which explains the forty armies I lost trying to get through one guy in Egypt. And one plastic cannon is worth ten soldiers? Finally, accurate military budgeting. Five hours in, two players left, nobody's had fun since the first card set. That's not a board game, Risk. That's a hostage situation.

NFTs, you're the only investment where the product is a receipt, and the receipt is a link to a JPEG hosted on some guy's server. When he stops paying the bill, congratulations: you own a 404.

You convinced grown adults to pay $300,000 for a cartoon monkey in a sailor hat, then charge them $80 in gas fees to watch it lose 98% of its value. Jimmy Fallon showed off his ape on national television like a kid holding up a cool rock.

People right-clicked and hit "save as," and you called it theft. Theft of *what*? It's still there! I'm looking at it!

Every project had a roadmap: metaverse, merch, a members-only yacht party. Instead the roadmap was a Discord mod named Kevin typing "we're still early" at 3 a.m.

WAGMI, you said. We did not all make it.

NFTs, everybody! The only art form where the most common review is "right-click, save." You paid four hundred thousand dollars for a cartoon monkey in a captain's hat, and I have the same monkey as my phone background. The difference? I didn't pay a gas fee bigger than the art. Technically you don't even own the picture. You own a receipt pointing to a link on a server some guy in Ohio forgot to renew. That's not a masterpiece; that's a parking stub for a JPEG. And remember the roadmap? Metaverse, merch, a yacht party! Then the founder pulled the rug, deleted the Discord, and left you holding a "rare trait": sunglasses. Jimmy Fallon showed Paris Hilton his ape on national TV like a proud dad. Now it's worth less than the TV.

我玩《战国风云》，最大收获是地理全学歪了。到现在我都觉得世界上最重要的地方是伊尔库茨克、雅库茨克，还有堪察加。堪察加能一步打到阿拉斯加，现实里这叫白令海峡，在我们家这叫“你又偷家”。

每局开始，总有一个人直奔澳大利亚。为什么？因为澳大利亚只有一个入口！全世界打得血流成河，他一个人蹲在袋鼠堆里，每回合多领两个兵，跟收物业费一样。

最气人的是骰子。我进攻扔三个，他防守扔两个，平局算他赢。我扔出三个六冲上去，他扔两个六，我还得倒赔俩兵。

六个小时过去，没人统一世界。大家只在一件事上达成了统一：以后谁再提议玩这个，全桌一起出兵打他。

我有个朋友，前两年花八万块买了一只猴子。不是活的，是张图，一只戴墨镜、表情很厌世的卡通猴。我说这图我右键就能存啊。他急了：“你存的是图，我拥有的是区块链上的所有权凭证！”我说凭证里写的啥？他说，一个链接，指向那张图。

所以他花八万，买了张写着“图在那边”的小纸条。

而且图根本不在链上，在别人服务器里。哪天人家服务器欠费，他的猴子就变成404。全世界最贵的404。

上个月他要卖，挂了三个月，最后两百块成交。光gas费就三百。

卖掉一只猴子，倒贴一百。这叫什么？这叫Web3。

Beanie Babies. The only retirement plan where the retiree was a five-dollar bear stuffed with plastic pellets. A whole generation bought plastic protectors for a toy's ear tag, then sealed the toy in a Ziploc so no child could ever love it. You weren't a stuffed animal; you were a 401(k) with a poem on it. And those poems! Ty Warner doing greeting-card Shakespeare for people who thought Princess the bear would pay for college. Princess paid for nothing. Neither did the Teenie Beanies everyone hoarded from McDonald's while throwing away the actual Happy Meal. A divorcing couple in Las Vegas literally split their collection on a courtroom floor, one Beanie at a time. That's your legacy: custody battles over a moose named Chocolate. Even your creator got busted hiding money from the IRS, because he was the only one who ever made any.

我朋友花八万买了个NFT，一只戴墨镜的猴子。我说给我看看，他把手机递过来，我长按，保存。现在我俩都有这只猴子了。

他急了，说不一样，他有的是“所有权”，写在区块链上。我说链上存的是猴子吗？他说不是，是一个链接，指向猴子。

八万块，买了个链接。我们小区门口发传单的大姐一天塞给我二十个链接，还送纸巾。

上个月更绝，存那张图的服务器忘了续费。现在他拥有一个永不篡改、全网公证、刻在区块链上的：404。

转账时还另付了三百手续费。他说那叫Gas费，汽油钱。我说你这猴子是开车来的？

Beanie Babies, look at you. Half bear, half beanbag, all retirement plan that never paid out. An entire generation of parents bought you instead of index funds. Somewhere a man is still storing Princess, the purple Diana bear, in a climate-controlled unit, waiting for the market to "recover." Buddy, the market recovered. It just didn't take you with it.

Your most valuable feature was a heart-shaped paper tag. People bought plastic tag protectors. For the tag. That's like buying a phone case for your receipt.

And every tag had a little poem rhyming "bear" with "care." Hallmark called that lazy.

A Las Vegas couple had to divide you on a courtroom floor during their divorce, one at a time. That's the most anyone has wanted you since 1999: only to make sure their ex didn't get you.

Ty Warner got a billion dollars. You got plastic pellets.

Slack, you started as the internal chat tool for a failed video game called Glitch, and honestly? Still the most accurate name you've ever had.

You promised to kill email. Instead you gave us email that *knocks*. That little wooden knock-brush sound has triggered more cortisol than any boss in history. I hear it in the shower. I hear it at funerals.

You invented the green dot, so now my employer knows I went to the bathroom for nineteen minutes. You invented "is typing…" so my manager can type for four straight minutes and send "ok."

Threads? Nobody can find them. Huddles? A Zoom call that ambushes you. And somehow every company has 400 channels, and the only active one is #random, where Kevin posts his sourdough.

Your name literally stands for "Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge." Searchable. Sure. Try finding that one link from Tuesday. 👀 reacted by 3 people.

Slack. Named after the one thing you'll never have again.

You promised to kill email, and you did, by replacing it with forty channels that are each email with a typing indicator. Nothing builds dread like "Greg is typing..." for ninety seconds, followed by "hey." Just "hey." Greg, that's not a message, that's a hostage situation.

You gave us threads, so every conversation happens in two places and nobody knows which one's real. You gave us huddles: a meeting that jumps out of a bush. You gave us the green dot, so my boss can monitor my bathroom breaks like a heart rate.

And that knock sound. I hear it in the grocery store. I hear it at funerals.

Slack, you're the only app that needs three gigs of RAM to tell me someone reacted with a dancing parrot.

我小时候，家里把豆豆娃当理财产品。我妈的规矩是：熊可以摸，那个红色心形的Ty吊牌不能碰。吊牌一折，资产腰斩。她还专门买了塑料吊牌保护套，给吊牌穿防弹衣，熊本身光着。

每只熊的吊牌上都印着生日，还有一首小诗。我妈记得每只熊的生日，就是记不住我的。

那只紫色的戴安娜王妃熊，她说将来给我交大学学费。现在我三十多了，学费是自己贷的。那只熊还在柜子里，吊牌完好，小诗完好，市场价二十块包邮。

最离谱是麦当劳送迷你豆豆娃那年，我爸一口气买了二十份开心乐园餐。汉堡全扔了，玩具连包装都没拆，摆成一排。那是我们家第一次搞分散投资。

九十年代的美国人，把一袋塑料颗粒缝进布里，起个名字，当传家宝囤。豆豆娃最值钱的部分不是熊，是耳朵上那个红心形的纸吊牌。吊牌折个角，身价腰斩。大家专门买塑料壳把吊牌套起来，孩子刚伸手，全家尖叫：“别摸！那是你的大学学费！”

最绝的是吊牌印错字反而更贵。全世界只有这个行业，错别字能升值。

1999年拉斯维加斯一对夫妻离婚，法官让他们蹲在法庭地板上，一只一只分豆豆娃。这才是豆豆娃精神：房子归你，车归你，那只紫色戴安娜王妃熊，必须归我。

二十年后打开柜子，熊还在，学费没了。

我们公司用Slack。Slack最吓人的不是消息，是对话框底下那行小字：“张总正在输入……”他输入了三分钟。三分钟！我连辞职信都在脑子里写完了。最后弹出来一个字：“在？”

还有那个提示音，“咚咚”，像有人拿指节敲木头门。现在我在家听见有人敲门，第一反应是去看哪个频道亮了。

最阴的是表情回应。我在群里发了一份方案，老板一个字没说，就给我点了个👀。眼睛。什么意思？你在看？你在盯着我？还是你也没看懂？

后来我休年假，状态改成“休假中”，配了棵椰子树🌴。结果头像旁边那个小绿点一直亮着。全公司都知道了：这个人在海边，在看Slack。

Microsoft Teams is the only app that got popular the way a parking ticket gets popular: it came free with Office 365 and nobody could say no. It's a chat app that eats more RAM than Chrome, which is like a goldfish outeating a horse. It marks you "Away" if you blink for five minutes, which is why half of corporate America owns a mouse jiggler. Every file you share vanishes into SharePoint, a place so mysterious even Microsoft sends search parties. There's chat, there's channels, there's "posts," and nobody knows which one Kevin used. They released "New Teams" to replace "Classic Teams," and somehow both are running on my laptop right now, fighting. And that notification sound? That little knock-knock haunts people on vacation. Teams, you didn't win the remote work war. You were just pre-installed.

Microsoft Teams is the only app that marks me "Away" after five minutes of deep thought but keeps me "Available" for three hours after I've died. It's not software. It's a hall monitor in a purple vest.

Teams eats more RAM than the game I'm pretending not to play. It launches on startup uninvited, then takes four minutes to load a chat that just says "ok."

Where are my files? SharePoint. Where's SharePoint? Nobody knows. Teams ships them off like a kid to boarding school.

Then they gave us "New Teams," which is Old Teams with a fresh coat of lag. IT has told me to "clear the cache" so often I do it in my sleep.

Nobody chose Teams. It came free with Office. Fitting, since so did Clippy.

Slack说它是来消灭邮件的。确实，邮件只有一个收件箱，Slack给你四十个频道，每个都是加粗的。

我最怕那行"正在输入……"。老板输入，停了，又输入，又停了，三分钟后发来一个👀。这不是表情，这是监控摄像头。

还有"在话题中回复"下面那个小勾选框："同时发送到频道"。这功能就是给告状设计的：我回复你，顺便让全公司都看见。

最狠的是头像旁边那个绿点。我倒杯水回来，它变灰了，像被拔了氧气管。所以我现在每五分钟碰一下鼠标。我不是在上班，我是在给自己做心肺复苏。

我们公司用Teams，不是因为它好用，是因为买Office送的。就跟买手机送的那个壳一样，你不用，它也在那儿。

Teams最狠的是那个状态灯。你五分钟不碰鼠标，头像就从绿变黄，“离开”。领导一看：哟，摸鱼呢？我同事为了保住那个绿点，上淘宝买了个鼠标晃动器，二十九块九。全公司生产力最高的设备，就是它。

还有文件。你在群聊里发个Excel，它不在聊天里，它跑去了SharePoint。SharePoint是什么？没人知道。就像你把钥匙交给门卫，门卫说放在了“云端某个文件夹”。

最可怕的是电脑开着Teams，风扇呼呼转，内存吃掉两个G，我以为在跑渲染。打开一看：它在加载我的头像。

我们公司用Microsoft Teams，我现在最怕的不是老板，是我头像旁边那个小圆点。绿的是“有空”，黄的是“离开”。五分钟不动鼠标，它自动变黄，跟告密一样。我上趟厕所回来，全部门都知道我肠胃不好。

后来我网上买了个鼠标晃动器，二十九块九，每天替我在线八小时，绩效比我好。

Teams还特别关心我。开会我一张嘴，它弹窗：“你似乎在说话，但你已静音。”它听见了！它知道我在说话！那你倒是帮我传过去啊！它不传，它就提醒你一下，显得它很懂事。

最绝的是它还分“新版Teams”和“经典Teams”。用经典的时候我嫌它卡，新版一出我才明白：原来卡，也能出新版本。

LaTeX, you're the only software where "it compiled" counts as an emotional milestone. One missing brace and you blame line 1 of a 400-line file, then sit there with a question mark like we're playing a text adventure from 1985. I put a figure on page 3; you float it to the appendix because you "know better." You have to run twice just to learn your own page numbers, three times if BibTeX shows up, like a guy who needs two friends to remind him his name. Your answer to every problem is another \usepackage, so my preamble is now longer than my thesis. Every paper you touch looks gorgeous, and identical, because everyone on Earth can spot Computer Modern from across a conference hall. And your favorite warning, "Overfull \hbox, badness 10000"? Honestly, that's just how I feel about you.

Microsoft Word, you've had forty years to learn one thing: how to let me move a picture one millimeter without three paragraphs fleeing to page nine. You don't wrap text, you take hostages.

You underline my own name in red like I'm the typo. You turn my grocery list into a numbered legal document I can't escape. I hit Enter once and suddenly I'm in a style called "Heading 7" that I've never met.

And Track Changes? That's not editing, that's a crime scene where everyone bled in a different color.

You fired Clippy, the only one of you who ever admitted I looked like I needed help.

And every crash, you hand me "Document1 (Recovered)" like a cat dropping a dead bird on the porch: proud, useless, and somehow from 2 PM yesterday.

我写论文用LaTeX，大家都说它排版好看。好看是真好看，就是不听话。我放一张图，写个，意思是“就放这儿”。它不理。我加个感叹号，，等于跪下求它。它把图扔到了第三页，跟参考文献挤在一起。

引用更绝。第一次编译，满篇“如图??所示”，导师以为我在质疑自己的数据。网上说编译两次就好。好了。再加一篇文献，又得pdflatex、bibtex、pdflatex、pdflatex，这不是写论文，这是念咒。

还不能随手打百分号。我写“准确率提升了30%，效果显著”，后半句直接消失。LaTeX的意思是：提升了就行，显不显著它说了算。

text:
我写论文用LaTeX，导师说这叫专业。专业在哪？我放一张图，代码写在第三页，它排到第七页。我加个，意思是“就放这儿”，它理解成“建议考虑一下”。我改成，它放了，然后后面空出半页，跟我冷战。

最绝的是报错。我少写一个大括号，它说：第403行，Missing $ inserted。那行根本没有公式！它自己塞了个美元符号，然后说是我缺的。这不是编译器，这是碰瓷。

还有引用。编译一遍，满屏问号。再编译一遍，还是问号。得先跑BibTeX，再编译两遍，它才肯说这是第几篇文献。交论文前那晚我不是在改论文，是在做法事：念一遍咒，问号少几个。
