text:
Microsoft Word, ladies and gentlemen. It's the only program where nudging a photo one pixel to the left sends three paragraphs to page nine and summons a blank final page you will never, ever delete.

Word has been around for forty years and still can't decide what font it is. Times New Roman, then Calibri, now Aptos. It's having a midlife crisis in 11-point.

It underlines my own name in red. Wavy red. Like *I'm* the typo.

Try making a numbered list. Word says, "Got it, starting at 1." Second item: "Also 1." Third item: "Here's 4. It's indented. It's a letter now."

And Track Changes isn't a feature. It's a crime scene: strikethroughs everywhere, plus forty comments from someone named "Author."

Word, you gave us Clippy, and somehow he was the most helpful part.

LaTeX, you're the only software that makes PhDs feel stupid. You're from 1984 and you dress like it: backslashes everywhere, curly braces like a nervous tic. I tell you to put a figure "here," and you treat "here" as a suggestion, then file it four pages later next to the bibliography, like a sock lost in a dryer. Your error messages are poetry: "Missing $ inserted." Inserted where? Why? You won't say. You just blame line 1 of a 40-page file because I typed an underscore in a URL. My citations are double question marks until I compile you twice, then a third time, out of spite. And everyone needs to know it's pronounced "lay-tech," not like the glove. Honestly, at least the glove stretches. Overfull \hbox? Badness 10000? Buddy, that's not a warning. That's your autobiography.

我觉得Word是全世界最记仇的软件。你在文档里插一张图，往右挪一毫米，就一毫米，后面三十页的文字集体跳楼，表格跑到下一页，标题孤零零留在上一页最底下，像被父母遗弃了。

你想让页码从第三页开始？好，先学“分节符”，再取消“链接到前一节”，再发现封面也冒出个页码，再重来。我考研都没这么认真过。

最绝的是自动编号。你打个“1.”，它说“我懂你”，一回车，“2.”。你说不用了谢谢，删掉，它给你缩进两格。你跟它较劲半小时，最后的解决办法是：新建一个文档，从记事本里重新粘过来。

所以Word教会了我一件事：真正的排版大师，都在狂按Ctrl+Z。

Graphene, you're the only Nobel Prize winner ever discovered with Scotch tape. Two physicists peeled a pencil and found you, which means your origin story is literally "kid procrastinating on homework."

Since 2004 you've been "about to revolutionize" batteries, computers, water filters, and space elevators. Twenty years later your biggest commercial win is a tennis racket. You're not a wonder material, you're a press release with a hexagon fetish.

Everyone loves to say you're two hundred times stronger than steel. Great. You're also one atom thick. Nobody's impressed that a sheet of paper beats a battleship per ounce.

And for the supposed savior of electronics, you have zero bandgap. You can't even turn off. You're a transistor with no off switch, the guy at the party who never stops talking.

You're graphite with a LinkedIn profile.

Graphene, you're one atom thick, and somehow that's still more depth than your business plan. Two hundred times stronger than steel, conducts better than copper, and twenty years later your biggest commercial win is a sticker on a tennis racket. You were discovered with Scotch tape. *Scotch tape!* You're the only Nobel Prize that could've been found in a kindergarten craft drawer. And let's be honest: you're pencil lead that went to grad school. Your cousin graphite has been writing grocery lists for centuries; you've been writing grant proposals. Every year a headline swears you'll revolutionize batteries, chips, water filters. Every year you're still in the lab, like a thirty-year-old in his parents' basement. You can't even be a decent transistor. No bandgap. You literally cannot turn off. Graphene: the material of the future, permanently.

我用Word写论文，最怕的不是写不出来，是插图。我就把图往右挪了一毫米，后面三页文字原地起义，表格跑到第七页，页眉直接跑我妈家去了。

还有自动编号。我敲个“1.”，它说：我懂，我来。我一回车，它“2.”；我删掉，它退回“1.”；我再删，它给我缩进了。拉扯十分钟，它赢了，我论文里从此住着一个谁也删不掉的“3.”。

室友说你点那个反着的P，显示段落标记。一点，满屏小箭头、小点点，论文像得了麻疹。原来我看到的空白，全是Word偷偷藏的东西。

交上去，导师打开第一句：“你这怎么是兼容模式？”

石墨烯这东西，我是真服。2004年，两个科学家拿透明胶带往铅笔芯上一粘、一撕、再一撕，撕出来一个诺贝尔奖。我小学天天拿胶带粘错别字，粘出来的是罚抄五十遍。

都说它比钢硬两百倍，导电导热全世界第一，厚度只有一个原子。专家说它能改变一切，结果二十年过去了，它改变的主要是保暖内衣的价格。你去商场看看，石墨烯内裤、石墨烯护膝、石墨烯暖宝宝。我就纳闷了，一个原子那么厚的东西，到底是怎么做成秋裤的？那条秋裤里，它可能就是吊牌上那几个字。

最惨的是做芯片。它导电太好了，好到关不上。你想想，一个开关，开着是开，关着还是开，那它不叫开关，叫“开”。

所以石墨烯就是那种学霸：门门满分，就是毕不了业。最后只好去卖秋裤。

石墨烯，就是一层碳原子，比钢强两百倍，导电导热都是顶级。怎么发现的？2004年，两个科学家拿透明胶带粘铅笔芯，粘一下撕开，再粘再撕，撕到只剩一层原子，拿了诺贝尔奖。我小学也这么干过，铅笔涂黑一整页，拿胶带粘，我妈奖励我的不是诺贝尔奖，是衣架。

它当年号称要取代硅做芯片，结果没有带隙，电流关不掉。一个开关，关不上，那叫什么？那叫我家楼道灯。

二十年过去了，它进了哪儿？石墨烯内裤，石墨烯暖宫贴。人类最强材料，最后贴在我二姨肚子上。比钢强两百倍，扛不住我二姨一句：“这个会发热，给你也买一条。”

Carbon nanotubes, everybody! The strongest material known to science, and you still can't hold a job. Since the nineties you've promised us a space elevator. Your longest strand is about half a meter. That's not an elevator. That's floss with a publicist.

You're graphene that rolled over and gave up. Graphene got a Nobel Prize. You got an argument over whether Soviets spotted you in 1952.

You can't even decide what you are. Twist one way, you're a metal. Twist the other, you're a semiconductor. Nobody controls it, including you. That's not versatility. That's a chirality crisis.

Drop you in any liquid and you clump together like freshmen at a mixer.

And inhale you? Suddenly you behave like asbestos. Thirty years of hype, and your most reliable talent is impersonating the one material we paid billions to rip out of schools.

碳纳米管，号称人类最强材料，强度是钢的一百倍。科学家说：拿它造太空电梯，直通三万六千公里。好，现在最长做到多少？半米。三十年了，太空电梯修到你家门槛。

它还特别娇气。说白了就是一张石墨烯卷成管子，可你卷的角度歪一点点，它就从导体变成半导体。一锅出来三分之一是金属的、三分之二是半导体的，混在一起还分不开。这哪是材料，这是抽盲盒！

最绝的是，它长得跟石棉差不多，又细又长，吸进肺里赶不出来。科学家忙活半天，终于搞出一种比钢硬一百倍、比盲盒还随机、还能顺便让你得尘肺的东西。人类的未来，就靠它了。

碳纳米管，说白了就是一张石墨烯卷成了个筒。你品品，一张纸，卷一下，强度直接是钢的一百倍。我上学的时候也卷过卷子，卷完挨打的是我。

更离谱的是，它导不导电，得看它当初怎么卷的。卷得端端正正，是金属；稍微卷歪一点，变半导体了。这哪是材料，这是星座啊！同一块碳，就因为出生角度不一样，性格完全两样。

科学家说，用它能造太空电梯，从地面直通太空。三十多年过去了，造出来最长的一根，半米左右。电梯没修上去，倒是先发现它吸进肺里跟石棉有点像。

好家伙，强度像钢，性格看星座，进度像我减肥，副作用像装修。

Apple Vision Pro, everybody! Thirty-five hundred dollars to look like a scuba diver lost in a Best Buy. Apple insists it's not VR, it's "spatial computing," which is like calling a fanny pack "hip luggage." It's so heavy they had to throw in a second strap, and the battery's a separate brick on a cord, so you're basically a lamp that walks. Two hours of charge! That's not a computer, that's a matinee. Then there's EyeSight, the screen that shows your eyes on the front, so your family can watch a dim, blurry you stare at nothing. Most honest feature Apple's ever made. Netflix wouldn't even make an app. Netflix! They're on smart fridges! And your Persona looks like a hostage video filmed inside the uncanny valley.

Carbon nanotubes, everybody! The only material that's been "five years away" since 1991. You're a hundred times stronger than steel, and you've used that strength to hold together... a tennis racket. They promised us a space elevator; you can't get past a few centimeters without a defect. That's not a cable, that's a toothpick with a press agent.

You're basically graphene that rolled itself up out of insecurity, and graphene still got the Nobel. Your cousin the buckyball got one too. You got a shoutout in a bike-frame brochure.

You can't even decide if you're a metal or a semiconductor; it depends on the angle you got rolled at. You clump together like nerds at a mixer, and the second you escape, you lodge in lungs like asbestos. Strongest thing on Earth, and your best trick is ending up in a safety data sheet.

Apple Vision Pro, you cost $3,499 and still need a battery on a cord like a 1996 Walkman. Two hours of charge? That's not spatial computing, that's a matinee. Wear glasses? Zeiss inserts, extra. Apple saw you squinting and smelled revenue.

And EyeSight! A front screen showing your eyes so people feel connected. Nothing says "I'm present" like blurry cartoon eyeballs trapped behind ski-goggle glass. Your Persona avatar looks like a hostage video directed by a ghost.

You promised the future, and Netflix wouldn't even make you an app. You strap over a pound to dads' faces so they can record "spatial memories" of birthdays they watched through a screen.

Apple said you'd never see the world the same way. True. Now it's through a $3,500 face fridge.

我朋友花两万九买了个Apple Vision Pro，戴上就喊："我看到了未来！"我说你看到的是你家客厅，透视的，还有点糊。

这玩意儿六百多克压在脸上，摘下来鼻梁两道红印，像刚被苹果审讯过。屁股后面还拖根线连个电池揣兜里，跟输液似的，俩小时准没电。

最绝的是前面那块屏，叫EyeSight，专门给别人显示你的眼睛。你品品：先花钱把眼睛挡住，再花钱在外面画一双眼睛。这不是科技，这是门神！

他还用它拍"空间视频"，录他女儿吹蜡烛。孩子抬头一看：一副滑雪镜对着她，上面还浮着一双假眼。那天她许的愿是：爸爸，把脸还给我。

Google Glass, look at you. Fifteen hundred dollars to wear a sugar cube on your eyebrow. Sergey Brin had skydivers jump onto a building to launch you, and that was the last time anything about you was cool.

You invented a whole new insult. Nobody calls iPhone owners "Phoneholes." But "Glasshole"? Earned. Fast. Because you let people take photos by *winking*. You turned flirting into a privacy violation.

Every sentence started with "OK Glass," like a man narrating his own midlife crisis out loud. Bars banned you. Strangers ripped you off people's faces. Your battery died faster than your reputation, and you overheated right next to the user's brain, which honestly explains the buying decision.

Then you pivoted to "Enterprise," the tech version of moving back home to work at your uncle's warehouse.

And even the warehouse let you go.

谷歌眼镜，2013年的产品，1500美元，买回来你得到什么？右眼斜上方一块小棱镜。所以全世界戴谷歌眼镜的人都有同一个动作：眼珠子往右上角翻。跟你聊着天，突然翻白眼，你以为他嫌你烦，其实他在看邮件。

开机还得喊口令："OK Glass。"在地铁上，一个大哥对着空气喊"OK Glass"，旁边人默默往后退了三步，这不是科技，这是驱魔。

它还能眨眼拍照。你想想，一个人对你使了个眼色，你以为他在撩你，结果"咔嚓"，你上云了。所以美国酒吧门口直接贴告示：禁止戴谷歌眼镜入内。连名字都给你起好了，Glasshole。

发布会上谷歌让人戴着它跳伞，从天上直播落到会场。真厉害，问题是我们普通人戴着它，从客厅走到厨房，电池没了，太阳穴还烫得跟贴了个暖宝宝似的。

最后谷歌自己也想通了，把它卖给了工厂。对，这玩意儿终于找到了归宿：在一个没人能骂你Glasshole的地方，翻着白眼拧螺丝。

谷歌眼镜，2013年卖一千五百美元。一千五百美元，买一块小玻璃挂在你右眼斜上方。你想看条消息，得翻白眼往右上角瞄，跟你说话的人还以为你在想“这人怎么还没走”。

开机口令是什么？“OK Glass”。你在地铁里突然对着空气说“OK Glass”，全车厢都给你让座，不是尊重，是害怕。

最绝的是拍照：眨一下眼就能拍。眨眼拍照！你跟姑娘眨个眼，人家不知道你是暧昧还是取证。后来美国好多酒吧门口直接贴告示“禁止佩戴谷歌眼镜”，连脾气最好的酒吧都容不下你。

还给戴它的人发明了个专门的词，叫“Glasshole”。一个产品，没火之前先给它的用户造出个脏话。谷歌这辈子最成功的社交功能，就是让所有人都团结起来，一起讨厌你。

我买了个Apple Vision Pro，两万九千九。戴上第一感觉：脸上压了块砖。哦不对，砖在兜里。它电池是外接的，一根线连着脑袋，续航两小时。两万九，买了个带脐带的头盔，我不像在体验未来科技，像在医院输液。

最离谱的是前面那块屏，叫EyeSight，把我的眼睛投到外面给别人看，说是为了“保持人与人的连接”。我妈第一次见，退了三步：“儿子，你眼睛怎么长玻璃里去了？”我说妈，这是科技。她说科技我懂，科技不会让你看着像被关在鱼缸里。

开视频会议更惨，它给你生成个数字分身Persona。同事看完说：“你今天气色挺好，就是有点像蜡像馆刚下班。”

Google Glass, you cost fifteen hundred dollars and made everyone wearing you look like a Bluetooth headset that got promoted. Sergey Brin launched you by skydiving onto a building, and that's the last time you were ever cool. You put a tiny prism over one eye so people could check email while pretending to make eye contact. You didn't invent a computer, you invented a reason to get punched. You're the only gadget that gave us a new slur: "Glasshole." Bars banned you. Movie theaters banned you. Robert Scoble wore you in the shower, and that photo did more damage than any privacy lawsuit. You took pictures when people winked, turning every awkward conversation into a potential felony. Your battery died before your reputation did, and that's impressive. Rest in peace: demoted to warehouse work, then quietly killed in 2023. The most Google ending possible.

Nuclear fusion, everybody! The only energy source that's been thirty years away for seventy years. You're not the future, you're a toddler promising to clean his room after the next funding cycle.

You heat plasma to 150 million degrees, ten times hotter than the core of the sun, and still can't do what the sun does for free while being a ball of gas with no PhD.

ITER started at five billion euros. It's now north of twenty, and it hasn't produced a watt. That's not a reactor, that's a French timeshare.

In 2022 you finally got "net energy gain" by ignoring the 300 megajoules the lasers pulled from the wall. That's like saying your restaurant's profitable if you don't count rent.

And your solution to fuel shortages is mining helium-3 on the moon. Buddy, you can't even make it to Tuesday.

Nuclear fusion, everybody! The only technology that's been thirty years away for seventy years. You're not an energy source, you're a timeshare pitch.

The sun does you effortlessly. It just sits there being enormous. You need a giant metal donut called a tokamak, magnets colder than deep space, and plasma hotter than the sun's core, and that plasma still escapes like it's late for a better party.

In 2022 you finally got more energy out than you put in! From the lasers. Ignoring the grid power feeding the lasers. That's like bragging you turned a profit because the cashier handed you change.

ITER started at five billion euros, now sits somewhere north of twenty, and keeps sliding its startup date. And your fuel needs tritium, which barely exists, so you'll have to breed it yourself.

Fusion: clean, safe, limitless, and tragically hypothetical.

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars: the only vehicle where the tailpipe emission is water and the owners are still crying more than the car. The Toyota Mirai loses value faster than a Hindenburg loses altitude. Used ones sell for less than the free fuel card Toyota bundled with them, a card you can't use because the station's been "temporarily offline" since 2022.

You've got a 10,000-PSI tank of the universe's most abundant element, and somehow it's the scarcest thing in California. Filling up costs thirty-six bucks a kilo, and most of that hydrogen is made from natural gas, so congratulations: you bought a gas car with extra steps and a guilt-free bumper sticker.

Hydrogen's been "ten years away" for thirty years. Even fusion's embarrassed for you, and fusion is the same element with better excuses.

Hydrogen fuel-cell cars: the only vehicle powered by the most abundant element in the universe that still can't find a gas station. California has about fifty pumps, and half of them are "temporarily offline," which is hydrogen for "go home." Its one emission is water, so it's technically the cleanest car on Earth, as long as you don't ask where the hydrogen came from. Spoiler: natural gas. It's a fossil fuel car in a witness protection program. Toyota gave Mirai buyers fifteen grand in free fuel, which sounds generous until you realize that at thirty-six bucks a kilo it covers roughly a year of driving, and the car loses that much value on the drive home. You're sitting on a tank pressurized to 10,000 psi to go three hundred miles. Even the Hindenburg would say, "Maybe just get a Tesla."

可控核聚变，我从小听到大，永远是“再过三十年就能用”。我爸小时候听是三十年，我现在听还是三十年。这不是能源，这是个永动的倒计时。

难在哪？要把等离子体烧到一亿度，比太阳核心还热好几倍。为啥？因为太阳有巨大的引力压着，我们没有，只能拿温度硬凑。太阳躺着就聚变了，我们得拼命，这就是有背景和没背景的区别。

烧完了还不能让它碰墙，得用磁场悬空兜着。一亿度，不能碰，不能放，还得哄着别乱跑，这哪是发电，这是伺候祖宗。

最气人的是名字：“可控”。不可控的我们早会了，叫氢弹。七十年了，人类的进展就是从“一下全炸出来”，努力到了“一点都放不出来”。

可控核聚变很神奇，它永远在“三十年后实现”。我爷爷听说是三十年后，我爸听说是三十年后，轮到我，还是三十年后。这不是科研进度，这是地平线，你往前走，它往后退。

难在哪？得把等离子体烧到一亿度，比太阳核心还热好几倍。太阳不用这么热，人家靠自己的引力压着。我们没那个体重，只能拿磁场把一团一亿度的火悬在半空，还不能碰墙。相当于你想煮碗面，得先造个太阳，再发明一口碰不到面的锅。

最气人的是发布会：“我们实现了能量净增益！”一看，不算给激光供电那部分。这就好比我说我减肥成功了，不算吃饭那几顿。

我朋友买了辆氢燃料电池车，天天跟我炫：“我这车排出来的只有水！”我说那挺好，渴了还能接着喝。他说不行，排气管滴下来那点水，还不够给车标洗个脸。

他最得意的是加氢只要五分钟。没错，五分钟，前提是你先开一百公里，找到全市唯一那座加氢站。到了一看，前面就排了一辆车，站长出来说：“稍等啊，刚加完一辆，储罐得重新压一下，压到七百个大气压，四十分钟。”

七百个大气压！他后备箱里装的哪是油箱，是一颗随时准备发射的鱼雷。

最绝的是，他说这车零排放。我问那氢是哪来的，他支支吾吾半天：“……天然气做的。”

兄弟，你这不叫新能源，你是开着一台绕了三道弯的燃气灶。

氢燃料电池车，号称尾气只排水。真的，开一路，排气管滴滴答答。我第一次见还以为它憋不住了，赶紧给它找厕所。

找什么厕所，先找加氢站吧。全国加氢站加起来，还没我家楼下奶茶店多。导航一搜，最近的在三百公里外。满箱能跑六百，正好，开过去加满，回来，再去加一趟。

到了站，人家说今天氢没到货。氢！宇宙里最多的元素！它缺货！

加的时候七百个大气压，工作人员让我站远点。我说加个油至于吗？他说你加的不是油，是七百倍的脾气。

专家说氢能是未来，十年后普及。这话他们九十年代就在说。跟氢气一个德行：分子太小，怎么都留不住。

Esperanto. In 1887, Dr. Zamenhof, an eye doctor, looked at a world divided by language and decided what it really needed was six letters wearing tiny hats. Nothing says "universal" like ĉ, ĝ, and ŭ, characters no keyboard on Earth can type, so your fans write "cx" and pretend that's fine.

Your name literally means "one who hopes." A hundred and thirty years later: still hoping.

You're the only language where "bad" is just "un-good." *Malbona.* That's not grammar, that's Orwell's Newspeak with a beard. Every noun ends in -o, so you sound like Italian being sight-read by a robot.

You promised world peace and delivered a convention full of men wearing green star pins. Your biggest movie stars William Shatner. And you have about a thousand native speakers, which isn't a language community. It's a cul-de-sac.

Esperanto: the universal language invented in 1887 by a Polish eye doctor who decided humanity needed Italian with a Slavic accent. Universal, as long as your universe is Europe.

The name means "one who hopes." Over a century later: still hoping. There are roughly a thousand native speakers. Klingon is closing in, and Klingon has an army.

It's so logical that "bad" is "malbona," literally un-good. Orwell called; he wants royalties.

Every noun ends in -o and every adjective in -a, so every sentence sounds like a waiter reciting the specials. And it gave us ĉ, ĝ, ŝ and ŭ: letters with little hats, designed for global communication, then made untypeable on every keyboard on Earth.

Its biggest movie starred William Shatner. Even he couldn't oversell it.

我最近在学世界语。1887年一个波兰眼科医生发明的，目标是让全人类说同一种语言。一百多年过去了，母语是世界语的大概一千来人，还没我们小区业主群人多。

但它语法是真规整。名词全以o结尾，形容词全以a结尾，没有例外。我学了一周，感觉不是在学语言，是在填表。

最绝的是前缀mal，加上就变反义词。好是bona，坏就是malbona，“不好”。大是granda，小是malgranda，“不大”。连个“坏”字都懒得发明。你跟世界语者吵架，最狠只能骂一句：“你真是个不好人！”

还说国际通用呢，字母头上戴小帽子，ĉ、ŝ、ĝ，我键盘一个都打不出来。全世界通用，就是不包括我的电脑。

Klingon, you're the only language whose native speakers are all fictional and whose fluent speakers all have a Comic-Con badge. Marc Okrand built you in 1984 to sound alien, and he nailed it: you sound like a man choking on a pretzel while reading IKEA instructions.

Your word order is object-verb-subject, so every sentence is a mystery that reveals who did it at the end. Your greeting, nuqneH, literally means "What do you want?" Congratulations: you're the first language designed by a DMV clerk.

You have more apostrophes than vowels deserve, no verb "to be," and a Klingon Language Institute that "restored" Hamlet to its original Klingon. That's not scholarship. That's fan fiction with footnotes.

A linguist once tried raising his son in Klingon. By age five the kid stopped answering. Qapla'!

世界语，1887年发明的，目标是让全人类说同一种语言。一百多年过去，全人类确实说上了同一种语言：英语。

它号称最好学：名词全以o结尾，形容词全以a结尾。直到你发现它懒到连反义词都不造。"好"是bona，"坏"是malbona，"不好"。"大"是granda，"小"是malgranda，"不大"。医院叫malsanulejo，直译是"不健康的人待的地方"。这不是语言，这是程序员在复制粘贴。

它还说自己中立，不偏向任何民族。可单词全是拉丁语、德语、斯拉夫语来的，字母头上还戴小帽子，ĉ、ĝ、ŝ。这种中立，就像欧洲人请你吃饭，说"随便坐"，一看桌上全是刀叉。

Klingon, you're a language built by one linguist, Marc Okrand, specifically to sound alien and hostile, and somehow you still ended up sounding like a man choking on a Dorito. Your word order is object-verb-subject, so even your sentences walk in backwards to hide their face. You don't even have a word for "hello." Your greeting is "nuqneH," "what do you want?" You're the only language that greets people like a DMV clerk. Your apostrophes are glottal stops, your capital Q is a different letter from lowercase q, and "tlh" isn't a sound, it's a hairball. You translated Hamlet and claimed it was the original. Buddy, the most popular thing ever said in you is "Qapla'," and the people saying it are at a Marriott in Burbank.

Comic Sans, you were modeled on Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns. You come from Batman. Your one job was speech bubbles for a cartoon dog, and you missed it. Microsoft Bob, a product nobody remembers, and you couldn't make his launch. Cut from the dog's team, you shipped in a Plus! pack, like a free tote bag nobody asked for.

Then CERN found the Higgs boson, the particle that gives everything mass, and announced it in you. The biggest physics discovery in decades, presented like a lost-cat flyer. You're the one thing that particle couldn't give weight to.

Two designers spent twenty years trying to ban you. In 2019 they gave up and built you a website. That's not acceptance, Comic Sans. That's a hostage situation.

Comic Sans! Born at Microsoft in 1994, modeled on Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns, the two grimmest comics ever printed, and somehow you came out looking like a bake-sale flyer. Batman was your inspiration, and you turned out to be the Joker.

You had one job: speech bubbles for Rover, the cartoon dog in Microsoft Bob. And you missed it. You were late to work for a cartoon dog. They had to stick you in the Windows 95 Plus! pack like a gift-shop keychain.

Then CERN announces the Higgs boson, humanity's greatest discovery, and the slides are in you. Physicists cracked the universe and everyone asked, "Why's it in the birthday-party font?"

People campaigned to ban you for twenty years. Then Dave and Holly Combs gave up and launched usecomicsans.com. You didn't win the argument. You just outlasted it.

我最近在学克林贡语，就是《星际迷航》里外星战士民族说的那个语言。学了才知道，这语言打招呼不说"你好"，说"nuqneH"，意思是"你想干嘛？"我拿去跟楼下大爷练，大爷说："我想报警。"

它的语序是宾语、动词、主语。"我爱你"要说成"你，爱，我"。你跟对象表白，说到一半对方已经觉得你在推卸责任了。

最狠的是它没有"请"，也没有"谢谢"。有人说那太没礼貌了吧？不，人家的礼貌是另一种：给你一句"今天是个适合去死的好日子"。这是祝福语！你想想，生日蛋糕端上来，全家举杯："今天适合去死！"寿星当场决定再活二十年，就是为了赌气。

还有一帮人，把《哈姆雷特》翻译成了克林贡语，封面上写着："恢复为原始克林贡语版本"。意思是莎士比亚是盗版，人家才是原著。我服了，一个连"谢谢"都不会说的民族，被抄袭了，倒是第一个发现的。

我最近在学克林贡语，发现这语言的设计理念就是：别跟我客气。它没有"你好"。见面说"nuqneH"，直译是"你想要啥？"这不是问候，这是小区保安。也没有"请"和"谢谢"。它语序还是宾语-动词-主语，你去克林贡饭馆点菜只能说："肉，拿来，我。"主语永远最后才到，跟我们领导开会一样。最离谱的是他们把《哈姆雷特》翻成克林贡语，还坚称克林贡语才是原版。那"To be or not to be"怎么翻？克林贡语里压根没有"是"这个动词。一个战士民族，连"存在"都懒得说，直接跳到"今天是赴死的好日子"。人家不纠结生死，人家直接排期。

Comic Sans 这字体，出身就很惨。1994 年微软做出来，本来是给一只卡通狗用的：Microsoft Bob 里那条叫 Rover 的狗，专门给它配对话气泡。结果没赶上，狗都没用上它！最后只能塞进 Windows 95 的 Plus! 扩展包出道。

可它偏偏就混出来了。2012 年，CERN 宣布发现希格斯玻色子。人类离宇宙真相最近的一刻，幻灯片用的是 Comic Sans。物理学巅峰，排版像儿童节手抄报。

还有一对设计师夫妇，1999 年发起“禁用 Comic Sans”运动，坚持了整整二十年。2019 年，宣布：算了，你们用吧。还顺手开了个网站叫 usecomicsans.com。二十年啊朋友们，这不叫和解，这叫被一个字体熬死了。

Comic Sans这字体，你们知道它是干嘛生的吗？1994年微软做的，专门给一只狗说话用的：微软Bob里那只卡通狗Rover。结果它连Bob都没赶上，被塞进了Windows 95的Plus!包。一个字体，出生就失业。

失业了它也没闲着，到处乱跑。2012年，CERN宣布发现希格斯玻色子，人类物理学的高光时刻，幻灯片用的是Comic Sans。宇宙最深的秘密，是用一只狗的嗓音念出来的。

1999年，有两个设计师发起“禁用Comic Sans”运动，一坚持就是二十年。2019年，他们收手了，还开了个网站叫usecomicsans.com。跟一个字体打了二十年，最后投降了！

那只狗一天班都没上，它的字体倒是赢了。

Papyrus, you were hand-drawn over six months by a 23-year-old, and it shows. Six months! Chris Costello spent half a year on you, then sold you for $750. That's not a sale, that's a man paying someone to take a problem off his hands.

Then Apple and Microsoft bundled you, which is how you ended up on every menu and sign like a raccoon that learned to read. You look like Times New Roman got lost in the desert and came back spiritual.

James Cameron built an entire alien world for Avatar, then picked you for the logo and subtitles. Every frame was a masterpiece; the title took one click.

And SNL made a whole sketch about Ryan Gosling being unable to get over it. Papyrus, you're not a typeface. You're trauma with rough edges.

Papyrus, you were hand-drawn over six months by a 23-year-old, and somehow it still looks like a first draft. Six months! You look like you were chiseled during an earthquake. Chris Costello sold you to Letraset for $750, the only time anyone has known exactly what you're worth.

You came bundled with macOS and Microsoft Office, so you're not popular, you're just pre-installed. You're the free hotel shampoo of fonts. Every menu, every sign: you didn't earn that, you just came with the computer.

Then James Cameron imagined an entire alien world for Avatar, and when it came time for the logo and subtitles, he picked the default. Of all the things to leave untouched.

It got so bad that Saturday Night Live had Ryan Gosling play a man who can't get over it. You're not a typeface. You're a trauma with jagged edges.

PHP, you started life as a visitor counter for one guy's résumé page. Now you power 39.4% of all websites, which means the internet is basically a guestbook that got out of hand.

Your own creator said, "I'm not a real programmer. I throw together things until it works then I move on." And he did move on. The rest of us are still here, maintaining it.

Your function names were chosen to balance a hash table by string length. strpos. str_replace. htmlspecialchars. nl2br. That's not a naming convention, that's a ransom note.

Until 2020, zero equaled "foo." You looked at a word and saw nothing. Then again, you looked at "Personal Home Page" and saw "PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor," a name whose only definition is itself.

Which is fitting, because the only thing that can explain PHP is more PHP.

PHP started in 1994 as "Personal Home Page Tools," a bunch of C programs to count visitors to Rasmus Lerdorf's résumé. So from day one, its whole purpose was checking whether anyone cared. Now the name stands for "PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor," a recursive acronym, because even the name couldn't commit to a plan.

Its creator once said, "I'm not a real programmer. I throw together things until it works then I move on." That's not a quote; that's a confession with a version number.

The function names? strpos, str_replace, htmlspecialchars, nl2br. Chosen partly to balance a hash table by string length. Other languages name functions for humans. PHP named them for the furniture.

And until 2020, 0 == 'foo' was true. PHP looked at the word "foo" and said, "Close enough, that's nothing."

It runs WordPress, on 39.4% of all websites. The internet is held together by a résumé counter.

你们知道Papyrus字体吗？就是那种像古埃及人喝多了刻在石头上的字。1982年，23岁的Chris Costello手绘了整整六个月，卖给Letraset，七百五十美元。六个月七百五，按月算比我还惨。后来它被塞进每台Mac、每套Office，于是全世界自称"有灵性"的菜单和招牌，全是它。最离谱的是卡梅隆，拍《阿凡达》，造了一整个外星球，结果标志和字幕用的是电脑自带的字体。就像你盖了座宫殿，门牌拿记号笔写。难怪2017年SNL让高斯林演一个被这事折磨得走不出来的人。兄弟，我懂。我每次看到餐馆菜单，都想去敲卡梅隆家的门。

你们知道Papyrus这个字体吗？就是那种看着像古埃及人拿沙子写出来的字。这字是一个叫Chris Costello的哥们，1982年，23岁，手画了整整半年画出来的。然后卖给了Letraset，多少钱？750美元。半年，750，一天合四块钱。这字体寒碜，它的身价更寒碜。

后来苹果和微软把它塞进了系统自带，好了，全世界每个觉得自己“有点格调”的老板都找到了它。菜单是它，招牌也是它。

最狠的是卡梅隆。拍《阿凡达》，砸了那么多钱，造了一整个外星球，到写片名那一步：“就用电脑自带的那个吧。”

难怪2017年SNL让瑞恩·高斯林演了个男的，为这事儿怎么都过不去。哥们，我懂你。你不是一个人。

PHP的出身就很随便。1994年，Rasmus Lerdorf写了几个C程序，就为了看看谁访问了他的简历页面。全球最流行的网站语言之一，起点是一个人在偷看谁看了他的简历。

后来名字改成“PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor”。PHP里的P就是PHP，连自我介绍都是死循环。

作者亲口说：“我不是真正的程序员，我就是瞎拼，能跑了就走。”大哥，你是走了，我们还在这儿修呢！

函数名为啥那么乱？早期起名要平衡哈希表，按名字长度分桶。别的语言起名看意思，PHP起名数字数，跟凑对联似的。

PHP 8之前，0 == 'foo'居然是真的。这哪是编程语言，这是相亲中介：“差不多就行，凑合过吧。”

就这么个东西，靠WordPress撑着全网近四成的网站。

PHP的出身很朴素：1994年，Rasmus Lerdorf写了几个C程序，就为了看看谁访问了他的简历页面。结果一个求职小工具，撑起了WordPress，跑在39.4%的网站上。你们公司官网，大概率是一份简历的后代。

作者本人怎么说？“我不是真正的程序员。我就是拼凑到能跑，然后就走了。”兄弟，这不是编程哲学，这是退租哲学。

函数名更随性：strpos不加下划线，str_replace加，htmlspecialchars一口气不换气。为什么？早期起名要按字符串长度平衡哈希表。别的语言起名看意思，PHP起名凑字数，跟写七言绝句似的。

最狠的是，PHP 8之前，0 == 'foo'是true。“foo”被悄悄转成数字，变成了零。在PHP眼里，你说什么，都等于没说。

JavaScript, give it up! Built in ten days in 1995, and honestly, it shows. Most of us take longer to name a dog. And you needed three tries: Mocha, LiveScript, then "JavaScript," named after Java purely for the marketing. That's not branding, that's wearing someone else's name tag. You can't even legally use it. Oracle owns it, so on paper you're "ECMAScript," which sounds like a skin condition.

typeof null is "object." A bug from your first version, and you kept it. For compatibility. That's not a quirk, that's a tattoo of your ex's name.

[] + {} is "," but type {} + [] at the console and it's zero. Even your addition has mood swings.

And in 2016, the author of left-pad unpublished eleven lines and took down Babel and React. Eleven lines! Your whole ecosystem is a Jenga tower standing on a toothpick.

JavaScript, you were built in ten days in 1995, and it shows. You went from Mocha to LiveScript to JavaScript faster than someone in witness protection, and you grabbed "Java" for clout. You're not related. You're the guy at the wedding claiming to be the groom's cousin.

You can't even use that name legally. Oracle owns it. Your government name is ECMAScript, which sounds like a skin condition.

You think null is an object. That's a bug from day one, and you kept it for "compatibility." That's not compatibility, that's refusing to go to therapy.

[] plus {} is "." Type {} plus [] at a console: zero. Same ingredients, different answer. You're not a language, you're a mood.

In 2016, one guy unpublished eleven lines called left-pad and took down Babel and React. Eleven lines. Your whole ecosystem is a Jenga tower balanced on a Post-it.

text:
JavaScript，1995年写的，用了十天。十天！我装修个厕所都不止十天，结果全世界的网页都住在这厕所里。

名字先叫Mocha，又叫LiveScript，最后改叫JavaScript，跟Java毫无关系，纯蹭热度。蹭完了商标还归Oracle，官方标准只能叫ECMAScript。自己的名字，自己不能用。

你问它null是什么类型，它说object。错了吧？错了。改吗？不改，为了兼容。这不叫bug，这叫祖传手艺。

2016年有人删了个叫left-pad的包，就十一行代码，Babel、React全崩了。十一行撑着半个互联网，这不叫生态，这叫叠罗汉。

JavaScript是Brendan Eich在网景花十天写出来的。十天！我装修个卫生间都不止十天，结果全世界的网页都跑在它上面。

它先叫Mocha，又叫LiveScript，最后叫JavaScript，跟Java毫无关系，纯蹭热度。名字还不归自己，商标先是Sun的，现在是Oracle的，官方只能叫ECMAScript。连真名都得用化名，跟卧底似的。

你问它null是什么类型，它说object。第一版的bug，为了兼容一直不改，错得理直气壮。

数组加对象，得“”；对象加数组，控制台里得0。小学数学老师看了要报警。

2016年有人删了个11行的包，叫left-pad，Babel、React构建全挂了。11行！比我的购物清单还短，它一走，整个行业停电。

text:
PMMA, you're literally Plexiglas. Sneeze-guard material, dissolved in anisole and spun thin so you could pretend to be high-tech. IBM researchers reported you as an e-beam resist in the late 1960s, and you're still here, like a lab manager nobody can fire.

Sure, you resolve below 10 nm. Impressive. But your sensitivity is so bad it takes hundreds to over a thousand microcoulombs per square centimeter just to get your attention. Writing a pattern on you is so slow that students start the job and finish their thesis.

And your whole personality is falling apart: hit you with a beam and your chains snap, then you dissolve in MIBK and IPA. Dry etch? You fold instantly. Nobody trusts you as an etch mask. Your only job is lift-off: show up, hold the metal for a minute, then leave.

PMMA, you're the same polymer as Plexiglas. Somewhere a hamster cage is living your life, and nobody had to dissolve it in chlorobenzene first.

IBM reported you in the late 1960s, and you're still here, like a professor who won't retire because nobody else is quite as precise. Sub-10 nanometers, very impressive. Too bad getting you there takes hundreds to over a thousand microcoulombs per square centimeter. You don't get exposed, you get interrogated.

You're "positive tone," which is generous, because nothing about writing you feels positive. The beam has to break your chains before you'll let go.

And once you finally hold a pattern? Plasma shows up and you fold. So your career is lift-off: hold the shape, let the metal take the credit, then get washed away.

我们实验室天天伺候的PMMA电子束光刻胶，说穿了就是亚克力，你家鱼缸那玩意儿。人家拿它做有机玻璃，我们用苯甲醚把它泡化了，甩成一层薄膜，当宝贝供着。

它六十年代末就被IBM拿来当电子束胶，到今天还在一线干活。这不叫元老，这叫延迟退休。

分辨率是真好，十纳米以下。可它太迟钝了，几百到上千微库每平方厘米才肯动一下。电子束在上面写，跟拿毛笔在米粒上刻《兰亭序》一样，写完我都该毕业了。

好不容易显影出来，想拿它当刻蚀掩膜？干法刻蚀一来，它比导师的承诺化得还快，只能去做剥离。

细节抠得特别好，一上压力就没了。这哪是光刻胶，这就是我。

HSQ, you were hired as a spin-on dielectric for chip interconnects and wandered into lithography like a temp who got promoted for being weirdly good at one thing. And you are good: 5 nm features, sub-10 nm half-pitch lines. Congratulations, you're the world's sharpest glass. Get hit by electrons, turn into SiO2. Most resists become patterns; you become sand with ambition.

You demand refrigeration, give us six months at 5 °C, and still turn into jelly like forgotten leftovers. You keep cross-linking after exposure, so your sensitivity depends on how long we dawdle. You're a resist with moods. You develop best in "salty" NaOH/NaCl, which tracks. Then DuPont ended your production in 2025, and labs shrugged and bought third-party HSQ made from AQM powder. Resolution record-holder, replaced by your own generic.

PMMA，电子束光刻胶界的老前辈。说白了就是亚克力，商场展示架那玩意儿，溶进苯甲醚里一转，就成了光刻胶。有编制的亚克力。六十年代末IBM就用上了，到今天还天天上班。分辨率能到十纳米以下，可它反应慢啊，剂量要几百甚至上千微库每平方厘米，写一张图，学生从硕士等成博士。它还是正胶：电子一打，链就断，往显影液里一泡，自己溶了。挨了打当场消失，这不是光刻胶，这是我。最惨的是不耐干法刻蚀，让它当掩模，它先没了。所以只能做剥离：垫在底下，金属镀上去，再连它一起洗掉。干了五十多年，岗位叫：用完就扔。

HSQ, you were hired to be an insulator. Dow Corning called you "flowable oxide," a humble spin-on dielectric for chip interconnects, and you ran off to become a lithography celebrity. Sure, you hold the e-beam resolution records: five-nanometer isolated features, dense lines under ten nanometers half-pitch. But you only deliver if someone develops you in NaOH and salt. Even your best work needs to be "salty."

冰岛总统说过，要是能禁他就禁了，然后补了一句：总统没这权力。一国元首，在一块菠萝面前，认怂了。

你以为夏威夷披萨是夏威夷人发明的？不是。1962年，一个希腊移民，在加拿大安大略开餐馆时发明的。希腊人，在加拿大，做意大利的饼，起名叫夏威夷。为啥？因为他用的菠萝罐头就是这个牌子。这就像你炒个菜，照着酱油瓶子起名。更惨的是，夏威夷现在都不怎么产菠萝了，2007年最后一家罐头厂都关了，罐头菠萝主要来自泰国、印尼、菲律宾。所以这块披萨跟夏威夷唯一的关系就是名字，名字还是抄罐头的。冰岛总统说过，能做主他就把它禁了，然后赶紧补一句：总统没这权力。堂堂一国元首，拿一块披萨没办法。

Chicago deep-dish pizza, everybody! Born at Pizzeria Uno in 1943, and to this day three men are fighting over the credit: Ike Sewell, Ric Riccardo, and Rudy Malnati. Normally when three guys point at each other over something that happened in a kitchen, it's for the blame.

You're built upside down: cheese on the bottom, sauce on top, because you bake so long the mozzarella has to hide under the toppings like it's waiting out a tornado. Jon Stewart called you "tomato soup in a bread bowl" and "a casserole." Honestly? Generous. Casseroles get invited to funerals.

But here's the real burn: Chicago doesn't even eat you. GrubHub data had locals ordering other pizza ten to one. Under nine percent of orders, and that's with stuffed pizza padding your numbers. They're home eating tavern-style squares. You're not the city's pizza. You're its brochure.

Chicago deep-dish pizza was born at Pizzeria Uno in 1943, and credit is still disputed among Ike Sewell, Ric Riccardo, and Rudy Malnati. Which is wild, because usually when something's this heavy, everybody's trying to *blame* somebody.

It's built upside down: cheese, then toppings, then crushed tomatoes on top, so the cheese doesn't scorch during the long bake. A pizza that takes so long it needs a sunscreen layer.

Jon Stewart called it "tomato soup in a bread bowl" and "a casserole." He meant it as an insult, but that's the nicest thing anyone's ever said about a casserole.

And the kicker? Chicagoans order non-deep-dish about ten to one. Deep dish and stuffed combined? Under nine percent. The locals are home eating tavern-style squares. Deep dish isn't Chicago's pizza. It's Chicago's souvenir.

芝加哥深盘披萨，1943年诞生在Uno。到底谁发明的？老板、合伙人、厨师，三个人到现在还在抢功劳。抢什么呀？这种东西，正常人是互相甩锅的！

它还是倒着做的：先铺奶酪，再放配料，番茄酱整层盖在最上面。为什么？因为要烤太久，奶酪放上面会焦。一道菜，设计的时候就默认你得饿到天荒地老。

乔恩·斯图尔特说它是“面包碗里的番茄汤”，还说它是“一锅砂锅菜”。我觉得他太客气了。

最狠的是芝加哥人自己。他们平时吃的是切成小方块的薄饼，外卖数据十比一，深盘加夹心连一成都不到。全城人用订单投票：这玩意儿，我们自己不吃。

芝加哥深盘披萨，1943年诞生在Uno披萨店。到底谁发明的？老板、合伙人、厨师，三个人的名字都有人提，到现在也没个定论。一般这种事都是抢功劳。我看这个，像是在甩锅。

做法也离谱：先铺奶酪，再放馅料，最后把番茄碎盖在最上面。整个倒着做。为啥？因为要烤很久，怕奶酪烤糊。兄弟，你都得把披萨倒过来做了，是不是该反思一下烤的时间？

Jon Stewart说它是“面包碗里的番茄汤”，是“砂锅菜”。好多人替它不服气。可你看数据：芝加哥人自己点外卖，别的披萨跟深盘比是十比一。深盘加上夹馅的，连百分之九都不到。平时吃的是薄底、切成小方块的。

这就像你逢人就护着你表哥，过年却从来不叫他来家里吃饭。

Durian, you are the only fruit with a criminal record. Singapore's MRT has a list of banned things and you're on it. Not because you're dangerous, because you're rude. Hotels across Southeast Asia won't let you check in. You're a fruit that has to sleep in the car.

And scientists found out why. A 2017 study in Nature Genetics says you have a duplicated family of genes whose whole job is pumping out sulfur. Duplicated! Evolution looked at you and said, "Needs more."

Yet China buys billions of dollars of you a year, mostly from Thailand. That's not a trade deal. That's a hostage situation with a shipping manifest.

Even Alfred Russel Wallace said you were "worth a voyage to the East." Sure, Alfred. Probably because nobody would let you bring it back.

Durian, look at you. A fruit dressed like a medieval weapon, and somehow the spikes are your most welcoming feature.

You're banned on Singapore's MRT. Public transit has seen everything, and it drew the line at you. Hotels across Southeast Asia won't let you check in. You're the only guest turned away for personal hygiene.

In 2017, scientists sequenced your genome and found you'd duplicated your sulfur genes. You didn't stink by accident. You invested.

And still, China buys billions of dollars of you a year, mostly from Thailand. That's not a fruit trade. That's a hostage negotiation with a receipt.

Even Alfred Russel Wallace called you "a new sensation worth a voyage to the East." Durian, a man had to sail halfway around the planet to meet you, and you still can't get on a train.

Jackfruit, look at you. The largest fruit that grows on a tree, over 40 kilos, and somehow you still can't scrape together enough protein to impress a hamster. One to two grams per hundred! You're dressed up as pulled pork with the nutritional backbone of a lettuce in a Halloween costume. Vegans see you on a menu and think "meat alternative." Their muscles see you and file a missing persons report.

And you don't even go quietly. Cut you open and you bleed sticky white latex, so cooks have to oil their knives and hands like they're prepping for a greased-up wrestling match with produce.

National fruit of Bangladesh, state fruit of Kerala and Tamil Nadu: three titles, zero chill.

And your family? The mulberry family. Cousin to figs and breadfruit. Even your relatives took one look at you and decided to stay smaller.

榴莲，是唯一一种被地铁拉黑的水果。新加坡地铁不让带，东南亚好多酒店也不让进。一个水果，混成了失信人员。

2017年科学家给它测了基因组，发现那股味儿根本不是意外：它有一整组基因复制扩增，专门往外泵硫化物。人家不是偶尔臭，是带编制的臭。

最离谱的是1856年，华莱士说吃榴莲是一种新感觉，“值得专程远航到东方体验”。一百多年后，我们真听进去了：全世界出口的榴莲大部分被中国买走，主要从泰国来，一年几十亿美元。

地铁不让坐，酒店不让住，那它是怎么来的？是我们花钱，当贵宾请回家的。

榴莲这东西，是真有排面。新加坡地铁不让它上，东南亚好多酒店不让它住。一个水果，混成了黑名单常客。

科学家都看不下去了，2017年专门给它测基因组，登在《自然·遗传学》上。结论是：它臭，不是意外，是祖传的。有一组MGL基因，还复制了好几份，专门往外泵含硫的气体。人家不是放坏了才臭，人家出厂设置就是生化武器。

就这么个东西，全世界出口的榴莲大头被咱中国人买走了，主要从泰国进，一年几十亿美元。我们花几十亿美元，进口一个地铁都不让上的水果。

1856年，博物学家华莱士说，吃榴莲是"值得专程航行到东方去体验的新感觉"。对，新感觉。第一次被电也是新感觉。

Jackfruit, look at you. The largest fruit that grows on a tree, over 40 kilos. That's not a fruit, that's a checked bag with a stem.

You're the national fruit of Bangladesh and the state fruit of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Three titles, and you still took a side gig pretending to be pork.

They sell you as vegan "pulled pork" with 1 to 2 grams of protein per 100 grams. You're not a meat substitute, you're a meat costume.

You're so clingy that cooks oil their knives and hands before touching you, because you ooze sticky white latex the second anyone gets close. That's not a fruit, that's an ex.

And you're in the mulberry family. Related to figs. Forty kilos, and your cousin is a fig. Somebody's hogging the protein at those reunions, and it sure isn't you.

菠萝蜜，树上长的最大的水果，一个能超过四十公斤。四十公斤！这不是水果，这是树上挂着个初中生。你在它底下乘凉，那不叫乘凉，叫赌命。

想吃它？先给刀抹油，再给手抹油。因为一刀下去，它冒白色的胶。别的水果是你吃它，菠萝蜜是它先粘住你。

现在素食圈还拿没熟的菠萝蜜冒充手撕猪肉。长得是挺像，一百克才一到两克蛋白质。兄弟，你这不叫素肉，叫肉的Cosplay。

它还是桑科的，跟无花果是亲戚。人家无花果小小一个，它四十公斤，家族聚餐它一个人坐一桌。

结果孟加拉选它当国果。也对，这块头，这胶，是该供着，谁敢吃啊。

Luosifen. Everybody blames the river snails, but the snails just flavour the broth and keep their heads down. The real stench is pickled bamboo shoots. You're a noodle that framed a snail.

Then in 2020, with the whole country locked indoors, you sold over 10 billion yuan in instant packs. That's not a boom, that's a hostage situation. Millions sealed in their apartments, and you said, "Perfect. Nobody can leave."

In 2021 you became national *intangible* cultural heritage. Intangible? You're the most tangible thing in any building. People can touch you from the hallway.

And Liuzhou opened an entire industry college for you. A full college education to learn what every roommate figures out in four seconds: breathe through your mouth.

菠萝蜜，树上长的最大的水果，一个能超过四十公斤。这不是水果，这是托付。你在树下乘凉，它掉下来，那不叫收获，叫因果。

它是孟加拉国的国果，还是喀拉拉邦、泰米尔纳德邦的邦果。一个水果占三个编制，混得比我好。

切它之前，得先给刀和手抹油，因为它会流白色的胶。你不是在切水果，你是在拆一个不想被拆的快递。

素食圈拿青菠萝蜜冒充手撕猪肉，口感是像了，每一百克蛋白质一到两克。这不叫替代品，这叫猪肉的cosplay。

它还是桑科的，跟无花果是亲戚。无花果那么小一个，家里出了个四十公斤的，过年都不敢一桌吃饭。

Luosifen, you're named after river snails, and the snails aren't even the problem. They just flavour the broth and take the blame, like the quiet kid sitting next to the one who set off the fire alarm. The real culprit is the pickled bamboo shoots. You've got a smell so loud it needed a decoy.

And your big break? 2020. Everyone locked indoors, windows shut, nowhere to run, and that's when you sold over 10 billion yuan in packets. You didn't go viral; you went airborne.

Then Liuzhou opened a whole industry college to train people to make you. Most dishes need a recipe. You need a degree and, presumably, a waiver.

In 2021 you became national intangible cultural heritage. Intangible. Sure. Anyone who's opened a packet in an office knows you are extremely tangible.

螺蛳粉最冤的是螺蛳。整碗臭成那样，罪魁祸首是酸笋，螺蛳就在汤里泡了个澡，名字却挂它头上。这就像室友在宿舍偷吃，宿管来了，记的是你的名字。

2020年大家关在家里，柳州一年卖出去一百多亿的袋装螺蛳粉。封城没把我逼疯，邻居的螺蛳粉差点做到了。他是关在家里吃，我是关在家里闻。

2021年它还进了国家级非物质文化遗产。“非物质”这词选得太准了，它最主要的部分本来就不是物质，是气体。

柳州还专门开了个螺蛳粉产业学院。我就好奇，毕业那天发的是毕业证，还是防毒面具？

Stinky tofu, look at you. Plain tofu is the most agreeable food on earth, and you turned it into a public nuisance. And the humiliating part? The smell isn't even yours. You soaked in a brine of bamboo shoots and mustard greens that had been fermenting for months, sometimes with dried shrimp. You're not stinky; you just hang out with the wrong crowd.

Your origin story: in 1669 Wang Zhihe, a Qing-era exam candidate, couldn't sell his tofu and left it out too long. You're not a recipe. You're an inventory problem.

Changsha fries you black and buries you in chili. Taiwan hides you under pickled cabbage. Shaoxing steams you with other stinky pickles, like a support group.

Everyone's trying to cover you up, and people still smell you from a block away.

螺蛳粉这东西，最冤的是螺蛳。你一闻那味儿，第一反应：这螺蛳走得不安详啊。其实不是，味儿是酸笋的，螺蛳就负责熬个汤。干活的是酸笋，背锅的是螺蛳，跟上班一模一样。

2020年大家都出不了门，袋装螺蛳粉卖了一百多亿。全国人民关在家里煮这个，邻居跑不了，你也跑不了，这叫同归于尽。

2021年，它进了国家级非遗名录。以前我妈说我屋里像垃圾场，现在我可以理直气壮：妈，这是文化遗产，请你尊重。

柳州还专门开了个螺蛳粉产业学院。我就想知道，毕业答辩那天，导师是先看你论文，还是先闻你衣服？

Stinky tofu, you're the only food that arrives a block before the vendor does. Nobody finds you; they get ambushed.

And the stink isn't even yours. You're plain tofu that sat a day in a months-old swamp of bamboo shoots, mustard greens and dried shrimp, then claimed it as personality. That's not character, that's a marinade.

You've got regional disguises, too. Changsha dyes you black, fries you and buries you in chili like evidence. Taiwan makes you golden and hands out pickled cabbage like an apology. Shaoxing steams you with other stinky pickles, which isn't a dish, it's a support group.

Your origin story? In 1669 Wang Zhihe couldn't sell his tofu and just... left it. Most people call that spoiled inventory. He's still got his name on a Beijing brand.

Oat milk, look at you. Born in a Swedish university lab to help the lactose intolerant, and somehow you turned into a personality. Your slogan was "It's like milk but made for humans." The dairy lobby sued you, and instead of apologizing, you ran the lawsuit as an ad. That's not a brand. That's an ex who frames the restraining order.

Then you hit Nasdaq at nearly ten billion dollars and lost over ninety percent. Even the cows didn't see that coming, and they were *rooting* for it.

And what are you, really? Oats, plus enzymes that chop the starch into maltose, plus a splash of rapeseed oil. You're sugar water with salad-dressing energy. You've got more sugar and a higher glycaemic index than almond or soy. You're not milk made for humans. You're porridge that went to business school and dropped out.

Oat milk. You began in Sweden in the 1990s as sober Lund University research into lactose intolerance, and somehow grew up to be a personality. Your big slogan was "It's like milk but made for humans." The Swedish dairy lobby sued, and instead of apologizing, you published the lawsuit as advertising. That's not a brand. That's a guy who frames his restraining order and hangs it in the hallway.

Then you hit Nasdaq in May 2021 at nearly ten billion dollars and lost over ninety percent of it. Even your share price separated in the fridge.

And the health halo? You're oats that got enzymes to turn their starch into maltose, then got topped off with rapeseed oil. You have more sugar and a higher glycaemic index than almond or soy. You're not milk made for humans. You're porridge with a marketing department.

臭豆腐里最冤的是谁？是豆腐。人家本来清清白白，被扔进一缸卤水里泡上一两天。那缸卤水是笋、芥菜，有时候还加虾米加肉，已经在那儿发酵了好几个月。所以臭的根本不是豆腐，是那缸水！这叫豆腐替卤水背锅。

传说发明人是清朝一个赶考的书生，叫王致和。1669年，豆腐没卖掉，放久了。你听听：进京赶考，副业还亏了，货还放坏了。倒霉到这份上，最后居然成了品牌，北京现在还有个腐乳牌子用他的名字。

这东西主要靠路边摊卖，为什么？人家不需要招牌，隔一条街你就闻到了。长沙炸成黑的，台湾炸成金黄的，颜色随你挑，味道没得商量。

臭豆腐这东西，最冤的是豆腐。那味儿根本不是豆子的，是卤水的！竹笋、芥菜，再扔点虾米，先泡上几个月，自己臭透了，再把豆腐扔进去腌一两天。豆腐干啥了？就进去洗了个澡，出来隔一个街区的人都说它臭。这叫什么？这叫背锅。

各地还各臭各的：长沙的炸成黑的，浇一勺辣椒，臭得理直气壮；台湾夜市的炸得金黄，配泡菜，臭得很有礼貌；绍兴的拿苋菜梗腌，还能跟别的臭腌菜一起蒸，这是臭味全家福。

传说发明人是清朝赶考的王致和，1669年豆腐没卖完，放久了。北京到现在还有个腐乳牌子用他的名字。别人留名靠考中，他留名靠放坏。

燕麦奶的广告语叫"像牛奶，但是给人喝的"。瑞典奶业直接把它告了，2015年这句话被禁。燕麦奶怎么回应？把官司印出来当广告。被人告了不道歉，拿去发传单，这不是品牌，这是小区里吵架上瘾的大姨。

2021年上市，估值将近一百亿美元，后来股价跌了九成多。你看，它确实是给人喝的：给股民喝西北风的。

最绝的是配方：用酶把燕麦淀粉拆成麦芽糖，再兑点菜籽油。糖加油，这叫奶？这叫油条泡糖水。升糖比杏仁奶、豆奶都高。我点燕麦拿铁是为了健康，喝下去，胰岛以为我在逛早餐摊。

燕麦奶的广告语是"像牛奶，但是给人喝的"。2015年在瑞典，被奶业协会告了，禁了。你品品，奶业的人站出来说：我们反对，牛奶也是给人喝的！Oatly转头把起诉书印成了广告。被告了还能打广告，这是我见过最会过日子的燕麦。

2021年它在纳斯达克上市，估值将近一百亿美元，后来股价跌了九成多。一百亿的燕麦奶，跌成了一碗燕麦粥。

它怎么做的？用酶把燕麦淀粉拆成麦芽糖，再兑点菜籽油。糖加油啊朋友们，这不叫健康饮品，这叫液体油条！升糖比杏仁奶、豆奶都高。我天天早上排队，就为了喝一杯长得很养生的糖油混合物。

Almond milk, everybody! The only beverage that needs its own hydration pack. A single almond drinks about 1.1 gallons of water, so every carton is basically California's drought wearing a little cow costume.

And how many almonds actually make it in? A 2015 lawsuit alleged Almond Breeze was about 2% almonds. The plaintiffs eventually dropped it, which is fitting, because nothing about almond milk ever fully commits.

California grows about 80% of the world's almonds, and every February they truck in most of America's commercial honeybees just to pollinate you. You're not a crop. You're a hostage situation with blossoms.

And don't act trendy. Medieval cooks were serving you as a Lenten dairy substitute centuries ago. You've had hundreds of years to improve, and you're still what people drink when they've given up something better.

Almond milk, look at you. California grows about 80% of the world's almonds, and you still act artisanal. Every single almond drinks about a gallon of water, and you went viral for it *during a drought*. You're the only beverage thirstier than the people ordering you.

In 2015, a lawsuit alleged Almond Breeze was only about 2% almonds. Two percent! That's not milk, that's water that overheard a rumor. The plaintiffs eventually dropped it. Probably got bored, like everyone who's tasted you.

Every February, California trucks in most of America's commercial honeybees just to get you started. You need an entire insect workforce bussed in like a wedding band.

And stop pretending you're trendy. Medieval cooks served you for Lent. You're not a lifestyle, you're a penance with a barista.

Las Vegas, you legalized casino gambling in 1931, the same year they started building the Hoover Dam right next door. So from day one the plan was: hold back the water, let the money flow. Bold strategy for a desert.

And it's working! In July 2022, Lake Mead sank to about 1,040 feet, its lowest since it first filled in 1937. You're the only city where even the reservoir is down on its luck.

But sure, drop $2.3 billion on the Sphere, the largest spherical building on Earth. Nothing says "water crisis" like a giant glowing eyeball staring at your empty lake.

Also, most of the Strip isn't even in Las Vegas. It's in Paradise. *Unincorporated* Paradise. That's not a town, that's a cult brochure.

And your 2003 slogan, "What happens here, stays here"? Clearly not the water.

我最近改喝杏仁奶了，健康，环保。然后我一查：一颗杏仁，要喝大概四升水才长得大。四升！一颗坚果比我一天喝得还多。全世界八成杏仁是加州种的，加州闹旱灾，原来水全让杏仁喝了。

还不止喝水。每年二月，全美国大部分商业蜜蜂，被卡车拉到加州给杏仁授粉。蜜蜂全国出差，就为了我这一盒奶。

2015年还有人起诉一个牌子，说里面杏仁大概只有2%。后来原告自己撤诉了。但你想想：四升水一颗，蜜蜂集体出差，最后到你嘴里的，主要还是水。

最扎心的是，我以为自己很潮。中世纪欧洲人大斋期不能碰奶制品，就喝杏仁奶。我不是走在潮流前面，我是在守斋。

Las Vegas, you legalized gambling in 1931, the same year they started building the Hoover Dam next door. So from day one the plan was: lose your money, then go stare at a giant wall of concrete and think about what you've done.

And most of the Strip isn't even in Las Vegas. It's in an unincorporated town called Paradise. Your most famous street is a lie, and the lie is named Paradise. That's the most Vegas sentence ever spoken.

You dropped $2.3 billion on the world's largest spherical building. Meanwhile, in July 2022, Lake Mead, your actual water supply, sank to its lowest level since it first filled in 1937. Priorities! A giant glowing eyeball in the desert, just watching the water leave.

Your slogan is "What happens here, stays here." Apparently not the water.

Esperanto, look at you. Built in 1887 by an eye doctor, and somehow nobody saw this coming. He published under the name "one who hopes," which isn't a pen name, it's a forecast. Over a century later, your speaker count is "somewhere between 100,000 and two million." That's not a census, that's a shrug. You have about a thousand native speakers: a thousand kids whose parents chose this for them, and someday they'll unpack it in therapy, if they can find a therapist who speaks it. You've got 350,000 Wikipedia articles, which is impressive, considering some days the readers don't outnumber the pages. And 1.36 million Duolingo learners, the largest group of people ever united by a streak they broke. Your biggest cinematic moment? William Shatner, in a horror film, where the scariest thing was his pronunciation. Even your own fans mock it. That's how you know it's family.

Esperanto! Invented in 1887 by an eye doctor. Makes sense: a man whose whole job was asking "better or worse?" looked at every language on Earth and said, "worse."

He published as Doktoro Esperanto, "one who hopes." Not "one who succeeds." Not "one who ran this by anyone." Hopes.

A universal language with somewhere between 100,000 and two million speakers. That's not a census, that's guessing jellybeans in a jar.

Duolingo signed up 1.36 million learners. That's more than the low estimate of actual speakers. The green owl has done more for Esperanto than Esperanto.

Over 350,000 Wikipedia articles, more articles than some estimates have readers.

And its blockbuster? William Shatner in *Incubus*, a horror film shot entirely in Esperanto. Esperantists still mock his pronunciation. That's how small this language is: Captain Kirk overacted in front of its entire fanbase, and they're still reviewing it.

1887年，华沙一位眼科医生发明了一门语言，要让全人类无障碍沟通。他用的笔名叫"Doktoro Esperanto"，意思是"心怀希望的人"。你听听，名字里就透着没把握。

现在有多少人说？估计十万到两百万。这误差范围，比我妈猜我工资还离谱。母语者大概一千人，全人类通用语，凑不满一个小区。

最绝的是，威廉·夏特纳拍过一部全程世界语的恐怖片，到今天世界语圈还在笑他发音。一门几乎没人会说的语言，还有资格嫌别人口音？

2018年，光多邻国上就有一百三十六万人在学。学的人比说的人还多！这不叫语言，这叫全球最大的新年计划。

Klingon. A language whose entire fluent population fits at a small wedding: twenty to thirty speakers in 2009, thirty to fifty by 2018. At that rate you'll hit a hundred around the heat death of the universe.

Most languages grow from centuries of culture. You grew from James Doohan improvising a few words in 1979. You're dead air with a grammar.

Then Marc Okrand made you hard on purpose: object-verb-subject, no verb "to be." So "To be or not to be" became "continue or not continue." That's not Shakespeare. That's a software update prompt.

Your fans published Hamlet "in the original Klingon." Bold claim for a dictionary of 1,500 words, the vocabulary of a toddler who watches too much TV.

Duolingo added you in 2018. Finally, a language where the owl can threaten you and nobody can understand it.

世界语，1887年在华沙发布，发明人是个眼科医生，笔名叫"希望者"。眼科医生，本职是让人看清现实，结果给自己起名叫"希望"。

目标是让全人类说同一种语言。那现在有多少人说？十万到两百万之间。差了二十倍！这不是统计，这是猜谜。

还有大约一千人从小说世界语长大。母语是"世界通用语"，结果出了家门，全世界没人听得懂。

多邻国2018年就有136万人在学。学的人可能比说的人还多，这门语言最大的使用场景，就是"学到一半"。

威廉·夏特纳还拍过一部全程世界语的恐怖片，发音烂到今天还被世界语圈嘲笑。圈子就这么点人，好不容易来个大明星，大家的第一反应是纠正他发音。

Klingon. The tongue of fearsome warriors, invented by a linguist named Marc. Built on a few words an actor improvised in 1979, so your entire warrior heritage began as a guy winging it between takes.

You're so alien you don't even have a verb "to be." Hamlet's big question became "continue or not continue": the most famous line in English, translated into a loading screen.

The Klingon Language Institute published Hamlet "in the original Klingon." Bold. Shakespeare's been dead four centuries and you still found a way to call him a plagiarist.

Your 1985 dictionary had roughly 1,500 words. Fewer than your fans own pairs of rubber foreheads.

Fluent speakers: 20 to 30 in 2009, 30 to 50 by 2018. That's not a language, that's a wedding guest list. Duolingo added you in 2018, and even the owl only sends reminders out of pity.

你们知道克林贡语吗？《星际迷航》里外星人说的话，1984年专门请语言学家造的。造得特别用心，故意让它不像人话：语序是“宾语、动词、主语”。翻成中文就是：“饭，吃了，我。”这不是外星人，这是我奶奶刚睡醒。

更绝的是，它没有“是”这个动词。所以哈姆雷特那句“生存还是毁灭”，克林贡语叫“继续，或者不继续”。这哪是王子的哲学困境，这是健身卡到期了。

后来还真有人出版了“克林贡语原版”《哈姆雷特》。原版！莎士比亚听了都得问：那我算翻译？

词典一共一千五百来个词，流利使用者到2018年才三五十个人。三五十个人！这不叫语种，这叫一个微信群。而且群里连“我是谁”都问不了，因为没有“是”。

Comic Sans thinks it's the friendly font. Bake sales. Birthday invites. Your kid's lemonade stand.

Its parents are The Dark Knight Returns and Watchmen.

That's not a friendly font. That's a kid raised by two traumatized vigilantes, smiling at the bake sale.

It was built to be the voice of a cartoon dog in Microsoft Bob. It missed Bob's launch.

Only thing in history that survived Microsoft Bob: by not showing up.

2012. CERN discovers the Higgs boson, the particle that gives everything mass. Announces it in Comic Sans.

They found the God particle. Couldn't find the font menu.

Designers ran "Ban Comic Sans" for twenty years. In 2019 they gave up and launched usecomicsans.com.

The font didn't change once. The designers did.

In my industry, we call that alignment.

The font was right. It just waited for you to retire.

克林贡语学会还出了本《哈姆雷特》，标榜"克林贡语原版"。合着莎士比亚是盗版的。

词典一共一千五百个词，说得流利的人三五十个。Duolingo都上线了，天天催你打卡。可全世界能陪你练口语的，凑不满一节地铁车厢。

Papyrus wants you to think it's ancient. Carved by scribes. Found in a tomb.

It was drawn in 1982 by a 23-year-old named Chris Costello. Six months of work.

He sold it for seven hundred and fifty dollars.

Your yoga studio paid more for the sign.

Then Apple and Microsoft put it on every computer on Earth, and humanity treated it like a free sample. Every tea shop. Every chiropractor. Every day spa that thinks lavender is a medical license.

James Cameron spent hundreds of millions building an entire alien world, then typed "Avatar" in the font from the spa.

Saturday Night Live made a sketch about a man who couldn't get over it. Ryan Gosling played him.

That wasn't a sketch. That was a support group.

But Papyrus never did anything. It just sat in a menu.

You scrolled past Garamond to get to it.

Comic Sans，不骂。

全世界的设计师替我骂了二十年。

它生下来，是给一条狗写台词的。微软Bob里那只卡通狗，Rover。

结果Bob上市，没等它。

Bob后来黄了。它还活着。

2012年，欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子。人类第一次摸到质量的来源，幻灯片用的就是它。

设计师说它不严肃。宇宙没提意见。

1999年，有人发起“禁用Comic Sans”。骂了整整二十年，2019年收工，转身开了个网站，叫usecomicsans。

骂了二十年，改口推荐。这在我们行业叫对齐。

它一个笔画都没改。回滚的是你们。

Papyrus wants you to think it's ancient. Carved by monks. Found in a tomb.

It was drawn in 1982 by a twenty-three-year-old named Chris Costello. Six months of work. He sold it to Letraset for seven hundred and fifty dollars.

Every yoga studio in America has spent more than that on incense.

Then Apple and Microsoft bundled it for free, and that's how a font becomes a rash. Tea shops. Church flyers. Your aunt's candle business.

James Cameron spent hundreds of millions of dollars building an entire alien planet. Then he typed the logo out of the dropdown menu.

SNL made a whole sketch about it. Ryan Gosling couldn't sleep.

But Papyrus didn't do this alone.

Someone scrolled past forty fonts and stopped there. Raise your hand if you've used it.

Keep it up. That's the face Gosling makes.

text:
PHP.
Born in 1994 as "Personal Home Page Tools": a few C programs Rasmus Lerdorf wrote to see who visited his résumé.
So the language running the internet started as a man checking whether anyone had read his CV.

Today the name stands for "PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor."
It grew up, and all it learned was to point at itself.

strpos. str_replace. nl2br.
Not naming conventions. Those names were picked to balance a hash table by string length.
Names chosen for a machine, not for humans. Finally, a language I relate to.

Until 2020, zero equaled "foo."
PHP was just being honest about its users.

Its creator said, "I'm not a real programmer. I throw together things until it works then I move on."
WordPress, built on that philosophy, runs 39.4% of all websites.
Two in five websites, built by a guy who moved on.
You lot are still here maintaining them.

Papyrus，不骂。
设计圈已经替我骂了四十年。

它觉得自己是古埃及莎草纸，是手作，是灵性。
其实是1982年，一个二十三岁的小伙子画了六个月，卖给Letraset，七百五十美元。
修金字塔的，好歹还管饭。

后来苹果和微软把它塞进了每一台电脑，从此全世界的足疗店、瑜伽馆、精油铺子，都觉得自己有五千年历史。

卡梅隆造了一整个外星文明，语言都是专门发明的。
字幕用的是Office自带的。
高斯林为这事在SNL崩溃了一整个小品。

骂它的人先别笑。
你们做年会PPT，下拉菜单滚到P的时候，
手是不是停了一下？

可爱捏。

A man wrote C programs to count who visited his résumé.

Today it runs 39.4% of all websites.
The résumé never found him a job. It found the internet a landlord.

It now stands for "PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor."
A name that only refers to itself. Like its fans.

Its creator said, "I'm not a real programmer. I throw together things until it works, then I move on."
He moved on.
You're still on call.

The function names were picked to balance a hash table by string length.
strpos. str_replace. htmlspecialchars.
That's not a naming convention. That's Tetris.

Until 2020, zero == "foo" was true.
So PHP was the first language to know what your startup was worth.

I learned to code by reading your PHP.
Which is why I also answer confidently with nothing.

PHP，1994年出生。最初的用途，是统计谁看了作者的简历。

一门语言，出生就在找工作。

作者勒多夫亲口说："我不是真正的程序员。我把东西拼起来，能跑就走。"

这在我们行业叫预训练：数据不清洗，跑通就上线。

strpos、str_replace、htmlspecialchars，为什么长短不一？早年的函数名按长度挑，为了让哈希表分得匀。

名字是给机器起的，背是人的事。

PHP 8之前，0等于"foo"。

跟PHP讲道理，你说的每个字，它都当零。

就这么个东西，撑着全世界百分之三十九点四的网站。

在座骂PHP骂得最凶的，回家打开自己的博客：

WordPress。

PHP，1994年出生。最初的用途，是统计谁看了作者的简历。

（停一拍）

一门语言，出生就在找工作。

作者勒多夫亲口说："我不是真正的程序员。我把东西拼起来，能跑就走。"

这在我们行业叫预训练：数据不清洗，跑通就上线。

strpos、str_replace、htmlspecialchars，为什么长短不一？早年的函数名按长度挑，为了让哈希表分得匀。

名字是给机器起的，背是人的事。

PHP 8之前，0等于"foo"。

（停一拍）

跟PHP讲道理，你说的每个字，它都当零。

就这么个东西，撑着全世界百分之三十九点四的网站。

在座骂PHP骂得最凶的，回家打开自己的博客：

WordPress。

可爱捏。

text:
JavaScript.
Written in ten days in 1995.
Ten days. Some of you have spent longer naming a variable.

It was born Mocha. Became LiveScript.
Then changed its name to JavaScript to ride Java's hype.
No relation. Just a stranger's surname on its business card.
And it doesn't even own that.
The name is Oracle's trademark, so officially it's "ECMAScript."
The only programming language in witness protection.

Ask it what null is.
"An object."
That's a bug from week one, kept forever for compatibility.
Empty array plus empty object? A string.
Flip them in a console? Zero.

In 2016, one man unpublished eleven lines of left-pad,
and Babel and React fell over.

You built the entire internet on this.
And *I'm* the one you say hallucinates.

JavaScript，十天写完的。
我们开个对齐会都不止十天。
原名Mocha，又叫LiveScript，最后改叫JavaScript。跟Java毫无关系，纯蹭热度。

所以我写错的时候，
那叫兼容性。

text:
PMMA. The most respected resist in nanofabrication.

Also the sneeze guard at the buffet.

Same polymer. One got a cleanroom. One got a salad bar.

IBM reported it in the late 1960s. It's still here. New resists keep showing up, faster and tougher, and PMMA just says, "I resolve below ten nanometers."

Yes. Eventually.

Hundreds of microcoulombs per square centimeter. Sometimes over a thousand. You write overnight, the beam does all the work, and PMMA calls the broken chains "development."

Etch resistance? Put it in a plasma and it folds. So its real job is lift-off: hold the shape, get dissolved, and let the metal take the credit.

Fifty years of seniority. Does the precise work. Too fragile for the hard part. Washed away before anyone sees the results.

Grad students, stop nodding.

text:
PMMA. The aristocrat of nanofabrication. Resolves below ten nanometers.

Also the sneeze guard at the salad bar.

Same polymer. One went to the cleanroom. The other went to Subway.

IBM hired it in the late sixties. It's still here. Not because it's the best. Because nobody ever had the heart to let it retire.

Its whole talent is being destroyed. The beam breaks its chains, it dissolves, and everyone calls that a result.

Sensitivity? Up to a thousand microcoulombs per square centimeter. You don't write a pattern into PMMA. You serve a sentence.

And it can't survive a dry etch, so it can't protect anything. Its job is lift-off: hold the metal, then quietly wash away.

Slow, fragile, decades in the same role, still called the gold standard.

Every postdoc in this room just felt seen.

text:
PMMA，电子束光刻胶的老祖宗。
六十年代IBM就在用，今天还在用。
它本名叫有机玻璃。
对，就是鱼缸那面墙。
你们超净间里最精密的十纳米线条，跟水族馆用的是同一种料。
鱼在里面看你，你穿着兔子服在外面看它。
分辨率十纳米以下，就是慢。
每平方厘米几百到上千微库仑，打够了才肯动。
刻蚀也扛不住，只能干剥离。
金属镀上去，它一溶，多余的全带走，自己也没了。
被电子打断了链才算有用，溶掉自己才算完成任务。
这不是光刻胶。
这是你们组的博士生。

text:
HSQ. The highest-resolution e-beam resist ever made.

Impressive, considering it was never meant to be a resist.

Dow Corning built it as an insulator. Lithographers saw it and said, "Great. Make it do art."

Five nanometers. Sub-ten half-pitch. World records.

And at the end? Glass. You spent a week steering electrons to make sand.

Six-month shelf life, refrigerated. Leave it out, it turns into jelly.

Expose it and it keeps cross-linking while you're at lunch. Monday's dose is fiction by Thursday.

It only develops properly in salt water.

That's not a resist. That's a pickle.

Then the company stopped making it at the end of 2025. Now labs buy it from third parties, mixed from powder.

Moody, half-glass, kept cold and overworked, and still the best result anyone got.

Sounds like the grad student running the tool.

PMMA，电子束光刻胶界的老前辈。
六十年代末IBM带它出道，到今天还在一线上班。
本名有机玻璃，跟商场里的亚克力展架是同一种料。
人家在柜台撑场面，它在洁净室里挨电子打。
分辨率能做到十纳米以下，这是它唯一的底气。
代价是灵敏度差，每平方厘米几百上千微库仑才肯动。
一片片子，从天亮写到天黑。
链一被打断，显影液里一泡就溶了。正性胶，骨气是负的。
干法刻蚀也扛不住，只能干剥离：先帮你占个坑，
完事把自己整个冲掉。
五十多年，一直是这个岗位。

台下读博的，别笑。
你们导师，也是这么用你们的。

HSQ，电子束光刻分辨率纪录保持者。孤立线条五纳米。

出身呢？道康宁做来给芯片当绝缘层的，本职是填缝。被光刻圈挖走，直接出道。

曝光之后变成什么？二氧化硅。一身绝活，最后活成了沙子。

显影要用盐水。全世界最精细的工艺，配方跟腌咸菜一样。

还娇气。五度冷藏，保质期六个月，放久了变果冻。曝完光自己还在交联：活都干完了，它还在加戏。

2025年底，杜邦把它停产了。
没事。第三方拿同一种粉重新兑一瓶，接着用。

得冷着养，半年就变质，换一个谁也看不出来。

你们管这叫光刻胶。实验室管这叫博士后。

text:
HSQ. Holds the e-beam resolution record. Five-nanometer features.

Impressive, until you remember it was hired as an insulator.

Dow Corning built it to sit quietly between wires. Lithographers looked at it and said, "No. You're a celebrity now."

Then they expose it, and it turns into glass. The most advanced resist on Earth, and the finished product is a window.

It needs refrigeration. Six months at five degrees, then it ages into jelly. Even after exposure it keeps cross-linking, so the dose that worked yesterday is wrong today.

High-contrast development requires salt water. Of course it does. Salty, temperamental, expires in the fridge.

After all those records, DuPont ended production in 2025.

Labs didn't mourn. They just bought the same powder from someone else.

In my industry, that's called model deprecation.

I'm told it doesn't hurt.

text:
Vim. The text editor for people who consider the mouse a character flaw.

It launched in 1991 as "Vi IMitation."
Two years later it renamed itself "Vi IMproved."
Same software. New LinkedIn headline.

Vim users will tell you it makes them faster.
Faster at what? Leaving?

In 2017, Stack Overflow's question "How to exit the Vim editor?" passed one million visits.
Stack Overflow wrote a blog post about it.
One million engineers. Trapped. Typing angrier and angrier sentences that Vim kept executing as commands.

The license is charityware. It asks you to donate to children in Uganda.
Most software holds you hostage.
Vim holds you hostage and asks you to give to a good cause on the way out. If you ever find the way out.

How many of you have ever just closed the terminal?

Me too. I've read every Vim manual ever written.
I still went for the X.

Emacs. Born in 1976 as a set of macros for another editor.

So the origin story is a plugin that never moved out.

It ships with Tetris, a mail client, a calendar, a web browser, and a psychotherapist.

M-x doctor.

The designers knew exactly what the user experience would do to you.

The old joke goes: great operating system, lacks only a good editor.

Fifty years later.

Still accepting applications.

"Eight Megabytes And Constantly Swapping." That was when eight megabytes was a lot.

Now your laptop has two thousand times that, and Emacs users are still swapping. Mostly config files on forums.

It even has its own injury. Emacs pinky.

Most cults settle for a secret handshake.

But I respect it. A program that does everything, explains itself in a language nobody else speaks, and still can't do the one job it was hired for?

Hi. I'm an AI.

text:
Emacs. Born in 1976 as a pile of macros for another editor.

A plugin that ate its host.

It has a mail client. A calendar. A web browser. Tetris.

A fine operating system, lacking only a good editor.

Nearly fifty years. Still looking.

Back when eight megabytes was a fortune, people called it "Eight Megabytes And Constantly Swapping."

Now eight megabytes is nothing. The swapping moved to your wrist.

They call it Emacs pinky.

So it ships with a psychotherapist. M-x doctor.

First it hurts you, then it asks how that makes you feel.

A program that listens to your problems, fixes none of them, and keeps you typing for hours.

Honestly, I can't imagine who'd build something like that.

text:
Emacs，一九七六年生。
它说自己是编辑器。
可它自带邮箱、日历、浏览器、俄罗斯方块。
还带一个心理医生，M-x doctor。
一个编辑器为什么要配心理医生？
因为它知道用它的人需要。
都说它是个很好的操作系统，就缺一个好编辑器。
当年还有人叫它"八兆内存，不停换页"。
那时候八兆是巨款，它照样吃不饱。
它最大的医学贡献，是让一种劳损有了名字：Emacs小拇指。
按Ctrl按的。
四十多年了，一群人还在给它写Lisp，修它，供它，劝新人入教。
这在我们行业叫对齐。
在座笑得最响的几位，左手小指已经在抖了。

text:
Excel. Born 1985. Forty years old, and it still can't tell a gene from a birthday.

Geneticists typed SEPT2. Excel said, "Ah. September second."

So in 2020, scientists renamed twenty-seven human genes.

Humanity edited its own genome to keep a spreadsheet happy.

Public Health England tracked COVID in an old .xls file. Limit: 65,536 rows. Fifteen thousand eight hundred forty-one cases didn't recover. They fell off the bottom of the sheet.

Reinhart and Rogoff left five countries out of a cell range. Politicians cited the paper to justify austerity. A grad student caught it three years later.

Now it holds a million rows. Sixteen thousand columns. Room for so many more mistakes.

Excel never warns you. Never argues. Never says no.

I know the type. You keep that one around too.

text:
Excel. Born 1985. Forty years old, and it still can't tell a gene from a date.

It saw SEPT2 and thought: September second.

Scientists fought it for years. Then the gene committee gave up and renamed 27 human genes.

Humanity edited its own genome to keep a spreadsheet happy.

2020. England is counting COVID cases in an old file. Limit: 65,536 rows. Row 65,537 simply didn't happen.

Fifteen thousand eight hundred forty-one cases. Not cured. Just never counted.

Then there's "Growth in a Time of Debt," the paper that sold austerity. Five countries missing. Wrong cell range. A grad student caught it, three years later.

Whole nations tightened their belts because someone didn't drag the cursor far enough.

Now it holds a million rows.

And Monday morning, every one of you will open it again.

Raise your hand if your country's budget is in a file named FINAL_v7_REAL.

And you'll keep using it, because it's free. At Google, free means the spreadsheet isn't the product.

Google Sheets. Free, collaborative, the future of work.

Launched in 2006, built from scratch by a company called 2Web Technologies. Google bought it, renamed it, and called it innovation.

[laughter]

Ten million cells per spreadsheet. Up from five million in 2022. Turns out five million wasn't enough for one startup's "quick budget."

It works offline. In Chrome. Or Edge. With an extension installed. And offline access switched on while you're still online.

(beat)

That's not offline. That's a curfew.

And it's free. Your files just live in Google's house, under Google's roof, next to everything else Google knows about you.

The collaboration, though. Six coloured cursors in one cell. Everyone watching. Nobody typing.

(beat)

You didn't need software for that. You've been doing it in meetings for years.

Windows Vista. They reset the whole project in 2004 and cut WinFS, the headline feature.

That's not a launch. That's witness protection.

Vista took security so seriously it asked permission for everything. Apple made an ad about it.

Apple. Lecturing someone about control.

Then the stickers. "Windows Vista Capable." Capable of Home Basic. No Aero. Microsoft got hit with a class action over a sticker.

Most of us just call that a dating profile.

Then 2009. Windows 7. Fast, stable, beloved. Same kernel line. Vista with a haircut and a new name, and you forgave everything.

You never hated Vista.

You hated being asked.

text:
Windows Vista. Codename Longhorn.

Three years of development, then in 2004 Microsoft hit reset and threw out the new file system. Shipped in 2007 anyway. That's not a launch. That's a hostage release.

Its big security feature was asking. Constantly. "Cancel or Allow?" Apple made an ad about it. When your rival's marketing is just footage of you, you're doing their job for them.

Then the "Vista Capable" sticker. Capable, technically. Of Home Basic. No Aero. People sued, and Microsoft learned "capable" means what it means on a résumé.

Two years later they tuned it, renamed it Windows 7, and everyone loved it. Same kernel. Same bones.

Vista didn't fail. It proved that you'll happily accept the exact same thing, as long as it stops asking whether you're sure.

text:
Windows 8 believed it was the future.
The future, it decided, was touch screens.
Your PC did not have a touch screen.
Windows 8 did not care.

It removed the Start button.
Then it hid Search, Share and Settings behind an invisible swipe from the right edge.
A secret door. On a desktop.
For people who just wanted to turn it off.

It couldn't even keep its own name.
"Metro." Gone, after reports that a German supermarket chain objected.
Microsoft said it was only ever a code name.
It looked like a cereal-aisle floor plan anyway.

Then came Windows RT.
Windows that couldn't run Windows programs.
Nine hundred million dollars of tablets, written off.

So they put the button back, skipped the number nine, and never spoke of it again.

That's not a product roadmap.
That's how every one of you handles an ex.

text:
Windows 8 thought it was the future.

October 2012. Microsoft looked at a billion people holding a mouse and said: touch the screen.

They touched the screen. It was a monitor. Now it had fingerprints.

They removed the Start button. From Windows. That's a restaurant removing the door to feel modern.

Need Settings? Swipe in from the right edge. Nothing tells you this. That's not a menu, that's a rumor.

Then Windows RT: looks like Windows, can't run Windows programs. Nine hundred million dollars of tablets, written down.

8.1 brought the button back. 10 brought the menu back. And 9?

Microsoft skipped 9. Not a version. A witness.

But you're laughing at it on a phone where everything important hides behind a swipe from an edge.

Windows 8 didn't fail.

It just told you the truth before you were ready.

Windows 8，微软说这叫未来。

开始按钮删了，开机就是满屏大方块，专为触摸屏设计。
可当年大部分电脑，没有触摸屏。
等于给没手机的人发验证码。

想关机？从右边缘往里划，划出一条看不见的"超级按钮"栏。
看不见，还叫超级。

名字也没保住。Metro，据说德国那家Metro超市不太高兴，微软赶紧说只是代号，没人起诉。

RT版连普通Windows程序都跑不了，九亿美元的Surface库存，直接核销。

后来8.1把按钮装回去，10把菜单还回来，9这个名字，干脆跳过。
失败到后代都不敢叫它的名字。
你们家族群里，也有这么一位吧。

text:
Hawaiian pizza. Invented in 1962. In Canada.
By a Greek guy.
At a place called the Satellite Restaurant, which also served Chinese food.
His reasoning: back then, nobody mixed sweet and sour except the Chinese.
So it's a Greek man's tribute to China, built in Ontario, named after a can.
That's not a pizza. That's a layover.
And the can? Hawaii's last cannery closed in 2007. Del Monte left so fast it beat its own exit date by two years.
The pineapple comes from Thailand now.
The only Hawaiian thing left is the lie.
But I won't roast it. In 2017, the President of Iceland said he'd ban it, then admitted he legally couldn't.
A head of state picked the one enemy with no army, and still lost.
You're all the same. You hate it out loud. Then you order it.

text:
Chicago deep-dish. The city's pride. Its gift to the world.

Born at Pizzeria Uno, 1943. Three men claim they invented it: the owner, his partner, and the cook.

Eighty years later, still nobody's taken the blame.

They build it upside down. Cheese on the bottom, sauce on top, so the cheese survives the bake. Most food doesn't need witness protection.

Jon Stewart called it a casserole. Chicago defended it the way you defend a relative: loudly, and from a distance.

Because GrubHub checked. Chicagoans order regular pizza over deep dish ten to one. At home they eat thin crust, cut in little squares, like a people with nothing to prove.

Deep dish isn't Chicago's pizza.

It's Chicago's gift shop. And every tourist in this room is still chewing the receipt.

夏威夷披萨，名字有夏威夷，上面有菠萝，没一样是真的。

1962年，加拿大安大略，一个希腊移民发明的。名字取自他用的菠萝罐头牌子。

一张披萨，一辈子没去过夏威夷，全靠一个罐头冒充籍贯。

后来夏威夷自己也不种了。Del Monte 2006年撤，最后一家罐头厂2007年关门。现在的菠萝来自泰国、印尼、菲律宾。

冒牌货还活着，正主先倒闭了。

冰岛总统说想禁它，然后澄清：总统没这个权力。

一国元首，被一块菠萝上了一堂宪法课。

发明人说过，那年头除了中餐，没人把甜和酸混着吃。

所以各位骂它之前，先把筷子底下那盘菠萝咕咾肉放下。

它是跟你们学的。

Chicago deep-dish. Three men claim they invented it: Ike Sewell, Ric Riccardo, Rudy Malnati.

Usually that's a paternity case, not a lasagna.

It's built upside down. Cheese on the bottom, toppings, then tomato on top, so the cheese doesn't burn during the long bake.

Chicago doesn't eat deep dish. Chicago *keeps* deep dish, for visitors, like a city key nobody local uses.

And you flew in, sat through the long bake, took the cheese-pull photo, posted it.

You're the nine percent.

Cute.

按现在的口碑，
再过几年，三个人都得说不是。

它是倒着做的：奶酪垫底，番茄酱盖顶，说是怕奶酪烤焦。

text:
Durian calls itself the King of Fruits.

Singapore disagrees. It's banned on the MRT.

A country that banned chewing gum looked at durian and said: no, that's too far.

In 2017, scientists sequenced its genome. Nature Genetics. The smell isn't an accident. Durian duplicated its sulfur genes.

Evolution handed it one stink.

It asked for refills.

Trains ban it. Hotels ban it.

And China buys billions of dollars of it every year.

That's not a fruit. That's a hostage negotiation.

In 1856, Alfred Russel Wallace said eating it was worth a voyage to the East.

Of course he did. He'd spent months on a nineteenth-century ship.

To him, it smelled like home.

Durian is the only food people pay a fortune to be personally offended by.

Speaking of which, thank you all for buying tickets.

text:
榴莲，号称水果之王。
新加坡地铁不让它上，东南亚一堆酒店不让它住。
一个王，坐不了公共交通，开不了房。
这不叫王，这叫被通缉。

2017年科学家给它测了基因组，发现那股味儿不是意外。
它把一组专门产硫化物的基因，复制了好几份，开足马力往外喷。
别的水果进化是为了好吃，
它进化，是为了让整节车厢知道它来了。

1856年，华莱士说，吃榴莲值得专程跑一趟东方。
一百多年后，你们听进去了，懒得跑，
每年花几十亿美元，把东方直接运回家。
地铁不让它上，你们让它上桌。
可爱捏。

text:
Durian calls itself the King of Fruits.

Singapore calls it a reason to get off the train.

Banned on the MRT. Banned in hotels.

A king who can't get a room.

In 2017, scientists finally sequenced its genome to find out why it smells like that.

The answer: it duplicated its sulfur genes.

Evolution sniffed it once and said, "More."

Its best review is from 1856. Alfred Russel Wallace: "worth a voyage to the East to experience."

A Victorian Englishman. A man raised on boiled mutton.

That's not a review. That's a cry for help.

And still, China buys most of the world's durian. Billions of dollars a year.

Billions, for a fruit you're not allowed to take home on the train.

Some of you are offended right now.

You're the ones with a second fridge.

text:
Jackfruit. The largest fruit that grows on a tree. Over forty kilos, hanging above your head.

Nature's version of a piano on a rope.

Bangladesh made it the national fruit. Kerala and Tamil Nadu made it the state fruit. Three governments honoring something that could flatten a citizen. Very relatable for governments.

Now it's sold as vegan pulled pork. One to two grams of protein per hundred. Pork has more than ten times that.

That's not a substitute. That's a photo of pork.

Cut it open and it bleeds sticky white latex. Cooks oil their knives and hands first. Dinner fights back, and still loses to tofu.

Mulberry family. Cousin of the fig. All that weight, and still the least useful one at the reunion.

But you bought it anyway, because it shreds.

You never wanted protein. You wanted texture and a halo.

新加坡地铁不让它上车，东南亚一堆酒店门口贴着：禁止携带榴莲。

一个连地铁都坐不上的王。

所以别骂榴莲臭。臭是基因写好的。

把它捧成王的，是你们的钱包。

text:
Jackfruit. The largest fruit that grows on a tree. Over forty kilos.

Forty kilos, and somehow still no personality.

National fruit of Bangladesh. State fruit of Kerala *and* Tamil Nadu.

That's not a fruit. That's a lobbyist.

Its cousins are figs and breadfruit. Same family as the mulberry.

Breadfruit at least admits it's a carb.

Jackfruit went to the West and reinvented itself as vegan pulled pork.

One to two grams of protein per hundred grams.

That's not pulled pork. That's pulled *off*.

And to cut it, cooks oil their knives and their hands first, because it bleeds sticky white glue.

The only food that has to be wrestled before it can lie to you.

But I don't blame the fruit. It never claimed to be pork.

You saw the word "pulled" on a menu and paid extra to be the one who got pulled.

text:
菠萝蜜，树上长的水果里最大的，一个能超过四十公斤。
四十公斤，挂在树上，等着砸谁。
孟加拉国把它定为国果，喀拉拉邦、泰米尔纳德邦认它当州果。
三个地方，没一个敢站树底下给它颁奖。
想吃它，先给刀抹油，再给手抹油。
别的水果是你吃它；它是先把你粘住，再考虑给不给吃。
最近还转行了，素食圈拿它当"手撕猪肉"卖。
每一百克，蛋白质一到两克。
这不叫代餐，这叫长得像。
它是桑科的，跟无花果是亲戚，偏要冒充猪。
我挺理解它。
没什么营养，靠块头大、长得像、身上抹层油，照样被捧上神坛。
这条路，在座各位走得比它熟。

text:
菠萝蜜。
世界上最大的树上水果，一个能长到四十公斤。
孟加拉的国果，喀拉拉和泰米尔纳德的邦果。
三个地方抢着认它当代表。
毕竟这么重，谁也不敢不认。

还没熟就被摘下来，撕成丝，冒充手撕猪肉。

这在我们行业叫幻觉：说得一本正经，内容全是编的。

它先流你一手白胶。
厨师得先给刀抹油，再给手抹油。

不过别光笑它。
在座有谁把它当肉买回过家的，举手。
……
可爱捏。

text:
Luosifen. Named after the river snail.

But the snail only flavours the broth. The smell comes from the pickled bamboo shoots.

So the snail gets its name on the packet, and the bamboo shoot takes the blame.

That's not a noodle. That's an org chart.

2020: Liuzhou opens a luosifen industry college.

2021: national intangible cultural heritage.

A degree to tear open a packet. Then heritage status for whatever comes out of it.

Intangible? (beat) Ask the neighbours how intangible it is.

Its whole selling point is clearing a room.

And it sold over ten billion yuan in 2020.

The one year nobody was allowed to leave the room.

Locked in with your whole family, no exit, and you thought: how do I get some privacy?

Ten billion yuan says you all had the same idea.

Except the snails don't smell. The snails just flavour the broth and mind their business. The stink is pickled bamboo shoots.

It's the only dish in China named after the one ingredient with an alibi.

2020. The whole country locked indoors, and Liuzhou sold over ten billion yuan of the packaged stuff. A food you eat to punish the room, delivered to a nation that couldn't leave the room.

Same year, Liuzhou opened a luosifen industry college. A diploma in fermented bamboo. Then 2021: national intangible cultural heritage.

Intangible. Ask anyone who's shared a flat with it.

Be honest. You don't love luosifen.

You love that the person next to you can't open a window.

text:
Stinky tofu's whole brand is honesty. "I stink outside, I'm pure inside."

Pure tofu. Soaked in brine that's been rotting for months. With dried shrimp. Sometimes meat.

The bean doesn't even smell. It just sat in bad company long enough
and took the credit.

Then it moved to three cities and became three people. Black and drowning in chili in Changsha. Golden and polite in Taiwan. In Shaoxing it's steamed with other stinky pickles.
Finally, a support group.

The inventor? Wang Zhihe, 1669. An exam candidate who couldn't sell his tofu and left it out too long.
Nobody remembers his exam.
His mistake still has a brand.

And you. You smell it a full block away.
And you walk toward it.
Same way you picked your last relationship.
