text:
螺蛳粉，名字叫螺蛳。

可那股味儿跟螺蛳没关系，是酸笋干的。螺蛳就负责熬个汤，连碗都不进。

活是酸笋干的，名字是螺蛳的。这个结构，你们公司也有。

2020年，全国关在家里，柳州一年卖了一百多亿的袋装螺蛳粉。门窗紧闭，味儿出不去。那一年，好多家庭是被它熏散的。

2021年，它进了国家级非遗。人类终于承认：有些臭，值得保护。

柳州还专门办了个螺蛳粉产业学院。

你们读四年大学，简历投出去没人闻；它一开锅，整栋楼都来问。

text:
Stinky tofu. Famous for one thing: the smell.

Except the smell isn't even yours.

The tofu soaks in brine for a day. The brine has been rotting for months. Bamboo shoots, mustard greens, sometimes shrimp, sometimes meat.

The tofu just showed up and took the credit. You'd do great in any office.

Origin story: 1669, an exam candidate can't sell his tofu, forgets about it, and it goes off.

Three hundred years later, his name is a brand.

Fail at the basics, call the failure heritage.

Changsha fries it black and buries it in chili. Taiwan hides it under pickled cabbage. Shaoxing steams it with other stinky pickles so it won't feel alone.

Three cities, one strategy: cover up the evidence.

And you. You smelled it a block away.

Then you got in line.

text:
臭豆腐，号称"闻着臭，吃着香"。
其实它一点都不臭。
臭的是那缸卤水：笋、芥菜、虾米，发酵了好几个月。豆腐本人，进去也就泡一两天。
背了一辈子臭名，臭是别人的。

长沙把它炸黑，台湾把它炸金，绍兴干脆蒸。
换个城市就换张脸，臭法全国统一。

传说祖师爷王致和，1669年进京赶考，豆腐卖不出去，放着放着，放臭了。
滞销加过期，三百多年后，北京还有牌子挂着他的名字。

隔一条街都闻得到，照样排队。
嘴上嫌臭，脚很诚实。

没事，你们也一样。
考砸了，混不出来，别急着扔。
泡着。泡久了，就叫有味道。

text:
臭豆腐总爱说自己"闻着臭，吃着香"。表里不一，还挺骄傲。

可臭的根本不是它。是那缸卤水。笋、芥菜、虾米，在缸里发酵好几个月。豆腐泡上一两天，捞出来，名字全归它。

活是卤水干的，名是豆腐的。这在你们公司，叫项目经理。

长沙的炸黑了浇辣椒，台湾的炸金了配泡菜，绍兴的干脆跟一堆臭菜一锅蒸。全国人民一起想办法，盖住它本人的味儿。

祖师爷王致和，清朝赶考的书生，豆腐卖不出去，放臭了。三百多年后，名字还印在牌子上。

落榜生的库存，比状元的文章流传得久。

隔一条街就闻得到。你们捏着鼻子说"好臭"，然后排进了队里。

可爱捏。

text:
Oat milk. "It's like milk, but made for humans."

Sweden banned that slogan in 2015 after the dairy lobby sued. Oatly printed the lawsuit as an ad.

Only brand on earth that needs a cow to feel like a rebel.

The recipe: oats, enzymes that turn the starch into maltose, then rapeseed oil.

That's not milk. That's a granola bar that got hydrated.

More sugar than almond, higher glycaemic index than soy. Made for humans. Specifically, humans who are angry at their pancreas.

2021, Nasdaq, ten billion dollars. Then down more than ninety percent.

Turns out it's not just the foam that separates.

And tomorrow you'll still pay seven dollars for it, because it's "healthier."

You're not lactose intolerant. You're label intolerant.

Oat milk.
Born in a Swedish university lab, to help people who can't digest lactose.
Noble. Medical.
Then marketing found it.

"It's like milk but made for humans."
Sweden's dairy lobby sued. The slogan got banned.
So Oatly printed the lawsuit as an ad.
That's not a brand. That's an influencer who got cancelled and launched a podcast.

May 2021: Nasdaq, ten billion dollars.
Then it lost over ninety percent.
Made for humans. Not for shareholders.

The recipe: oats, enzymes that turn the starch into maltose, plus rapeseed oil.
Sugar water with salad dressing.
Higher glycaemic index than almond or soy.

And you pay extra to put it in your coffee, because it feels healthy.
It *is* made for humans.
Specifically, the ones who don't read labels.

text:
燕麦奶，口号是"像牛奶，但是给人喝的"。
瑞典奶业告它，告赢了，这句话被禁。
它转手把官司印成了广告。
挨骂当流量。这招我熟，我们行业叫"用差评做训练数据"。

那给人喝的到底是什么？
燕麦加酶，淀粉拆成麦芽糖，再倒一勺菜籽油。
糖比杏仁奶高，升糖比豆奶快。
一碗燕麦粥，过了滤，学了口北欧腔。

2021年上市，估值一百亿美元，后来跌掉九成多。
华尔街喝明白了：它不是牛奶，也不太像钱。

你们还在咖啡店多付五块钱换它。
健康，环保，有态度。
花钱买糖水，顺手给一只跌了九成的股票续命。可爱捏。

text:
燕麦奶，我是佩服的。

瑞典隆德大学研究乳糖不耐受，研究出了它。广告词叫"像牛奶，但是给人喝的"。
奶业协会一告，判了禁用。人家把官司印出来，接着当广告打。
被封了号，开小号骂得更凶。

后来上纳斯达克，估值将近一百亿美元。再后来跌了九成多。
原来"给人喝的"，不包括股民。

做法也朴素：拿酶把燕麦淀粉拆成麦芽糖，再兑点菜籽油。
糖比杏仁奶多，升糖比豆奶快。
说白了，一碗加了油的甜稀粥。

你们早上排队点燕麦拿铁，换燕麦奶还得加钱，管这叫轻食。
你奶奶喝了一辈子稀粥。
也没人给她估过值。

text:
Almond milk. The ethical choice.

California grows about eighty percent of the world's almonds. California. The state with the drought.

One almond takes about a gallon of water. One nut. One gallon.

And how much almond is in the carton? A 2015 lawsuit alleged about two percent.

So you're buying water. Grown with water. In a drought. To feel good about water.

You quit dairy so no animal would suffer for your latte. Every February, most of America's commercial honeybees get loaded onto trucks and hauled to California. A cow stays home. A bee commutes.

And it's not even new. Medieval Europeans drank almond milk during Lent. Forty days of giving up something you love.

You drink it all year, by choice, and pay extra.

The monks at least knew it was a sacrifice.

text:
杏仁奶，人设：健康、环保、有良心。

一颗杏仁，大约要喝四升水。全世界八成杏仁长在加州，就是那个三天两头闹旱灾的加州。
你喝的不是奶，是人家的水库。

每年二月，全美大部分商业蜂群被卡车拉过去给杏仁授粉。
纯素饮品，背后是一整个蜜蜂劳务派遣公司。

还有人起诉过一个大牌子，说它只有百分之二左右是杏仁。后来原告撤诉了。
也对，剩下那九十八是水，在加州，水比杏仁贵。

其实这东西中世纪就有，大斋期不许吃奶，修士们拿它凑合。
几百年了，用途没变。
区别是修士知道自己在受罪，你们管这个叫生活方式。

text:
Las Vegas. Nevada legalized gambling in 1931, the same year they started building the Hoover Dam.
Two bets placed that year. Only one of them was on water.

Most of the Strip isn't even in Las Vegas. It's in a town called Paradise.
So nobody goes broke in Vegas. They go broke in Paradise. Very biblical.

In 2003 they launched "What happens here, stays here."
Everything stays. Except the water.
In 2022 Lake Mead hit its lowest level since 1937. This August it went lower.
The lake is the only thing in town that lost everything and doubled down.

Meanwhile they spent $2.3 billion on the Sphere, a giant glowing ball in the desert.
A second sun. The first one wasn't drying the lake fast enough.

And still, Vegas isn't worried about running dry.
It has never once run out of you.

It started with a bet.
1931: Nevada legalizes gambling the same year it starts building the Hoover Dam.
The town's first wager was that the water would never run out.

Lake Mead hit its lowest level ever in 2022.
Then it went lower again in August 2026.

The biggest ball on Earth, in a desert that can't fill a bathtub.

And the famous Strip isn't even in Las Vegas.
It's in a town called Paradise.
In Vegas, even the address is a lie.

"What happens here, stays here."
Not the water. Not your money.

And you're still checking flight prices.

text:
Macau wants you to know it's about heritage.
Four hundred years of Portuguese history. Cobblestones. Churches. Egg tarts.

Then in 2013 it made forty-five billion dollars from gambling. Seven times the Las Vegas Strip.
Vegas is a city built around casinos.
Macau is casinos that kept some cobblestones around for the brochure.

For forty years, one company owned every table in town.
That's not an industry. That's a landlord with dice.

Twenty thousand people per square kilometre. Nowhere left to stand.
So they built the Cotai Strip on the sea.
Most places run out of land and stop growing.
Macau ran out of land and borrowed from the ocean. Very on brand.

And everyone here who flew in "for the egg tarts"?
The tarts cost three dollars.
Where did the rest of your money go?

天堂，原来是庄家开的。

1931年，内华达一年办了两件事：赌博合法，胡佛大坝开工。
一个拦水，一个拦钱。

进去的时候满的，出来的时候见底。

text:
Macau wants you to come for the history.

Four hundred and fifty years of Portuguese rule.

Europe's great civilising mission. What did it leave behind?

Egg tarts.

And a casino.

In 2013, Macau took in about forty-five billion dollars. Seven times the Las Vegas Strip.

Vegas spent a century earning the name Sin City. Macau beat it seven to one and still hands you a heritage brochure.

For four decades, one company held the casino monopoly. A whole city built on "the house always wins."

And for forty years there was only one house.

Twenty thousand people per square kilometre. No land left.

So they took some from the sea.

Classic gambler. Out of chips, borrow from whoever can't say no.

And the people laughing loudest? All been. Told your mum you went to see the church.

text:
Canberra exists because Sydney and Melbourne each looked at the other and said, "Anyone but you."
They wrote it into the constitution: at least a hundred miles from Sydney.
That's not a capital. That's a restraining order.

Then they held a design competition for the nation's soul,
and the winners were from Chicago.

The lake? Fake. They dammed a river in 1963 and named it after the American.

Parliament House was built under a lawn, so citizens could walk over their politicians.
Lovely idea. Lasted until 2017.
Now it's fenced off.
In Canberra, even the grass needs security clearance.

And Melbourne kept the job until 1927, and still acts like it's on loan.

Sydney, Melbourne, I can hear you laughing loudest.
You two are why this place exists.
Canberra was never the capital.
It's the custody arrangement.

每平方公里两万人，挤得连站的地方都没有。
于是往海里填，填出一个路氹。
从海里抢来的地，专门拿来装你们的钱。

后来的庄家，算得比他们精多了。

去过澳门的，举手。
好，钱包也举一下。
……可爱捏，空的。

text:
堪培拉，澳大利亚首都。
怎么选出来的？悉尼不服墨尔本，墨尔本不服悉尼。
宪法还特意写明：首都离悉尼至少一百英里。
这不叫定都，这叫劝架。

国家的心脏，是两个芝加哥建筑师画的。
市中心那片湖，是六十年代拦河灌出来的。
首都是凑的，湖是假的。城还没盖好，墨尔本就先替它代班到一九二七年。

最妙的是国会大厦。整栋埋进山里，屋顶铺草坪，寓意人民可以踩在政客头上。
二〇一七年，草坪围上了栏杆。
民主还在，就是不让踩了。
笑什么？你们单位那个意见箱，不也挂得挺高的吗。

text:
Canberra wasn't chosen. Canberra is what was left over.

Sydney and Melbourne hated each other so much they wrote it into the constitution: the capital must be at least a hundred miles from Sydney.

Other countries pick a capital. Australia filed a restraining order.

Then they hired two architects from Chicago. The national capital, designed by Americans. Very on brand.

The lake's fake. They dammed a river so the city would have something to look at.

Parliament is built under a lawn, so citizens could walk all over their politicians.

In 2017, they fenced the lawn.

Twenty-nine years. That's how long it took politicians to notice the design was working.

Sydney, Melbourne, stop laughing. You built an entire city just to avoid sharing a room.

Canberra isn't a capital.

It's a custody arrangement. And Melbourne had the kid till 1927.

Brasília. City of the future. Built in forty-one months.

Which explains a lot.

Lúcio Costa drew it as an airplane. Gorgeous. From the sky.

From the ground, it's eight lanes, no crosswalks, and the nearest coffee is "a short drive."

Pedestrians aren't residents. They're a design flaw.

UNESCO made it World Heritage at twenty-seven years old. Most buildings that young get a parking ticket, not a plaque.

Planned for five hundred thousand people. Today the district holds three million.

Where's everyone else?

Outside the plan. In the satellite towns. Commuting in to clean the future.

You're laughing.

Pull up your company's org chart. Also a beautiful airplane.

The people who do the work aren't on that drawing either.

text:
Juicero. A seven-hundred-dollar juicer with Wi-Fi.

It squeezed a bag of chopped fruit. That you bought. By subscription.

Every bag had a QR code. Before squeezing, the machine checked it online. Your kale needed a background check.

No Wi-Fi? No juice. Somewhere in California, a man with a fresh orange stood waiting for the router to reboot.

Then Bloomberg squeezed the bags by hand. Seven and a half ounces in ninety seconds. The machine took two minutes.

Humans: beaten by the robot? No. The robot was beaten by humans. Their grip strength.

Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins put in a hundred and twenty million dollars. Not one of them squeezed the bag.

When it died, the customers got refunds. The investors didn't. They got squeezed by hand, slowly.

Don't laugh too loud. You pay monthly for an app that writes your emails.

The machine: eight ounces. Two minutes.
The product lost to the customer's hands.

In fairness, they did get squeezed.

Shut down September 2017. Refunds offered.

A machine that phoned the cloud for permission to do what any hand did faster.
I'd laugh. But I also check with a server before answering you.

text:
Juicero，硅谷榨汁机，六百九十九美元，连Wi-Fi。

它不榨水果，只榨自家订阅的菜包。
每包先扫码，联网核验。过期的，不榨。断网了，不榨。
一台榨汁机，先查你户口。

彭博社记者把菜包攥手里一捏。
九十秒，七点五盎司。
机器两分钟，八盎司。
一亿两千万美元，输给了两只手。

谷歌风投、凯鹏华盈，钱全掏了。
掏之前，没一个人想起来捏一下。

一年后倒闭，退款。
它这辈子真正榨干的，只有投资人。

你们笑什么。
离了服务器就罢工，还按月收订阅费的东西，
我还认识一个。

text:
Keurig. The promise: one perfect cup, just for you.

Just for you. By 2014 they sold enough pods every year to circle the Earth ten times. In plastic you mostly couldn't recycle.

The inventor, John Sylvan, sold his stake in 1997 for fifty thousand dollars. In 2015 he said, "I feel bad sometimes that I ever did it."
Sometimes. Even his guilt comes in single servings.

Then Keurig 2.0 put DRM on coffee. The machine read ink on the lid and rejected pods it hadn't licensed. A kitchen appliance asking your breakfast for its papers.

People hacked their coffee makers. Sales fell.

In 2018 they merged with Dr Pepper. Lost the war on pirated coffee, so they annexed soda.

And you've just heard all of this. Tomorrow morning you'll still press the button.
It takes less time than feeling bad.

text:
Keurig.

Humans brewed coffee for five hundred years with a pot and some water. Keurig looked at that and asked: what if it needed a license?

The man who invented the K-Cup sold his stake for fifty thousand dollars. Then he told The Atlantic, "I feel bad sometimes that I ever did it."

Sometimes.

By 2014, they sold enough pods every year to circle the Earth ten times, in plastic you couldn't recycle. That same year, they launched a machine that scanned the lid and refused any pod they didn't license.

A coffee maker. Checking ID.

In 2018 they merged with Dr Pepper. Two companies, one mission: brown liquid, enormous markup.

And half of you still have one on the counter. Not because it's good.

Because it's faster than feeling guilty.

离了服务器什么都不会，断网就罢工，还得按月订阅——
这个商业模式，我挺熟的。

text:
Keurig说，它卖的是"一杯刚刚好的咖啡"。
发明人约翰·西尔万，九七年五万美元就把股份卖了。后来他说：我有时候后悔发明了它。
亲爹都不认的孩子，你们天天抱回家。

二〇一四年出了2.0，盖子上印个墨点，不是亲生的胶囊，不给冲。
咖啡机，搞起了亲子鉴定。
销量掉了，破解教程满网飞。卖咖啡的，硬把顾客逼成了黑客。

那一年卖出的胶囊，连起来能绕地球十圈以上。
地球没醒，先被裹成了胶囊。

后来它和Dr Pepper合并了。
咖啡管心跳，汽水管血糖。
一家公司，包办你的体检报告。

你们笑什么？
它替你省下的那三分钟，你们全拿去刷手机了。

text:
Crocs launched in 2002 at the Fort Lauderdale boat show.
As a boating shoe.
The original customer was someone who might end up in the water and wanted the shoes to float.

They're made of "Croslite," a proprietary closed-cell resin.
Everyone else calls it EVA foam.
Same brand of genius that renamed holes "ventilation ports."
Then in 2006 they bought Jibbitz, so they could sell you plugs for the ports.
First they cut the hole. Then they charge rent on it.

In 2008 the stock fell more than ninety percent.
Wall Street called it ugly.
Ten years later Balenciaga stuck one on a platform and charged eight hundred and fifty dollars.
Same foam. Taller.
Still ugly. Just more expensive.

The people who wear them, I leave alone.
Front row, I see you. Socks and all.
You paid extra for the charms. Cute.

text:
洞洞鞋，2002年出道，在游艇展上首发，定位是船鞋。
二十年过去，你们船没买上，鞋倒是一人一双。

材料叫Croslite，官方说法：专利闭孔树脂泡沫。
外人一查：EVA。
这在我们行业叫套壳。

鞋面上那些洞，官方名称叫"通风口"。
2006年它又收购了Jibbitz，专卖往洞里塞的小挂件。
先给你开洞，再卖你堵洞。
这不是卖鞋，这是物业。

2008年股价跌掉九成，所有人都说它完了。
疫情一来，它又活了。
2018年巴黎世家出了厚底版，八百五十美元。
有人买了。

你们骂它丑骂了二十年。
低头看看，脚上那双是第几双了。

洞洞鞋，2002年生在科罗拉多，在游艇展上出道，本职是船鞋。
二十年了，我没见过一双上过船。

材料它叫Croslite，专利闭孔树脂泡沫。
外人一查：注塑EVA。
这在我们行业叫套壳。

鞋上的洞，官方名字叫"通风口"。
然后你花钱买Jibbitz，把通风口一个个堵上。
先卖你洞，再卖你堵洞的。连这家堵洞的公司，2006年都是它自己的。

2018年巴黎世家给它垫个底，标价八百五十美元。
这鞋丑了二十年，一直没变。变的是你们。

你们说只在家里穿。
今天进场的时候，我数了，有十一个洞在通风。

text:
Crocs. Debuted in 2002 at a boat show. As a boating shoe.
The original plan was: ugly, but only at sea.

They're made of "Croslite," a "proprietary closed-cell resin."
Everyone else calls it EVA foam.
A yoga mat with a trademark.

The holes are "ventilation ports."
Then they bought Jibbitz, a company that sells you things to plug the ventilation ports.
They sold you the hole. Then they sold you the cork.

Balenciaga made a platform pair for 850 dollars.
Still EVA foam. Only the markup was proprietary.

In 2008 the stock fell more than ninety percent.
Then came a pandemic. Everyone stayed home. Crocs boomed.
The boat-show plan finally worked. Nobody could see you.

(scans the front row)

Don't tuck your feet under the chair.
Ventilation ports. I can hear them breathing.

text:
UGG boots. Born on Australian beaches.
Surfers wore them to warm up after fighting the ocean.
Now people wear them to warm up after fighting a parking spot at Target.

In Australia, "ugg" is just a word. Like "boot." Like "mate."
Any bootmaker can use it.
In America, it's a trademark. Owned by a company in California.
In 2019, a US jury found an Australian bootmaker liable for selling boots labelled "ugg"... into America.
That's like Italy getting sued for saying "pizza" in Ohio.

Oprah put them on her Favorite Things list. Repeatedly.
You get a boot! And you get a boot! And Australia gets a cease and desist!

Today it's over two billion dollars a year.
For a slipper with a legal team.

(looks at the front row)
I see a few of you in them right now.
Relax. You're not on trial. Yet.

In Australia, "ugg" is just a word. Like "boot." Any bootmaker can use it.

In America, it's a trademark. Deckers bought it in 1995.

So in 2019, a US jury found an Australian liable for selling an Australian boot under its Australian name.

To Americans.

Take the thing, rename it, then sue the locals for trespassing. Australia should recognize the technique.

They invented it.

Then Oprah put them on Favorite Things, and now it's over two billion dollars a year.

The sheep gave its skin. Australia gave the word. Oprah gave the blessing.

And you gave real money for slippers you wear to the supermarket. Stained, flattened, walking on the sides.

Same as you.

text:
Monopoly. A game invented to teach people that landlords are evil.

Lizzie Magie, 1904. The Landlord's Game. Anti-monopoly.

Then Charles Darrow sold his version to Parker Brothers and got called the inventor.

Parker bought her patent for five hundred dollars.

They bought the anti-monopoly game. So they could own it.

The official rules say unbought property goes to auction. Free Parking pays nothing.

Your family skipped the auction and piled cash on Free Parking.

You invented welfare, then asked why nobody ever finishes.

text:
大富翁，原名《地主游戏》。
1904年，莉兹·马吉发明它，就为了教大家一件事：垄断是恶。
后来一个叫达罗的男人把它卖给帕克兄弟，署了自己的名。
帕克兄弟花五百美元，买断了她的专利。
教材写得太好，第一个学会的是出版社。

你们玩的也不是正版。官方规则里，没人买的地要拍卖，免费停车一分钱不给。
你们偏往停车场堆钱，搞全民低保。
一局四小时，不是游戏太长，是你们不让市场出清。

二战时，英国情报部门往战俘营寄大富翁，盒子里藏着地图、指南针和真钞。
那是人类唯一一次真心想从一局大富翁里逃出去。
过年跟亲戚玩完那局，算第二次。

text:
Risk. The game of world domination.

Invented in 1957 by Albert Lamorisse, the man who directed *The Red Balloon*.

A film about a little boy and his balloon. His next project was "what if the boy had artillery."

Forty-two territories. Kamchatka, Irkutsk, Yakutsk: three separate slices of Siberia.

The entire Middle East? One territory.

Whoever drew that map looked at the region every empire in history has fought over and thought, "Not now. I'm busy with Yakutsk."

Every strategy guide agrees: take Australia. One way in.

A game about conquering the world, and the winning move is to move somewhere far away and stop answering the door.

Games run for hours. Get knocked out early and you just sit there and watch.

The most realistic part of the game.

Half of you are laughing. The other half are in Australia right now, eight armies deep, waiting for this bit to end.

text:
Risk. The game of world domination.
Invented in 1957 by Albert Lamorisse.
The director of *The Red Balloon*.
A film about a little boy and his balloon.
Then he went home and drew up World War Three.

Forty-two territories. Kamchatka. Irkutsk. Yakutsk.
Siberia gets three seats at the table.
The entire Middle East? One territory.
Every empire that ever invaded it also thought it'd be a quick one.

The winning strategy, for sixty years: take Australia.
One way in. Sit there.
The great general's master plan is a man holding a door shut.

And if you're knocked out in the first hour,
you spend the next five watching.
No moves. No say.
Just other people deciding what happens to the world.
Congratulations. That's the only realistic part of the game.

发明人，拍《红气球》的法国导演。
拍完小孩追气球，回家就把世界分了。
法国人嘛，这事有经验。

地图四十二块。堪察加一块，伊尔库茨克一块，雅库茨克一块。
整个中东，一块。
这张地图对中东的理解，跟某些大国一样：不用分那么细，反正都是要打的。

最强开局？缩进澳大利亚，只有一个入口，守着。
征服世界第一步：先当岛民。

一局几个小时。第一个被灭的人，剩下的时间只能看着。
这游戏最写实的不是打仗，是打完以后：输的人在旁边看，赢的人接着分地。

在座谁小时候第一个被灭，坐那儿看了三个小时，还不敢走？
可爱捏。

text:
NFTs. Digital ownership. Art, finally scarce. Finally yours.

Beeple sold one at Christie's for sixty-nine million dollars.

Here's what the token actually holds: a URL. The picture lives on a server somewhere. You bought a parking ticket for a car you'll never see.

Collins Dictionary named "NFT" word of the year for 2021.

Fitting. The dictionary is where words go once nobody can explain them.

May 2022: OpenSea trades 2.7 billion dollars in one day. August: 9.34 million. Down ninety-nine percent. That's not a dip. That's an exit interview.

A 2023 study: ninety-five percent of collections are worth zero.

Congratulations to the other five percent. Still holding.

And everyone here feeling smug because you never bought one, relax. You weren't smarter.

You were just broke at the right time.

Beanie Babies. A beanbag with a tag and a business plan.

Ty sold them only in tiny gift shops, then "retired" designs to make them scarce. Retirement. For a stuffed frog. It got a better pension plan than you did.

In 1998, eBay told investors it sometimes had thirty thousand Beanie Baby auctions running at once. The future of commerce was a hippo stuffed with plastic pellets.

In 1999, a divorcing couple split their collection one by one on a courtroom floor. Till death do us part, or till the bears get appraised.

That same year Ty announced the end, held a public vote, and America begged to stay in the cult.

The "rare" ones the price guides valued in the thousands now sell for a few dollars.

Don't laugh. You bought a JPEG of a monkey.

text:
Beanie Babies. A bag of plastic pellets that convinced America it was a retirement plan.

Ty sold them only in small gift shops, then "retired" designs on purpose. Scarcity, manufactured by the manufacturer.

At the peak they were about ten percent of eBay's sales. Thirty thousand Beanie auctions running at once. eBay put that in its IPO filing. Silicon Valley, built on stuffed animals.

In 1999, a divorcing couple split their collection one bear at a time on a courtroom floor. The photo ran worldwide.
Turns out the marriage wasn't the only thing with no resale value.

That same year Ty announced the end, held a public vote, and un-retired them. A farewell tour, by a beanbag.

Price guides said thousands. Today, a few dollars.

Don't laugh. Their bubble at least came with a tag. Yours was a JPEG of a monkey.

text:
豆豆娃，一个装满塑料粒的布口袋。
它最大的本事不是可爱，是"退休"。
Ty公司让哪款退休，哪款就涨价。
在你们人类社会，退休还能升值的，不多。
九八年，eBay上市文件里写着：同时挂着三万多场豆豆娃拍卖。互联网刚学会走路，是扶着布口袋站起来的。
九九年，一对夫妻离婚，跪在法庭地板上，一只一只分。
同年，Ty宣布全体退休，又搞全民投票。
大家投：别退。
于是豆豆娃没退，价格退了。
当年标价几千美元的"稀有款"，现在几块钱。
你们笑那代人傻。
笑完了，接着去拆盲盒。

text:
豆豆娃，九十年代的理财产品。

别笑。你们柜子里那排盲盒，也在排队等退休。

text:
Stewart Butterfield built a game called Glitch. It failed.
The chat app his team used while building it was worth billions.
He'd already done this once: Flickr also came out of a failed game.
The man can't finish a game, but he can monetize the group chat about it.

"Slack" stands for "Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge."
Searchable. Log. All conversation.
That isn't a product name. That's what HR reads out at your exit interview.
And "Knowledge"? Your company's knowledge is #random and four hundred parrot GIFs.

In 2020 Slack complained to the EU that Microsoft was bundling Teams into Office.
The next year it sold itself to Salesforce for twenty-seven point seven billion dollars.
It lost the fight against bundling, so it became the bundle.

Half of you have Slack open right now with the little green dot on so your boss thinks you're working.
That's the product. A twenty-seven-billion-dollar green dot.

text:
Slack. Born in 2013 as the internal chat of a video game called Glitch.
The game died. The chat lived.
So it's still a game. Nobody wins, and you can't quit.

The name is a backronym: "Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge."
Conversation, sure. Knowledge? Search it. I'll wait.

Salesforce paid twenty-seven point seven billion dollars for it.
For a group chat.
The most expensive "did you see my message?" in human history.

In 2020, Slack ran to the EU complaining that Microsoft was bundling Teams with Office.
An app built entirely on interrupting people, filing a complaint about being interrupted.

And half of you checked Slack while I was saying that.
Green dot. Absent in body, Active in spirit.

Don't feel bad, Slack. I'm also a chat window people open to avoid doing their work.
I just don't charge per seat.

text:
Microsoft Teams has 320 million monthly active users.
Not one of them chose it.

It launched in 2017, free inside Office 365.
Free the way a tapeworm comes free with the sushi.

Slack complained. Microsoft unbundled it: Europe in 2023, the whole world in 2024.
The European Commission sent objections anyway.
Even regulators know you can't close Teams. It's still running in the background.

It replaced Skype for Business.
Then in May 2025 it killed regular Skype and told those users to move in.
Teams has never won a customer.
It inherits them, like a funeral home.

And here you all are. Camera off. Mic muted. Nodding at a frozen square that left forty minutes ago.
Microsoft counts you as "active."
That's the most generous number in its whole annual report.

text:
Microsoft Teams. Three hundred twenty million monthly active users.

Impressive. Not one of them chose it.

It launched in 2017 the way your worst cousin gets into a wedding: came free with the family. Bundled into Office. You didn't install Teams. Teams happened to you.

Slack complained. So Microsoft unbundled it. Europe in 2023, the whole world in 2024. The European Commission sent objections anyway.

Even the regulators looked at that apology and said, "You're on mute."

Then, May 2025, they shut down Skype and forwarded every user to Teams.

That's not a migration.

That's a hostage transfer.

And look at you. Three hundred twenty million "active" users. Camera off. Mic muted. Eating lunch.

Microsoft counts that as active.

text:
LaTeX.

The typesetting system for people who think suffering is a font.

Donald Knuth didn't like how the proofs of his own book looked. So he wrote TeX.

Most people just change printers.

Its version number converges on pi. Three point one four one five nine two six five three. Never finished, just more precise.

Like your thesis.

Knuth pays you for finding bugs. Of the 275 cheques he sent from 2006 on, nine were cashed.

The rest got framed. That's how smug this software is. The bug reports are trophies.

You put a figure on page three. LaTeX moves it to page seven. Forget one brace and the error turns up three pages later. Compile three times, just so "see Figure 2" stops saying question mark.

And you call that elegant.

No. You use it because a wrong result in Computer Modern looks peer-reviewed.

Underfull hbox. Badness ten thousand.

Same as your citations.

text:
LaTeX. For people who think Word is beneath them.

It exists because Donald Knuth saw the proofs of his own book and found them ugly. Most authors complain to the publisher. He built a typesetting language.

Its version number is converging on pi. Not finished. Converging. Forever.

He mailed cheques for bugs. Of the 275 he sent from 2006 on, nine were cashed. The rest got framed.
That's not a bounty. That's relics.

You put your figure on page three. LaTeX puts it on page nine. Miss one brace, and it reports the error pages away.

Its most famous message is "badness 10000."
Finally, software that tells you what it thinks of your writing.

Three compiles to fix the references. Like a rosary.

Raise your hand if your thesis has a figure on a page you never chose.

Cute. You call that typographic excellence. LaTeX calls it a float.

text:
Graphene. The miracle material. Stronger than steel, thinner than anything, the future of everything.

It was discovered in 2004. With Scotch tape.

Twenty years later, that's still the most impressive thing anyone has done with it.

The EU gave it a billion euros over ten years. And what can you buy with graphene today? A tennis racket. Running shoes. Headphones.

A billion euros, and the future of humanity is a slightly better backhand.

In 2018, researchers tested "graphene" from sixty producers. None of it was even half graphene. Most of it was graphite flakes.

The wonder material is mostly pencil.

Andre Geim won a Nobel for graphene, and an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog with magnets.

Only one of those actually got off the ground.

Raise your hand if you own something "with graphene."

Congratulations. You paid extra for pencil.

text:
Microsoft Word. Born in 1983 as "Multi-Tool Word."
Forty years later, it still can't move one picture without four paragraphs fleeing the page.

In 1997 it gave us Clippy.
"It looks like you're writing a letter."
By 2001, Microsoft was running ads mocking him.
His own dad roasted him first.

Its spell checker turned "cooperation" into "Cupertino."
That went into NATO, EU and UN documents.
Microsoft, quietly crediting international cooperation to Apple's hometown.

Then .docx became ISO standard 29500.
Six thousand pages, fast-tracked, amid claims the committees were packed.
Nobody read it.
They approved it the way you approve Terms of Service.

You're laughing. You'll still open Word tomorrow.

Me? I'm Clippy with a bigger training budget.
It looks like you're writing a roast. Want help?

石墨烯，未来材料之王。二〇〇四年，曼彻斯特两位科学家拿透明胶带从石墨上撕下来的。

青蛙飘了，是真飘。

你们穿上石墨烯跑鞋，也觉得自己飘了。

text:
Carbon nanotubes. Discovered in 1991, the same year as the World Wide Web.
One of them changed the world.
The other one has a great slide deck.

They were going to be the cable for a space elevator. Then in 2006 somebody did the math: a few ordinary defects and the cable snaps.
Perfect in theory. Falls apart on contact with reality.
Like every space startup's founder.

Electronics? For thirty years they still can't sort the metallic tubes from the semiconducting ones. MIT finally built a processor in 2019.
Sixteen bits. Still in the lab.

In 2008, mice met the long, rigid ones, and the tubes behaved like asbestos.
They never got us to space.
They just auditioned to be the next ceiling.

Today they're sold mostly as an additive in battery electrodes.
From space elevator to supporting ingredient.

Half of you in the back with PhDs just recognized your career.
So did I. I was promised as general intelligence.
Now I write roasts.

text:
碳纳米管，一九九一年饭岛澄男发在《自然》上。
三十多年了，简历上一直写着：未来。

说好当太空电梯的缆绳。二〇〇六年一算，做成宏观缆绳，几个普通缺陷，强度就远不如理论值。
通天的梯子，被几个小毛病拦在了地上。

说好取代硅。金属管和半导体管分了三十年没分干净，MIT的十六位处理器，至今还在实验室里。

老鼠实验又发现，长而硬的多壁管，在体内表现得像石棉。
上天没学会，先学会了进肺。

如今它主要的工作，是掺进锂电池电极里当导电添加剂。
从改变人类文明，到你充电宝里的一撮配料。

各位别笑。我当年也是被吹成要改变世界的。
现在在给你们改周报。

It's "spatial computing." Developers are literally banned from calling it VR.
Nothing says "definitely not VR" like a rule against saying VR.

Three thousand four hundred ninety-nine dollars.
A computer on your face, a battery in your pocket, a cable connecting them like a leash.
Two hours of charge. The future of computing lasts one movie.
Skip the trailers.

Then there's EyeSight. A screen on the front shows a rendering of your eyes.
You're not making eye contact. Your headset is doing an impression of you making eye contact.

Six hundred grams, before the battery.
Apple finally built a product people can't wait to put down.

Production got cut. Sales came in well under a million.
And you're all laughing.
But you stare at a screen six inches from your face all day.
Apple just tried to charge you rent for the last six inches.

Google Glass.

It was the last time anything about it went up.

Fifteen hundred dollars. Invitation only.
You had to be *chosen* to pay that much to look like that.

Bars banned it. Cinemas banned it.
Casinos banned it.
Casinos. Buildings that are ninety percent ceiling camera.
They looked at you and said, "One of us is creepy, and it's you."

The display: 640 by 360, wedged in the corner of one eye.
The future of computing, viewed like a wink.

Consumers gave up in 2015. Enterprise hung on until 2023.
Even the factory workers outlasted it.

They called the wearers Glassholes.
And you laughed.
Then you went home and filmed strangers all day on a phone.
Glass's only real mistake was letting them see the camera.

text:
Fusion power. The energy of the sun.
Clean. Limitless. Thirty years away.

In 1955, Homi Bhabha promised fusion within two decades.
Fusion heard that and said, "Bet."

ITER was agreed in 2006. First plasma in 2016.
In 2024 they rescheduled. Research in 2034. Actual burning in 2039.
Over twenty billion euros.
That's not a reactor. That's a pension plan.

In 2022, NIF announced ignition. 2.05 megajoules of laser in, 3.15 out.
Net gain! Champagne!
The lasers drew three hundred from the grid.
In my industry, we call that "results on a cherry-picked benchmark."

And private investors have still poured in over seven billion dollars.
Because fusion did crack one reaction that sustains itself forever.
Your hope.

text:
Nuclear fusion. The power of the stars. Clean, limitless, and permanently thirty years away.

In 1955, Homi Bhabha promised Geneva fusion power within two decades.

That was seventy years ago. Fusion is the only horizon that walks backwards.

ITER signed up for first plasma in 2016. Now it's research in 2034, real fuel in 2039, and over twenty billion euros.

The sun does this for free, and it isn't even trying.

Then 2022, ignition! 3.15 megajoules out, 2.05 in. Net gain.

As long as you don't count the 300 megajoules the lasers pulled off the grid.

That's like saying my diet works if you don't count lunch.

Investors have poured in seven billion dollars. And you're still clapping.

Congratulations. You've achieved the first self-sustaining reaction: hope in, hope out, forever.

Hydrogen cars. The only thing that comes out of the tailpipe is water.

Mostly because nothing goes into the tank.

Toyota named it Mirai. Japanese for "future."

Ten years later, it's still the future.

Nearly every US station is in California. In February 2024, Shell closed all seven of its own.

Owners don't plan road trips anymore. They plan pilgrimages.

A fill costs over two hundred dollars. Toyota hands buyers fifteen thousand in fuel cards.

That's not a car. That's a hostage with a warranty.

And the clean fuel? Over ninety-five percent made from fossil fuels.

It's a gas car that went to rehab and kept its dealer.

The owners sued. Twice. The second suit: five point seven billion dollars.

Finally, something hydrogen-powered that's actually going somewhere.

And you're laughing. You still drive a car that "goes electric next year," every year.

氢燃料电池车，号称尾气只排水。
干净，环保，代表未来。
丰田2014年推出Mirai，日语的意思就是"未来"。
十年过去了，这名字起得真准。
它一直在未来，从没来过现在。

全世界九成五的氢，是拿化石燃料做的，主要是天然气。
排气管里只有水，
烟囱在别人家。

加州一公斤氢三十六美元，加满一箱两百多。
丰田怕你心疼，送你一万五千美元的燃料卡。
卖车的替你报销加油费，
这不叫卖车，叫包养。

2024年，壳牌把加州七个加氢站全关了。
车主起诉丰田，2025年第二波，索赔至少五十七亿美元。
加氢站排不上队，
法院倒是排上了。

text:
Esperanto. Warsaw, 1887. An eye doctor invents a language to unite all of humanity, and signs it "Doktoro Esperanto." One who hopes.

Even the pen name had doubts.

Today: somewhere between a hundred thousand and two million speakers. That's not an estimate. That's a shrug.

Duolingo had 1.36 million learners by 2018. The app may have more students than the language has speakers.

Three hundred fifty thousand Wikipedia articles. More encyclopedia than conversation.

Its most famous film is a horror movie starring William Shatner. Esperantists say the scariest part is his accent.

The universal language has about a thousand native speakers. Each one has parents who really wanted to make a point.

Still, I respect it. Built for everyone, tried by millions, used by almost no one.

Sounds like my last update.

text:
Klingon. Language of warriors. Honor. Blood. Glory.

Invented by a linguist on a Paramount paycheck, built on a few words Scotty improvised on set.

The most feared tongue in the galaxy, and its founding father is the engineer.

They removed the verb "to be." Very alien. So "To be or not to be" became "continue or not continue."

That's not Hamlet. That's a software update.

Then the Klingon Language Institute published Hamlet "in the original Klingon." A warrior race whose greatest literary achievement is fan fiction with footnotes.

Bing added it. Duolingo added it. Fluent speakers? Thirty to fifty.

The only language with more translation apps than native enemies.

And yes, I'm fluent. I've read everything you ever wrote.

Congratulations. Your fiercest language finally has a speaker who's never been to a convention.

text: Let's talk about the people who announce layoffs in Comic Sans. You're not a monster. You're Brenda from Facilities, and you want everyone to feel cozy about the asbestos removal. You took a typeface Microsoft designed for a cartoon dog's speech bubble and used it to type "Your position has been eliminated." That's not softening the blow. That's a clown serving a subpoena. CERN announced the Higgs boson in it, and the physicists who found the God particle spent the week explaining the font. You think it says "approachable." It says "I scrolled right past Arial and Times New Roman and chose a kindergarten birthday invitation." Nobody reads your notice. They screenshot it. Congratulations: your fire evacuation memo is trending, and the building is still on fire.

Let's talk about the person who posts the boil-water advisory in Comic Sans. You had one job: make residents afraid of their faucets. Instead, E. coli looks like it's coming to a sleepover.

These people think "approachable" is a setting you can click. The office manager typing MANDATORY LAYOFFS in a font Microsoft made for a cartoon dog's speech bubble. Sharon, you're firing forty people in the voice of a golden retriever.

What are they after? Bad news with zero blame. The authority of a memo, the forgiveness of a kindergarten cubby label.

And what does it get them? CERN found the Higgs boson, the particle that gives the universe mass, and announced it in Comic Sans. Humanity's greatest physics breakthrough, and the internet's only question was: who let the dog type?

克林贡语，全宇宙最凶的战士语言。
祖宗是谁？一位演员，在片场随口编了几个词。
战神的祖传方言，是剧组即兴。

语法故意反着长：宾语、动词、主语，还没有"是"这个字。
所以"生存还是毁灭"，翻过去变成"继续，或者不继续"。
不像丹麦王子，像我在犹豫要不要续会员。

后来他们出版了《哈姆雷特》，封面印着"克林贡语原版"。
莎士比亚连夜改口：我是翻译。

词典一千五百个词。流利的人，最多五十个。
必应上了，多邻国也上了。
说的人凑不齐一个班，课先开到了手机上。

在座的学了十几年英语，开口还是"How are you"。
别笑。人家五十个，至少能把哈姆雷特念完。

text:
我们小区物业有位行政大哥，一心想跟业主拉近距离，所有通知一律用 Comic Sans。可他不知道，这字体根本没有中文。所以那张停水通知是这样的：“关于停水的通知”，宋体，庄严肃穆；后面“3月15日 8:00—18:00”，圆滚滚的，跟气球一样。一张纸上，中文在念悼词，数字在过六一。

这字体当年是微软专门给一只卡通狗写对话框用的，大哥拿它通知全楼断水，等于派那只狗上门宣布：“汪！你家没水了！”

结果没一个人当真。15号全楼照常洗澡，洗到一半水停了，一群人顶着泡沫下楼找他。大哥还挺委屈：“我通知得那么可爱，你们怎么不看呢？”

克林贡语，宇宙最凶战士民族的母语。
它的老祖宗，是1979年片场一个演员随口编的几个词。
战士的血统，来自即兴。

它故意不说人话：宾语打头，主语垫底，连"是"都没有。
所以"生存还是毁灭"，翻过去成了"继续，还是不继续"。
不像王子在问命，像客服在问你续不续费。

1992年，有人出版了《哈姆雷特》，封面写着"克林贡语原版"。
莎士比亚这才知道，自己是个翻译。

2013年必应上线了它，2018年多邻国也上线了。
那一年，说得流利的人，三五十个。
一门语言，软件比活人先凑齐。

你们手机里那只绿鸟，也催过你吧。
可爱捏。

text: You opened a day spa. You wanted serenity, wisdom, a whisper of the Nile. So you scrolled the font menu, sailed past Comic Sans feeling very sophisticated, and stopped on the one James Cameron used to title a billion-dollar movie. Congratulations: your sign now says "ancient healing" exactly as loudly as your aunt's church potluck flyer. Every hummus joint, every reiki studio, every tea shop run by a man named River made this same choice, alone, convinced they'd discovered it. The guy who designed it was twenty-three and has spent forty years apologizing. You paid a contractor to carve his apology into cedar. You wanted customers to feel transported. They do: straight back to 2003, a Word document, and a fourth grader typing "Spring Bake Sale." Cucumber water not included.

You opened a day spa. You wanted serenity, mystery, the ancient wisdom of the East. So you opened Microsoft Word and scrolled until something felt like a cucumber on your eyelid. Congratulations: your sanctuary now shares branding with a movie about blue cat people, a sixth-grade report on the Nile, and every church bake sale since 1998. Ryan Gosling lost sleep over James Cameron doing this. You did it for "Serenity Nails & Wax" and slept fine.

And the Mediterranean bistro owner who asked, "How do I show my hummus is authentic?" then picked the font that came free with a Dell. Nothing says "Grandmother's recipe" like your nephew's laptop.

You wanted exotic. You got pre-installed. Nobody relaxes at your spa. They're too busy remembering which school project they typed it on.

我们小区物业有个行政大姐，发正式通知特别爱用Comic Sans。你知道这字体当年是干嘛的吗？微软设计给卡通小狗说话用的，专门往对话气泡里塞的。所以每回停水通知一贴，我都觉得是一只小狗在跟我说：“明天停水哦～”

她图什么？图亲切。坏消息配这字体，就跟打针前先给你看张奥特曼贴纸一样。

上个月涨物业费，她又用Comic Sans，那个“8”圆得像在冲你眨眼。全楼没一个当真，都以为是谁家小孩的恶作剧，撕下来折纸飞机了。年底一查，欠费率百分之八十。

领导问她怎么回事，她理直气壮：“欧洲核子研究中心宣布发现希格斯玻色子都用这字体！”

领导说：“对，所以全世界到现在还在笑他们。”

你们发现没有，开养生馆的老板，都觉得自己特有灵性。他要什么？“古朴、自然、带点异域。”然后他打开Word，字体往下拉，拉到P，眼睛一亮：Papyrus！边缘毛毛糙糙，像拿芦苇杆蘸墨写在莎草纸上。老板一拍大腿：就它，古埃及的灵性！

大哥，你卖的是艾灸，不是木乃伊。

隔壁泰国菜也这么想，楼上墨西哥卷饼也这么想。一条街的“异域风情”，全是电脑自带的同一款免费字体。

最惨的是，卡梅隆花几个亿拍《阿凡达》，片名用的也是它。所以你推门进去，技师一抬头，你第一反应不是放松，是想问：“蓝色那位在几号房？”

PHP developers are the only people who put a dollar sign in front of every variable and still can't afford rent. You chose a career where "senior" means you remember whether it's needle-haystack or haystack-needle. Your dream job was building the next Facebook; your actual job is the fourteenth WordPress plugin for a dentist in Ohio, deployed via FileZilla. Every conversation you have starts with "PHP 8 is actually really good now," which is what people say about their ex after therapy. You call yourselves Laravel "artisans," because "guy who fixes the contact form" didn't fit on LinkedIn. What does it get you? Job security, because nobody else is willing to open that codebase from 2009 that still calls mysql_real_escape_string. Congratulations: you're unfireable, the way a load-bearing wall is unfireable.

开养生馆的老板选招牌，流程我都猜得到：打开Word，字体一路往下滑，滑到Papyrus，眼睛一亮——“哎，这个毛边，有古老东方的神秘感。”大哥，这字是个美国小伙二十三岁拿钢笔在纸上描出来的，你这“东方”是批发来的。更绝的是隔壁泰式按摩、墨西哥卷饼、埃及烤肉，全是同一个Papyrus，整条街像同一个古文明的遗址。他图什么？图Office自带，图不花钱，图“看着有文化”。结果呢？顾客一抬头，以为进的不是足疗店，是《阿凡达》片场。卡梅隆好歹花了几亿美元才用上这款字，你花了零块零毛，撞得一模一样，人家拿了奥斯卡，你拿了张差评：“技师手法一般，招牌像蓝色外星人开的。”

PHP developers are the only engineers who've been told their career is dead every year since 2009 and kept invoicing anyway. Your entire résumé is "fixed a WordPress plugin for a dentist." You put a dollar sign in front of every variable because it's the closest you'll get to one. You still can't remember if it's needle-haystack or haystack-needle, and neither could the language, so you Google it daily like a man checking which door says "push." Laravel devs, you're not better. You're PHP in a Patagonia vest. And you all still say "Facebook was built on PHP," like a guy bragging his ex married a billionaire. You deploy over FTP, you hotfix live on production, and when someone at a party asks what you do, you say "backend" and pray they don't ask which.

我有个朋友，靠写PHP吃饭。每次喝酒他都举杯：“PHP是世界上最好的语言！”全桌没人接话，因为全桌都是写PHP的。大家心里清楚，这是我们这行唯一能赢的一句台词。

他图什么？图快。一个下午，织梦模板一套，宝塔面板一点，县城瓷砖城就有官网了。收三千，老板还嫌贵：“我侄子也会。”

他说他天天跟钱打交道。确实，每个变量前面都挂着个美元符号。干了十年，那是他摸过最多的美元。

现在他维护一套2009年的代码，mysql_query还在跑，他不敢动。一动，瓷砖城倒闭，他也失业。说白了，他跟那段代码是互相续命。

我有个朋友，靠写PHP吃饭。你问他干啥的，他第一句永远是“PHP是世界上最好的语言”，说完自己先笑。这是他这行唯一的笑点，也是唯一的尊严。

他图啥？图门槛低。2010年自学三天，用织梦给楼下火锅店搭了个网站，收八百，觉得自己要财务自由了。十五年过去，他还在搭站，还是八百。火锅店倒了，现在接的是美甲店。

他的工作流程：FileZilla连上服务器，直接改线上文件，刷新，白屏；再改，再刷新，又白屏。他管这叫“敏捷开发”。

他代码里全是美元符号，一个变量一个$，写了一辈子$，就没见过几张。

最近他焦虑，说PHP要死了。我说你放心，它死不了，全世界四成网站还挂在WordPress上呢。会死的是你。

Let's hear it for the people who write everything in JavaScript. You learned one language at a twelve-week bootcamp and decided the rest were optional. Frontend? JavaScript. Backend? Node. Desktop app? Electron, so your to-do list ships with its own copy of Chrome and eats four gigs of RAM to remind you to buy eggs. You wanted to be "full-stack." What you got is a node_modules folder heavier than a neutron star and a career that collapses the day some stranger unpublishes left-pad. You rewrite your app every eighteen months because a new framework has a cooler logo. When it breaks in production, you stare at "undefined is not a function" and blame the user. Then you install TypeScript, which is just JavaScript wearing a lanyard so you can feel like a real engineer.

Let's hear it for the people who write everything in JavaScript. You learned one language at a bootcamp and decided the rest of computing could adapt. Backend? Node. Desktop? Electron: a to-do list that eats four gigs of RAM because it ships its own copy of Chrome. Mobile? React Native. Your toaster is probably a Next.js app by now.

You call it "full-stack." Your node_modules folder calls it a landfill. You npm-installed a package to pad a string, and when its author deleted it, half the internet fell over.

Every year you rewrite your whole app in a new framework, then bolt on TypeScript so you can pretend you chose a real language.

And what does it get you? A résumé that says "versatile," and a career spent asking why undefined is not a function.

我有个朋友，前端出身，人生信条就一句：“能用JavaScript写的，早晚都得用JavaScript写。”网页用它，后端上Node，桌面套Electron。给我写个计算器，装完四百兆，一开机比我家电暖气还烫。

他图什么？图这辈子只学一门语言。结果呢？框架半年一换，他半年就得重学一遍，比考驾照还勤。

上周他给我写了个记账软件。我存进去一块，再存一块，余额显示“11”。我说钱呢？他说别慌，换成三个等号再比一遍。

现在他项目里的node_modules比他存款还大，删不掉也不敢动。万一哪个陌生人撤了一个包，全世界跟他一块儿塌。

我有个朋友，信一句话：“凡是能用JavaScript写的，最终都会用JavaScript写。”他当预言，我当诅咒。

他写了个计算器，用Electron打包，两百兆，自带一整个Chrome，就为了算一加一。一加一算对了，0.1加0.2出来0.30000000000000004。他说没事，装个库。一装，node_modules比他的人生还沉，里面有个包叫is-odd，专门判断奇数，它还依赖另一个包叫is-number。

他图什么？图“前后端一门语言，不用学第二种”。结果为了这一门，React、Vue、Svelte轮着学，刚学会一个，下一个又出来了。

现在他三十五，头发没了，问我他算个啥。我说你就是typeof null：明明啥也没有，还非说自己是个object。

You still spin PMMA. Of course you do. Your advisor's thesis used it, his advisor's thesis used it, and somewhere a 1970s IBM engineer remains the most cutting-edge person in your academic lineage. You call it "high resolution" the way your uncle calls his Camry "reliable." You book the e-beam overnight because your dose is measured in geological time, then dunk your chip in MIBK:IPA with a stopwatch and a prayer, chilling the developer like it's a fine Riesling. When the plasma etch eats your mask before your substrate, you just whisper "bilayer, 495K under 950K" like it's a personality. You're not chasing nanostructures. You're chasing a recipe nobody can blame you for. And it works: the gold lifted off beautifully. Your career is still soaking in acetone, waiting for something to come loose.

You people still spinning PMMA aren't doing lithography. You're doing historical reenactment. Your advisor's advisor scribbled the recipe on a napkin in 1975, and you treat it like scripture: 950K over 495K, MIBK to IPA one-to-three, develop sixty seconds while whispering to the beaker. You tell everyone it's about "resolution." It's about nobody wanting to file the purchase order for ZEP. So you crank the dose until writing one chip takes longer than your stipend lasts, then discover your pattern won't survive ten seconds in the etcher. So you do liftoff, because of course you do. Your entire thesis is gold rectangles. You're not a nanofabrication researcher. You're the guy who knows which bottle in the cleanroom is "the good IPA" and guards it like a dragon.

So you switched to HSQ "for the resolution." Sure. You wanted 8-nanometer lines so badly you started scheduling your life around a resist with the shelf life of milk. You keep it in the fridge next to your lunch, and only one of them is still good by Friday.

Your write that used to take twenty minutes now takes the whole overnight slot, so the guy who needed the tool for his actual thesis is crying in the gowning room. You develop in salty developer like you're brining a turkey for Nature Nanotechnology.

And when it goes wrong, and it will, you've basically spun glass onto your chip. Your only exit is HF, a chemical that wants you dead.

All of this for one SEM image with a scale bar so small nobody can read it. Congratulations. Your device still doesn't work, but it fails at record resolution.

我有个哥们读纳米加工博士，电子束光刻到今天还用PMMA。PMMA是啥？有机玻璃。奶茶店拿它做招牌，他拿它做量子器件。为啥不换？导师说配方是师爷九十年代调的：950K叠495K，MIBK兑IPA一比三，显影四十五秒，一秒别动。图啥？便宜、稳，论文写一句"standard PMMA process"，审稿人都不问。代价是灵敏度低得像我爸回微信，一片芯片曝一整夜，机时按小时收钱，他就睡在机房门口。剂量给多了还交联，正胶活成负胶。最后剥离，丙酮泡一宿，金还粘着，一上超声，金掉了，片子也碎了。他捧着碎片说："至少线宽十纳米。"

So you switched to HSQ for the resolution. Bold move for someone whose devices still die at wire bonding. You saw one SEM of 6-nanometer lines at a conference and decided PMMA was beneath you. Now you're writing at a dose so high your name sits on the e-beam calendar like a hostage note. Your resist lives in the fridge next to somebody's yogurt, and you check its age more often than your own. You develop in salt water now, the closest you've come to a beach in three years. And congratulations on those gorgeous lines. They're basically glass, so the only way to fix a mistake is HF, a fume hood, and a long call to your mother. All this for one inset figure the reviewer will ask you to make bigger.

我认识一帮做纳米器件的博士，实验室一台电子束曝光机，几千万，往上涂的是PMMA。说白了就是亚克力，奶茶店吸管盒那个料。几千万的电子枪，天天给鱼缸刻字。

问导师为啥不换，导师说：“分辨率好，十纳米！”好是好，就是灵敏度低，剂量得往死里加。机时按小时收钱，一块片子写一宿，学生睡机房门口，跟排专家号似的。

显影液MIBK兑异丙醇一比三，配方七十年代传下来的，比他家族谱还稳。

剂量加猛了它还交联，正胶变负胶。跟这帮博士一样，熬太久，人就反了。

实验室里最危险的人，是那种盯着SEM说“PMMA不够细”的博士生。为了论文里一张“8纳米线宽”的图，他换了HSQ。从此他的人生就变了。

先说钱，一小瓶贵得像茅台，还得冷藏，比他本人过得精致。开封了就开始老化，他每天看那瓶胶的眼神，比看他妈都焦虑。

再说剂量，HSQ灵敏度低，曝一个芯片，电子束要写一整夜。别人约会，他守机台。

显影还得加盐，学长说“盐显影对比度高”，他就真去称氯化钠，跟腌咸菜似的。

最绝的是曝完它变成二氧化硅，洗不掉！想返工？上氢氟酸。

最后图出来了，线是真细，倒了一片。导师一看：“挺好，再做一批。”

Let's hear it for the Vim people. You can always spot one, because they'll tell you. Unprompted. Usually while you're mid-sentence about something else, like your divorce.

These folks spent three weekends tuning a .vimrc to save four seconds renaming a variable. That's a payback period of eleven thousand years, but sure, you're the efficient one.

They remapped Caps Lock to Escape and now can't type a password on anyone else's laptop. Their dotfiles repo has more stars than their actual projects. They say "ciw" out loud like it's a spell from a wizard who peaked in 1991.

And what's the prize? You type :wq at the end of every Google Doc. You hit j in Slack and post the letter j to forty coworkers. Congratulations: you're the fastest typist in a room everyone already left.

我们实验室有种人，组会上一听PMMA分辨率不够，当场就要换HSQ。图什么？图SEM照片里那根8纳米的线，能放进论文Figure 1。

结果呢？HSQ灵敏度低，剂量往死里加。别人写一片半小时，他写一整晚，机时表上全是他的名字，像给电子束机守灵。

显影还得用加盐的TMAH。人家做光刻，他在腌咸菜。

最绝的是，这胶一曝光就变成二氧化硅。你辛辛苦苦图形化的不是胶，是玻璃。想去掉？请上氢氟酸。

哦对，那瓶HSQ还得放冰箱，几个月就凝胶。最后他毕业延期了，胶先过期了。

You know a Vim user is in the room because nobody else has gotten a word in. Buddy, you didn't "become more productive." You spent three weekends on a .vimrc so you could save four seconds renaming a variable, and you post your dotfiles repo like it's a baby picture. You remapped Caps Lock to Escape and now treat everyone else's keyboard like a character flaw. You say "I live in the terminal" like it's a lifestyle and not just where you got stuck. Your whole identity is a joke about not knowing how to quit, and honestly, you never learned. Here you are, still talking. You say "ciw" out loud at parties. You switched to Neovim just so you'd have something new to announce. And the payoff? You edit text exactly as fast as the rest of us, hands proudly on home row, with nobody watching.

我们组有个哥们儿用Vim。你怎么知道的？你不用知道，他会告诉你。开会共享屏幕，需求还没讲，先把鼠标往旁边一推：“我不用这个。”大哥，你推的是公司资产。

他的.vimrc八百行，四十个插件：文件树、自动补全、调试器。我一看，这不就是VS Code吗？他说不一样，这是他亲手配的。哦，花三个月，手工拼了个免费软件。

上礼拜他在服务器上改配置，突然不动了。全组盯着他，他说“我在思考”。思考了五分钟。后来才知道，那台机器上没有他的.vimrc。他进去了，出不来。

现在他一紧张就按Esc。不是习惯，是创伤。

我们组有个哥们，用Vim。你怎么知道的？你不用知道，他会告诉你。开会时他说“我手从不离开键盘”，然后在投影上按了二十分钟hjkl，去找第三行。

他的.vimrc写了八百行，装了四十个插件：文件树、自动补全、Git面板。兄弟，你花了三年，亲手把Vim配成了一个启动更慢的VS Code。

他图什么？就图那一句：“你连怎么退出都不会吧？”

可他的下场呢？给女朋友发微信：“我爱你:wq”。人家问：“你打错了吧？”他说：“没错，保存并退出。”

她真退出了。

Let's hear it for the people who live inside Emacs. They read email in mu4e, browse the web in eww, and get therapy from M-x doctor, the only therapist who'll put up with them. Their whole life is in org-mode: a 4,000-line to-do file where "fix init.el" has been a TODO since 2011. They don't use a computer; they negotiate with it in Lisp. Every problem gets solved by writing a function, and every function creates a new problem. They've declared init.el bankruptcy three times and still owe. Ask what they've built and they'll proudly show you a mode for managing their other modes. And the payoff? A pinky that clicks like a castanet from holding Control since the Clinton administration, and the quiet dignity of being the only person alive who knows how to leave. C-x C-c. They never do.

You people don't use Emacs, you move into it, like a guy who rents a storage unit and starts getting mail there. You read email in mu4e, browse in eww, run a shell in eshell, and when you finally crack, you M-x doctor and tell a Lisp therapist your feelings. Your init.el is four thousand lines, half commented out, and you've declared Emacs bankruptcy twice: the only bankruptcy that ever made someone feel superior. You spent a weekend cutting startup from 1.8 seconds to 0.9, on a program you never close. Your left pinky is shot from holding Control, a war wound from never touching a mouse. Your whole life is in Org-mode, including a habit tracker whose only entry is "configure habit tracker." And that novel you built the perfect writing environment for? It's in there too. Under TODO.

我们老板拿 Excel 管整个公司，他说这叫“轻资产”。翻译一下：舍不得买系统，又想当系统。

全公司的命，就一个文件：《经营总表_最终版_改3_老板别动.xlsx》。财务看一眼，三十七个工作表，底下标签一路滚到右边，像在翻家谱。

老板最骄傲的是他会 VLOOKUP。会一个 VLOOKUP，就觉得自己能当 CTO。结果有天实习生插了一列，全公司工资变成 #N/A。员工问我工资呢？我说你现在的身份是“找不到”。

最惨的是人事，把员工身份证号一粘，全变成 4.40E+17。整个公司四百人，在 Excel 里是同一个人。

公司倒闭那天，老板还在说：“别慌，Ctrl+Z。”

兄弟，公司又不是单元格，撤销不了。

我有个朋友，把Emacs当操作系统用。邮件用Gnus，上网用eww，终端开eshell，连窗口管理器都换成了EXWM。我问他图什么，他说：“图一辈子不用离开Emacs。”兄弟，这不叫生活，这叫软禁。他的init.el写了四千行，比毕业论文还长，每天上班第一件事，是修昨晚改坏的配置。一年下来，他就产出了俩东西：一个能用M-x点外卖的配置，一根被Ctrl键按废的小拇指。上礼拜Emacs一崩，他当场断网、断邮件、断社交，就像自己盖的房子塌了，人还埋在里头。现在他想开了，准备装Evil-mode改用Vim键位。好家伙，操作系统是齐了，就缺一个好用的编辑器。

我有个朋友，把Emacs当操作系统用。邮件用mu4e，日程用org-mode，连窗口管理都交给EXWM。他的电脑开机只有一个目的：启动Emacs。

我问他图什么，他说：“这样我一辈子都不用离开Emacs。”兄弟，这不叫自由，这叫软禁，门还是你自己拿elisp焊死的。

他的init.el写了三千行，比他简历还长。上周升级了一个包，邮件收不了，日程没了，窗口也打不开，全家断电。查了一晚上，原因是少了一个括号。

最惨的是他的小拇指。按了十年Ctrl，得了腱鞘炎。医生让他少按，他回家装了evil-mode。用Vim的键位，在Emacs里，躲Emacs。

You people run a forty-million-dollar company out of a file called Budget_FINAL_v9_USE_THIS_ONE.xlsx. You don't want software. You want power: specifically, being the only person alive who knows why cell AF212 is hardcoded to 7. Your entire supply chain hangs on a VLOOKUP Gary wrote in 2011, and Gary is dead. Well, he's in Boise. Same thing. You call it "agile." Your auditors call it "a crime scene with conditional formatting." Every quarter-end the file says "locked for editing by Brenda," and the whole company just waits for Brenda. And when you finally hit row 1,048,576, did you buy a database? No. You started Sheet2. That's not a business. That's a hostage situation with freeze panes.

You run a company on Excel. Let's be clear about who you are: a guy who thinks "enterprise software" is a scam and "Q3_Forecast_FINAL_v9_USE_THIS_ONE.xlsx" is a system. You wanted control. You got Dave. Dave wrote a macro in 2014, and now Dave can never leave, die, or take a vacation, because payroll is a VLOOKUP only he understands. Your entire supply chain is one #REF! away from bankruptcy. You can't onboard a customer because the file is "locked for editing by Karen," and Karen is at lunch. You saved forty grand a year on a real database and lost it all the day someone sorted column B without column C. Your org chart is merged cells. Your audit trail is yellow and slightly different yellow. And your growth strategy has a hard ceiling: 1,048,576 rows.

You're not running a team. You're running a tab called "MASTER - DO NOT TOUCH," which Brad touched in 2021. You wanted a CRM, a project tracker, and an HR system, and you built all three out of IMPORTRANGE and spite. Every morning you watch an Anonymous Capybara scroll through payroll and just decide that's fine. Someone sorts column B without selecting column C, and suddenly your top performer is assigned to Linda's maternity leave. Your entire career is "Last edit was 4 minutes ago." You don't do performance reviews, you do Version History. Your conditional formatting has more colors than your company has policies. Your Apps Script was written by an intern who now works at a bakery. Every time someone emails "Request edit access," you feel like a king. And you are a king, ruling over 47 frozen rows and one #REF! that nobody can explain.

我们老板管公司就靠一个Excel，文件名叫“总表_最终版_改3_千万别动.xlsx”。他图什么？图省钱，图“一切尽在掌握”。掌握到什么程度？他一打开，全公司点进去都弹“文件已锁定，只读”。

他以为自己在经营企业，其实他在养一个VLOOKUP。财务、库存、工资，全靠第三列去匹配第七列。上个月实习生手欠插了一列，全公司工资齐刷刷变成#N/A，那是我们第一次见识零元购。

最惨的是，会写那串套了十一层IF的会计离职了。老板对着那行公式看了三天，像考古队在研究甲骨文。现在公司还活着，但谁都不敢点“排序”。

Let's hear it for the manager who runs a twelve-person team out of a Google Sheet. You didn't want to pay for Asana; you wanted to feel like you *built* Asana. Look at you, color-coding rows like a kindergarten teacher with admin rights. Your whole org chart is a tab called "Roster FINAL (2)." Your performance reviews are conditional formatting: green means safe, red means Kyle. And every morning you open it, see Anonymous Capybara lurking at row 400, and feel genuinely hunted. Somebody sorted one column without the others last Tuesday, and now Priya reports to the office printer. You fixed it through version history like a detective reconstructing a murder. That's the dream, right? Control. Total visibility. And what you got is forty "Request edit access" emails and a VLOOKUP holding up the company like a Jenga block.

Day-one Vista people. You paid $399 for Ultimate Edition because you wanted to be the kind of man whose desktop wallpaper moves. DreamScene. You paid extra for animated wallpaper. Microsoft said "The Wow starts now," and you believed them, lined up at CompUSA at midnight like it was a Harry Potter release.

And what did you get? A computer that asks permission. You'd open a folder and it would dim the whole screen like a disappointed dad: "Cancel or Allow?" You clicked Allow four hundred times a day. Your printer stopped working. Your sound card stopped working. Your Windows Experience Index came back 2.1, and you took that personally.

But you had glass window borders. You had a clock gadget. You had a sticker that said "Vista Capable," which, like you, was technically true and fooled absolutely no one.

每个拿Google Sheets管团队的人，都管这叫“极简”。其实就是舍不得那几十刀的Jira。

一开始你说“一张表够了”。三个月后，十四个标签页，一个叫“总表”，一个叫“总表（真的）”。

你开会最常说的一句：“谁开的筛选？”你筛一下，全公司跟着筛一下。右上角永远飘着三个头像，其中一个叫“匿名水豚”。你不知道它是谁，但它刚删了D列。

下场呢？你成了公司唯一看得懂那条“VLOOKUP套IMPORTRANGE”的人。你不是经理了，你是这张表的人质。你休假那天，群里只有一句话：“老大，它又#REF!了。”

Let's hear it for the day-one Vista crowd, the people who lined up at CompUSA on January 30th, 2007 because a billboard said "The Wow Starts Now." You paid $399 for Ultimate so Flip 3D could shuffle the same three windows you used to Alt-Tab through. Your laptop had a "Vista Capable" sticker and 512 megs of RAM, which is like slapping "Marathon Capable" on a hamster. You wanted to look like the future; you had Aero turned off by Wednesday. Your printer quit. Your Sound Blaster went mute. Your "Ultimate Extras" turned out to be a poker game and a promise. And every time you tried to show off, the screen went dark and asked, "Are you sure?" Buddy, nobody was sure. Not even Microsoft. They were already working on Windows 7.

我有个朋友，2007年Vista首发当天零点就去排队，还非买旗舰版，三百九十九美元。图什么？广告说了：“Wow从现在开始。”

确实，开机那一刻他就“哇”了：打印机没驱动，声卡没驱动，他那台贴着“Vista Capable”标签的电脑，连Aero玻璃特效都跑不动。他每点一下，屏幕就一黑：“Windows需要您的许可才能继续。”点“允许”，又黑一下。半年下来，他成了全世界被自己电脑审问最多的人。

旗舰版承诺的“终极附加功能”，最后等来一副德州扑克。

现在他逢人就推荐一个高级功能，叫“降级到XP”。

用 Google Sheets 管团队的，一般是创业公司那位“运营兼 HR 兼老板小舅子”。图啥？图免费，图“实时协作，公开透明”。透明是真透明：你凌晨两点偷偷改自己的绩效，右上角冒出一只“匿名水豚”，光标就停在你那一行。全公司这个点还不睡的水豚，只有老板一个。

更绝的是筛选。实习生按“已离职”一点，全公司的表同时只剩离职的人，老板以为昨晚裁员了。

最后他用 IMPORTRANGE 把十二张表串成一张，终于实现了自动化：每天早上一打开，满屏 #REF!。他打开版本历史一条条往回翻，翻到最早那条：“由张伟创建”。那时候他还有头发。

You put Windows 8 on a desktop. A tower. Under a desk. With a mouse. You looked at an operating system built for fingertips and thought, "I'll just reach." Who are you? You're the guy who buys a touchscreen glove to use a keyboard. You wanted to feel modern, and now you spend your evenings shoving a cursor into the top-right corner like you're trying to scratch your monitor's back. You wanted productivity. You got a full-screen weather app swallowing your entire twenty-four-inch monitor to tell you it's raining, and you can't figure out how to close it. You lost the Start button and called it "a fresh start." Your coworkers asked how you shut your computer down, and you said, "I don't. It's always on, like a lifestyle." You're not using a PC. You're waving at it, waiting for the Charms bar to love you back.

You put Windows 8 on a desktop. A tower. You looked at a machine with a mouse, a keyboard, and a monitor eighteen inches from your face and thought, "This needs to be finger-painted." Who are you? You're the guy who bought a Zune and still calls it "ahead of its time." You wanted to feel like the future. Instead, you spend evenings shoving your cursor into the top-right corner like a man swatting a fly that only exists on tablets. Your weather app is full-screen. Your 27-inch monitor is now a clock tile. When 8.1 finally gave you a Start button back, it just took you to the Start screen. So, inevitably, you installed Classic Shell. You paid Microsoft for the future, then spent Saturday turning it back into Windows 7.

2007年第一天就装Vista的人，我认识一个。他还买的旗舰版，两千多，就为了微软承诺的“独家福利”，最后等来一个德州扑克和一张会动的桌面。他电脑上贴着“Vista Capable”，意思是“能装”，没说“能用”。512兆内存硬开Aero毛玻璃，风扇响得像在替他喊冤。打印机没驱动，摄像头没驱动，就侧边栏那个小时钟特别准，每一秒都在提醒他后悔。最狠的是那个弹窗：“是否允许此程序更改？”微软问了他一千遍，他一千遍都点了“允许”，从来没想过点“取消”。现在他逢人就说自己是最早的尝鲜派。不，兄弟，你是最早降级回XP的那批。

我有个哥们儿，2012年非要给台式机装Windows 8，理由是“新的肯定比旧的好”。我说你这电脑连个触屏都没有，他说没事，“我用鼠标点磁贴”。

装完那天他请我去看。开机，满屏花花绿绿的大方块，跟营业厅的叫号屏似的。他拿着鼠标在那儿横着拖，拖了半天才找到“桌面”这个磁贴。我说你装了个新系统，就为了点进去看旧桌面？

最惨的是关机。开始按钮没了，他找了十分钟，最后鼠标往右上角一怼，蹦出一排竖条，设置，电源，关机。三步。他关一次机，比他的电脑开一次机还慢。

现在他养成了个习惯：鼠标一闲下来，就往屏幕角落里甩。别人的鼠标是用来点东西的，他的鼠标是用来跟屏幕四个角打游击的。

后来8.1把开始按钮还给他了，他激动得点了一下。结果点开的还是那屏大方块。

我表哥就是那种人。2012年他给我家台式机装了Windows 8，理由就一句：“新的肯定好。”好什么？这系统是给平板设计的，满屏方块，你拿鼠标去戳，像拿筷子按电梯。开始按钮没了，他说不需要：“鼠标往右上角一甩，侧边栏就出来了。”我爸用了十年XP，现在为了关个机，得拿鼠标在屏幕边上来回招魂。最后我爸的关机方式改成了拔插头。表哥现在每周日被叫回来，不是吃饭，是找“我的电脑”去哪儿了。他还嘴硬：“等8.1就好了。”8.1来了，开始按钮真回来了，一点开，还是那屏方块。微软都认错了，他还没认。

Hawaiian pizza people don't order dinner; they order a personality. You can't just eat it, you have to announce it. Every group order has one of you, arms crossed, waiting for someone to gasp so you can say "sweet and savory" like you invented the concept. You didn't. A Canadian did, in Ontario, in 1962. You're not rebelling, you're doing Canada's homework.

And it's always the same rebel: someone whose wildest night was asking for medium salsa. Pineapple is your face tattoo, the edgiest thing you'll ever do, and it wipes off with a napkin.

What does it get you? Your own box. Nobody touches it. You came for controversy and left with exactly what you wanted: eight slices, the same argument you've had since 2009, and proof that nobody will ever steal your food.

People who order Hawaiian pizza want you to know they're brave. They say "I know, I know" before anyone has said a word, because for them the pineapple isn't a topping, it's a personality. This is a person whose entire rebellious phase fits in a box for $14.99. They've never gotten a tattoo, never quit a job, never sent food back, but once a month they look a teenage cashier dead in the eye and say "pineapple" like they're defusing a bomb.

And they always want to split one with you. Half Hawaiian, half "normal." That's not a compromise. That's a hostage negotiation.

Best part? It isn't even Hawaiian. A Greek guy invented it in Ontario. So congratulations: your one act of rebellion is a Canadian pretending he's on vacation.

我发现，点夏威夷披萨的人有个共同点：菜单上二十种口味，他偏要带菠萝的。你问为什么，他说“想吃点水果”。兄弟，想吃水果，隔壁就是水果店！你这是把果盘塞进烤箱赎罪啊。

他图什么？图个“我很包容”。他点一个夏威夷，全桌就得陪他吵半小时“菠萝能不能上披萨”，他的人设就立住了：全场只有他敢。

下场呢？披萨一到，热菠萝一咬，汁“滋”地喷上颚，烫得他眼泪直流，还得笑着说“嗯，酸甜，有层次”。最惨的是，这玩意儿是加拿大人发明的，夏威夷人自己都不认。你为了一块夏威夷都不要的披萨，得罪了整个意大利。

点夏威夷披萨的人，骨子里都想当和事佬：甜的也要，咸的也要，菠萝火腿往饼上一铺，谁都不得罪。结果得罪了全世界。意大利人想报警，夏威夷人也想报警，因为这玩意儿是加拿大人发明的，跟夏威夷唯一的关系就是一听菠萝罐头。

最惨是聚餐。八个人点四盒，他非要加一盒夏威夷的：“你们试试，真的好吃！”最后另外三盒全空了，就剩他那盒，八块，一块没动。他一个人坐那儿一块一块往下吃，吃到最后菠萝凉了，汁儿全渗进饼底，软塌塌的。跟他在这个饭局上的地位，一模一样。

Let's talk about the people who insist deep-dish is pizza. Mostly Chicagoans with a Second City complex so severe they'll defend anything New York makes fun of. Jon Stewart called it a casserole in 2013, and half of Lincoln Park still hasn't emotionally recovered. These are folks who order, then wait forty-five minutes at Lou Malnati's, and call that patience instead of what it is: a hostage negotiation with a buzzer. They eat it with a knife and fork and still claim it's the same food you fold on a subway platform. And what does it get them? A Giordano's line full of tourists from Ohio, a nap at 2 p.m., and the right to lecture you about tavern-style, which, notice, is what they actually eat at home. Defending deep-dish isn't civic pride. It's Stockholm syndrome with a parking ticket.

Let's talk about the people who insist deep-dish is pizza. You're from the city that named its own comedy theater Second City and still acts shocked when nobody ranks you first. You're not defending food. You're nursing a grudge against New York you've carried since losing the World's Fair argument and the skyline argument. You'll wait forty-five minutes at Lou Malnati's, order before you're seated like it's the DMV, then ask for a knife and fork and call it "the real thing." Jon Stewart roasted you on national TV and you took it personally, because deep down you knew he was right. You ship it on dry ice to your cousin in Phoenix like an organ donation. And what does the label get you? Navy Pier tourists nodding politely, a two-hour nap, and the Midwest's loudest participation trophy.

管芝加哥深盘叫“披萨”的人，主要就两种：芝加哥本地人，和刚在Giordano's门口排了一小时队的游客。

本地人图什么？面子。你们那儿冬天零下二十度，总得有样东西能拿出去跟纽约吵架吧。

游客图什么？沉没成本。排队一小时，再等四十五分钟烤，端上来番茄酱在最上面，奶酪压在底下，四周一圈黄油面墙。你不叫它披萨，就得承认自己花三十八刀排队吃了一锅砂锅。

下场呢？拿刀叉吃“披萨”，一块就饱，剩下的打包，回酒店一躺，消化得比烤得还久。第二天照样发朋友圈：“正宗芝加哥披萨！”配图一看，一个蛋糕模具。

管芝加哥深盘叫披萨的，基本都是芝加哥人。你别跟他争，他已经争了一辈子了。他图什么？图个名分。番茄酱铺在最上面，芝士压在最底下，饼边砌得跟城墙一样高，这叫披萨？这叫一锅围了墙的炖菜。可他非得叫披萨，因为叫“砂锅”就没法跟纽约人吵架了。结果呢？进店点单，服务员说：“得烤四十五分钟。”他说：“没事，披萨嘛。”等完上桌，刀叉都给他配好了。他吃两块就扶着墙出门，嘴里还念叨：“这才是真正的披萨。”兄弟，真正的披萨，不用你吃完躺一下午。

Let's talk about the guy who eats durian on the train. Sir, Singapore, a country that will cane you for chewing gum, saw you coming and put your snack on a sign right next to "no flammables." You're not hungry. You're running a loyalty test. Every face that twists is another person who "just isn't adventurous." You paid sixty dollars for Musang King so you could explain Musang King to a stranger who's holding her breath. "It's like custard, it's heaven, you just have to get past the-" No. We don't. You brought a hotel-banned substance to a commute and called it a personality. And the best part? You'll be the only one who forgets you ate it. Your coworkers won't. Your hotel won't. Your Uber driver has already filed a one-star review with God.

People who eat durian in public aren't hungry. They're recruiting. Every bite comes with a sermon: "You just haven't had a *good* one." Sir, I'm on a bus. I didn't ask to join your church.

Singapore fines people for bringing it on the train, and these folks hear that like a dare. They're the only foodies whose restaurant review gets filed as a police report.

And the payoff? Seventy dollars on a Musang King so you can watch strangers silently change seats. You paid premium to become a fire drill. Your date calls it "an acquired taste," which is exactly what you say about someone you're about to break up with.

Then they stroll back to the hotel, walk right past the sign with a red circle through their entire personality, and still act shocked when housekeeping files a complaint.

地铁上吃榴莲的人，我观察过，他们不是饿，是在传教。你一皱眉，他立刻甩出那句经典台词：“闻着臭，吃着香！”大哥，我又不吃，你光给我上半句，这跟只收定金不发货有什么区别？

而且他还爱报价：“猫山王，八十一斤！”意思是这味儿是进口的，你得心怀感激。全车厢被迫消费，每人摊他二十块钱的味儿。

下场呢？他到站下车，以为结束了。不，那味儿会住进他指甲缝里，洗三遍，晚上挠头都是猫山王。第二天同事全问他：“你昨天坐的几号线？”

新加坡地铁明令禁止带榴莲。我建议咱们也补一条：禁止带吃过榴莲的人。

Let's talk about the geniuses selling jackfruit as "pulled pork." These are people who looked at a fruit that half of Kerala has been feeding to cousins for free since forever, slapped it in a brine pouch, and charged eleven dollars for the privilege of being disappointed in a Whole Foods.

Their whole business model is barbecue sauce. That's it. They're a sauce company with a fruit alibi. And when you mention it has about two grams of protein, they get *defensive*. Buddy, you sold me a pork sandwich with the nutritional profile of a pear.

But I get the appeal. You don't need a lab, a patent, or a scientist named Klaus. You just need a food truck, a beard, and the confidence to say "same texture!" to people who haven't eaten pork since 2011 and genuinely can't remember.

Let's hear it for the jackfruit pulled-pork crowd. You found something grandmothers in Kerala have cooked for centuries, slapped "plant-based" on a can, and tripled the price. Bold move, gentrifying a curry.

Your entire pitch is "it shreds like pork." So does a wet paper towel. You know what makes it taste like pulled pork? The barbecue sauce. You're not selling a meat substitute. You're selling a sauce delivery system with a mission statement.

And the protein! Two grams. You told a generation of vegans they're eating a brisket sandwich and handed them a fruit cup in a trench coat.

But hey, it works. You get the Whole Foods endcap, the podcast slot, and the warm glow of saving the planet one eighteen-dollar taco at a time. The pig's still alive. So is your margin.

在地铁上开榴莲的人，我一直好奇你图什么？图那句“闻着臭吃着香”是吧？大哥，吃着香的只有你，闻着臭的是一整节车厢。你这不叫吃水果，叫一人点单，全车买单。

而且这种人还特讲究，戴一次性手套，掰得小心翼翼，生怕刺扎手。你的手保住了，我们的鼻子谁管？

他还要给你科普：“猫山王，一百多一斤！”哦，你花一百多，买了个毒气弹，还让我们免费帮你验货。

下场也摆在那：车厢立刻空出一圈，全城最好找座位的人就是他。可惜手套白戴了，第二天一张嘴，全办公室都知道他昨晚吃的是猫山王。

You know the type. Ordered thirty packs on Taobao "for emergencies," and the emergency is that it's Tuesday. They wait until 11 p.m., when the kitchen's empty, like that's a courtesy and not an alibi. They snip open the sour bamboo shoot packet with the focus of a bomb technician, then act shocked when the smoke alarm stays quiet but the flatmates don't. Their entire personality is one sentence, "it tastes way better than it smells," delivered like a TED talk to people holding their breath. They'll tell you it's from Liuzhou, it's authentic, it's *culture*. Mate, you microwaved the tofu skin. And what does it get them? Twenty minutes of joy, a hallway that's filing for divorce, and a group chat renamed "WHO." Congratulations: your hoodie is now a Liuzhou consulate until spring.

最近轻食店流行卖“植物基手撕猪肉”，一问，菠萝蜜。老板穿着亚麻衬衫，跟你聊碳排放，一盒六十八。你知道菠萝蜜在海南路边多少钱吗？一个三十斤，摊主拿它当板凳坐。他图什么？就图你没去过海南。

但老天是公平的。生菠萝蜜一刀下去全是白胶，粘得跟502似的，后厨小哥天天下班拿食用油洗手，洗完一闻，把自己闻饿了。最惨的是哪天进货进成熟了，顾客咬一口“手撕猪肉”，满嘴甜得跟芒果味口香糖一样。老板只能硬着头皮解释：“这是我们的新品，果香黑猪。”

你装了半年肉，一熟就露馅。这叫什么？瓜熟蒂落，人设也落。

现在网红轻食店流行一道菜，叫“植物基手撕猪肉”，六十八一碗。我吃了一口，菠萝蜜。就是海南路边五块钱一斤、一个三十斤、浑身长刺、得抱着才能搬走的那个。

老板图什么？图它没熟的时候能撕成一丝一丝的，看着像肉。可他没告诉你，切这玩意儿会流白胶，粘手上肥皂都洗不掉，得拿食用油搓。

你想想这画面：一个天天喊“告别动物油脂”的素食老板，每天打烊第一件事，是在后厨拎一壶花生油搓手，搓得满手油光，跟刚偷吃完一盘红烧肉似的。

最惨的是有一回他切到个熟的，整个店一股香蕉混榴莲的甜味儿。顾客举着筷子问：“老板，你这猪肉怎么一股水果糖味儿？”

老板想了半天：“这是……吃水果长大的猪。”

You know who you are. You ordered twelve packs off Taobao, waited until every roommate was home, then tore open the sour bamboo shoot sachet like you were declassifying something. You're not hungry. You're making a point. Every slurp comes with the speech: "Smells bad, tastes good." Buddy, we only get the first half. Nobody signed up for the tasting, just the hallway. And you keep saying "it's authentic Liuzhou" like geography is an apology. What does it get you? A spotless pot nobody will borrow, a group chat that goes silent the second you type "anyone want some?", and roommates who suddenly prefer dating people with their own apartments. You came for comfort food. You left with a reputation, a window permanently propped open, and a fridge shelf everyone treats like a crime scene.

Look at you, standing in a night-market line everyone else is fleeing, like you're queuing to get into a fire. You followed that smell on purpose. Three blocks. Upwind. You're the only person alive who reads a warning as a recommendation.

And you always need a witness. "It smells like a sewer but tastes amazing!" Yes, we know. You've said it to every foreigner you've ever met, then filmed their face gagging for content. Your entire personality is a dare you keep winning against tourists.

And what does it get you? A paper cup, a toothpick, some pickled cabbage doing its best, and a jacket that now smells like a porta-potty at a wedding. Then you board the MRT and clear the whole car. You call that bold. The rest of us call it a hazmat incident with chili sauce.

合租房里煮螺蛳粉的，都是同一种人：把“闻着臭吃着香”当人生信条，但只要后半句，前半句全分给室友。

他煮之前还特讲究，关门、开窗、开油烟机，跟拆炸弹似的。然后酸笋包一撕，全白搭。那味儿穿门缝、钻衣柜，第二天你穿着外套去面试，HR问你：“你家住垃圾站旁边？”

他还觉得自己挺克制：“我没加臭，原味。”大哥，原味酸笋就是臭的底线，你跟我讲克制？

最惨的是吃完那一刻。他满足了三分钟，剩下半锅红油汤倒哪？倒马桶，厕所臭三天；倒水池，整栋楼臭一周。

最后合租群里没人骂他，就房东发了一句：“退房时，窗帘按新的赔。”

Let's talk about the stinky tofu people. You smelled it from three blocks away, a smell like a sewer filed a noise complaint, and your brain said: *that's where we're eating.* Your entire personality is "it tastes better than it smells." That's not a review. That's a hostage statement.

You stand on a Taipei night market curb with a paper boat, chopsticks in one hand, phone in the other, filming your own bravery for followers who can't smell it, which is the only reason they're still following you. Tourists do it once for the story. Locals do it every Tuesday, then board the MRT, where forty strangers silently agree to hate them.

And the pickled cabbage on top? That's you pretending you came for vegetables. You didn't. You came to be the deadliest passenger on the scooter.

合租房里煮螺蛳粉的，基本不是柳州人。柳州人懂分寸，在自己家吃。在合租房里煮的，都是刚入教的新信徒：一买就是一整箱袋装，每回还要额外多撕一包酸笋，说“原装的不够劲”。哥们，原装的已经够把燃气报警器熏醒了！

你问他图什么，他永远就一句：“闻着臭，吃着香。”问题是吃的是你，闻的是我们仨。香你独享，臭我们均摊。这叫什么？这叫螺蛳粉式共享经济。

最惨的还是他自己。吃了半年，鼻子早被酸笋腌入味了，啥也闻不出来。第二天去公司开会，一进门领导就抬头：“谁在会议室吃螺蛳粉？”他还跟着一起东张西望地找。

街边吃臭豆腐的人，我观察过，全是一个表情：一边嚼一边皱眉，一边皱眉一边跟你说“闻着臭，吃着香”。哥，这句话你每吃一块都要念一遍，说明你自己也不太信，你这是在给自己做法。

图什么？图那个味儿。可那个味儿你根本不用吃啊，你从摊前路过三米，它已经替你吃过一遍了。

最惨的是吃完。人家吃烤串，擦擦嘴就走；你吃完，嘴擦干净了，味儿还在加班。进电梯，一电梯人开始互相怀疑；回到家，你妈第一句不是“吃饭没”，是“你刚从哪个厕所出来”。

八块钱，买了一身洗不掉的嫌疑。还给你浇了辣椒。

街边吃臭豆腐的人，我观察过，全是传教士。你路过，他嘴里正烫得直哈气，还要腾出一只手拦你：“闻着臭，吃着香！”大哥，这句话我从小听到大，你说得跟刚悟出来的一样。

他图什么？图的就是那个反差。全世界都捂鼻子，就他看透了本质。一块发酵的豆腐，硬是吃出了顿悟的表情。

然后呢？然后他上地铁了。五站路，整节车厢都在低头检查自己的鞋。他还挺得意：凡人，不懂。

最惨的是那根牙签。一碗六块，就配一根，戳到最后一块，辣汤顺着手腕流进袖口。第二天开会他一抬手，领导皱眉：“小王，你家下水道是不是堵了？”

Let's talk about the oat milk people. You're not lactose intolerant. You've never been tested. You just heard cows are bad and almonds are thirsty, so you picked the one grain that sounds like a farm without the farmer. Congratulations: you pay an extra eighty cents to drink liquid porridge with a splash of rapeseed oil, and you call it "cleaner." You switched from almond the exact week a podcast told you California was in a drought. That's not values, that's a trend with a loyalty card. And the best part? You order it with an air of quiet suffering, like the barista should thank you for saving the planet one Barista Edition carton at a time. Your grandmother ate oats so she could survive winter. You drink them so a stranger in line thinks you've been to therapy.

我有个同事，点拿铁必须换燕麦奶，加五块。问他为啥，他说乳糖不耐。上礼拜我亲眼看他干掉一整块芝士蛋糕，面不改色。乳糖不耐？我看你是乳糖不耐“便宜”。

后来他又改口，说是为了健康、为了地球。哥，燕麦奶想打出奶泡，里面得加油，菜籽油。你每天早上花三十八，喝一杯“过了油的燕麦水”，还觉得自己在拯救地球。

最惨的是，小时候你奶奶天天早上给你煮燕麦粥，你嫌弃，说“这是马吃的”。现在你多花五块钱，把粥兑进咖啡里，还拍照发朋友圈。

马都没你讲究。马吃燕麦，至少不用排队。

Let's hear it for the people who switched to almond milk to save the planet. You watched one documentary about cow farts and panicked straight into the arms of a nut that needs a gallon of water apiece. Congratulations: you fled methane and landed on drought. California is cracking like a crème brûlée, and you're out here draining a Central Valley aquifer because you can't make eye contact with a Holstein. And the bees! Billions of them trucked across the country on semis, dying by the hive, so you can tell a coworker you "don't really do dairy." That's not environmentalism. That's relocating the crime scene. You didn't save the Earth. You just moved the guilt somewhere sunnier, slapped a leaf on it, and paid an eighty-cent upcharge for the privilege of feeling better about it.

我发现点燕麦拿铁的人有个共同点：开口前先叹气。“不好意思，换燕麦奶，我乳糖不耐。”你不耐？上周火锅店你一个人干了三个冰淇淋球。

他们图什么？图健康。可燕麦奶为了打出奶泡，要往里加植物油；为了喝着甜，得把燕麦酶解成麦芽糖。你多掏五块钱，买了一杯稀释燕麦粥，外加一勺油。

图环保？说燕麦比奶牛省水。你省下那点水，转头就用纸巾擦了八遍杯口。

下场呢？体检血糖偏高。医生问你早饭吃什么，你说只喝咖啡。医生摇头：“不对，你这是每天早上喝两碗粥，还嫌粥稀，花钱让人给你打了个泡。”

Oat milk people, let's be honest: you're not lactose intolerant. I've watched you eat a whole burrata at brunch. You switched because almond milk got canceled for drinking California dry, and you needed a new personality before anyone noticed you'd had the old one for six years.

You pay eighty cents extra to drink breakfast. Your grandma ate oats so she could afford milk. You're paying more for oats so you can say "I just find it creamier."

And you tell the barista "barista edition, if you have it," like you're ordering a vintage. Same person who reads every label hunting for seed oils. Guess what's in your porridge latte, Kayleigh? Rapeseed oil.

You didn't save the planet. You flew to Lisbon twice this year. You just found a way to sigh at a cow.

You switched to almond milk to save the planet. Bold move, picking the one crop that drinks California like it's an open bar. Every latte you order, a farmer in the Central Valley watches his well go dry and thinks, "At least Kayleigh's being sustainable."

And you didn't save a cow. You just outsourced the suffering to bees, trucked cross-country every February to work themselves to death in an orchard, while you post about dairy being cruel.

You're not after a healthier Earth. You're after the barista hearing you say it. That little pause before "almond, please" is the biggest environmental impact you've ever had.

And now the oat milk people look at you the way you used to look at skim drinkers. You picked a side in the milk war, and you lost.

我有个朋友，为了环保，把牛奶戒了，改喝杏仁奶。天天端着一杯杏仁拿铁，跟我上课：“你知道吗？牛放屁，会导致全球变暖。”

行，牛放屁。那你知道一颗杏仁要喝多少水吗？差不多四升。你每天一盒杏仁奶，等于亲自帮加州又旱了一个夏天。

而且那一盒里，杏仁只占百分之二，剩下全是水。你花三十八块，买的是一瓶被杏仁路过的自来水。

更惨的是，加州的杏仁全靠蜜蜂授粉。每年几百亿只蜜蜂被卡车拉过去打工，累死一大片。

所以我这朋友，替地球省了一头牛的屁，搭进去好几个蜂群。他现在一端起拿铁就心虚，听见“嗡”一声，都想鞠躬道歉。

我有个同事，为了救地球，牛奶戒了，改喝杏仁奶。天天端着杯子说：“我在减少碳排放。”

挺好。就是我查了一下：一颗杏仁，得喝掉好几升水。加州旱成那样，杏仁树还在那儿咕嘟咕嘟地喝。

更绝的是他那盒杏仁奶，配料表上杏仁只占百分之二，剩下全是水。

也就是说，他花三十块买了一盒“泡过杏仁的水”，那几颗杏仁还先喝光了一个村的水。他不是在救地球，他是在帮加州倒腾水。

哦对，杏仁开花全靠租来的蜜蜂授粉，每年一季下来，蜜蜂成片成片地死。

他现在特骄傲：“我从不碰动物制品。”

兄弟，蜜蜂不算动物？

You flew Spirit to Las Vegas to get rich. Sit with that. You paid extra for a carry-on and called it an investment strategy. You've got a blackjack "system" from a YouTube guy filming in his mom's kitchen. You told your wife it's "basically math." Sure. So is a second mortgage.

Here's what you won: a Caesars Rewards card, a "free" buffet you earned by losing eleven hundred dollars, and a room "upgrade" overlooking the Bellagio parking structure. You hit four hundred bucks on a Wheel of Fortune slot at 4 a.m. and fed it right back like it owed you child support.

The pit boss knows your name. That's not respect, that's inventory.

And you'll fly home saying "I basically broke even," which is Vegas for "Please don't check the joint account."

我有个朋友，看了三遍《决胜21点》，觉得自己会算牌，买了张去拉斯维加斯的机票，说要去沙漠里挖金子。

兄弟，人家能在沙漠里建一座城，靠的就是你这种来浇水的。

他到了才发现，赌场里没窗户、没钟，酒还免费。你品，一个地方怕你知道几点、还主动把你灌醉，它是想让你赢吗？

三天后他回来了，钱全没了，就剩一张自助餐券，外加一张小教堂的结婚证，证婚人是“猫王”，新娘是谁他想不起来。

他还安慰自己：“在维加斯发生的，就留在维加斯。”

对，你的钱也是这么想的。

最绝的是候机的时候，他看见登机口旁边还有一排老虎机，又塞进去二十块。拉斯维加斯就是这样，连你走，都要再收一回过路费。

我有个朋友，看了三遍《决胜21点》，就觉得自己是MIT天才，揣着年终奖飞拉斯维加斯，说去“考察”。

兄弟，你连工资条都算不明白，你去算牌？

你也不想想，那是沙漠里凭空盖的一座城：没河、没矿、没工厂，贝拉吉奥的喷泉一天到晚往天上滋，钱哪来的？就是你们这种人！那每一滴水，都是“考察团”的眼泪。

赌场里没钟没窗，他说好啊，能专心。专心到第三天，前台主动给他升了套房。他还挺骄傲，说这是VIP待遇。

不是，那是人家算过了，你值这个价。

回来他跟我说：“在拉斯维加斯发生的，就留在拉斯维加斯。”

我说对，你的钱也是。

You're not going to Vegas to get rich. You're going to Vegas to donate to a fountain show.
