Others make you write code first, then compile your essay, like it's a rocket. One missing bracket and you get an error message written in what I can only call ancient Sumerian.

And the bullet point! You press Enter, and it's indented. Press backspace, and it's gone, along with the formatting of the entire document. Now your title is in a font that doesn't exist.

We didn't make paper obsolete. We just made it harder to align.

办公聊天软件最大的发明，是“在吗”。两个字，没下文。你回“在”，他不说事；你不回，软件告诉他：对方已读。好家伙，等于每人脖子上挂了个监控。

最恐怖是下班后，手机“叮”一声，红点99+，点进去，群里三百人，二百九十九个在发“收到”，剩一个发“👌”。没一个人干活，但所有人都很忙。

领导还爱发语音，一发59秒。不点开，它就在那儿挂着；点开，前40秒全是“呃……那个……”。

最绝的是撤回功能。屏幕上写着“某某撤回了一条消息”，这比不撤回还吓人。全群都在想：他刚才到底说了啥？然后三百个人，同时回了一句：“收到。”

现在上班最累的不是干活，是那句“在吗”。就俩字，没标点，没内容，比恐怖片还吓人。我赶紧回“在”，屏幕上跳出“对方正在输入……”。输入了五分钟，发来三个字：没事了。我这五分钟心跳一百二，他就一句没事了？

还有那个“已读”，谁发明的？这不叫功能，这叫电子手铐。我不是不回，我是在组织语言，我得想怎么回一个“收到”，既显得积极，又不像答应了什么。

最可怕是下班以后，手机一震，红点，我手比脑子快，点开了。领导说：“明天说。”明天说，你今天发什么？你这不是发消息，你这是往我晚饭里撒沙子。

现在上班最累的不是干活，是“在吗”。老板发俩字，后面没了。我说在吧，怕他派活；说不在吧，我头像还亮着。

还有那个“已读”，我已读不回，不是没礼貌，是在组织语言，组织完发现，只能回俩字：收到。

现在全公司就会三句话：收到、好的、辛苦了。吵架也这样，“收到。”“好的。”这比骂人狠多了。

最绝的是下班，手机一震，99+，点进去全是“@所有人，请知悉”。我知悉了，我周末没了。

还有人发错群，手快撤回，系统还贴心提示“某某撤回了一条消息”。平时没人看群，那一秒，全员在线。

Document preparation systems promise you'll just type words and they'll make it pretty. Then you spend four hours figuring out why one paragraph is indented like it's hiding from the others.

You move one image and the whole document rearranges itself like a toddler flipping a board game. There's a table of contents that updates automatically, except when it doesn't, and you'll never learn why. The page break appears exactly where you didn't ask for it, and vanishes where you begged for it.

Some systems are WYSIWYG, which stands for "What You See Is What You Get," a lie so confident it should run for office. Others make you write code to get a bold word, which is like being asked to build a car so you can drive to the mailbox.

And the formatting? Haunted. Delete one invisible character and everything turns purple.

Document preparation systems promise you'll "focus on content." Then you spend six hours on why the figure appears on page nine when you put it on page two. The figure isn't lost. It's floating. It has chosen freedom.

These systems fall into two camps. In the first, you click a button and the whole document rearranges itself like a haunted house. In the second, you write code to make a paragraph, and one missing bracket produces an error message that reads like a ransom note from a Victorian ghost.

Every one of them has a "simple" mode that handles about four things and a "powerful" mode that handles everything except what you need.

And the page numbers? Always wrong. The table of contents? Always confident, and wrong.

You didn't write a document. You negotiated with a bureaucrat who prints.

我发现排版系统这东西，本质上就是跟一个特别有主见的实习生合租。你只想把一张图往左挪两毫米，它说行，然后第三页的字全搬去第九页了。你问它为什么，它说：这是自动的。

我现在一听“自动”两个字就发怵。在排版里，自动的意思就是它说了算。

有的系统号称所见即所得，可我看见的和我得到的，从来没见过面。屏幕上好好的，一打印，页码自己开了个派对。

还有的更狠，要你写代码。你以为自己成程序员了，结果为了一个标题居中，查了四十分钟，最后发现是少了个括号。凌晨两点，我一个成年人，在跟一个标题道歉。

最后老板来一句：“就改一个字。”就一个字！多一个字，多出一行；多出一行，图掉下一页；图一掉，整本书重新来过。

这哪是排版啊，这是搭积木，还是别人踢一脚就全倒的那种。

排版系统这类东西，本质上不是工具，是个有脾气的室友。

我说：“这张图放这儿。”它说：“好的。”然后放到了下一页。

我说：“不是，我要它在这儿。”它说：“明白。”然后把整段文字也请到了下一页。

最离谱的是“所见即所得”。我见到的，从来不是我得到的。屏幕上好好的，一打印全变样。这不叫所见即所得，这叫所见即所骗。

我为了对齐一行字，按了十七下空格。别人一打开，那行字像喝多了，歪在角落。

我就加了一个逗号，整篇文章像地震后重建：标题在第三页，页码在第五页，我的尊严在第零页。

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's incredibly small" is both the product and the excuse. Every press release says "revolutionary," and every follow-up says "promising in mice."

They've been about to change everything since 1995. Stronger than steel! Lighter than air! Cheaper than... well, we'll get back to you on that. Currently priced at roughly one kidney per gram.

The lab demo is always flawless. Then someone says "let's make a pound of it," and suddenly the miracle needs a clean room, a PhD, and a prayer. It works perfectly in a sample you need a microscope to find. Convenient! Can't prove it's not working if you can't see it.

And the funding pitches: "This will revolutionize medicine, energy, computing, and sunscreen." Sunscreen! Your world-changing breakthrough ended up in lotion.

Twenty-five years, billions of dollars, and the biggest consumer impact is a tennis racket that's slightly stiffer.

Truly, the biggest thing about nanomaterials is the hype.

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's very small" counts as a business model.

Every one of them was going to change everything. Cure cancer, power your phone for a year, make bridges out of pencil lead. Then you read the fine print: "Results observed once, in a lab in 2009, at minus 200 degrees, by a guy named Dennis."

They're always "a revolutionary breakthrough" in the press release and "not yet scalable" in the footnotes. Scalable is science for "we made enough to fill a thimble and cried."

And the pitch decks! "Stronger than steel, lighter than air, conducts electricity, also heals your emotional wounds." Sir, it's a smudge.

Meanwhile, the actual products are sunscreen and tennis rackets. We promised a space elevator and delivered a slightly less greasy lotion.

But sure, give them another grant. This time it's 10,000 times thinner, which is exactly how I feel about my patience.

你们用过排版系统吧？就是那种你以为自己在写东西，其实是在跟一个有脾气的室友合租的东西。

有一类叫“所见即所得”。我看见的是图片在这一页，我得到的是图片在下一页，这一页留一大片空白，像是在向极简主义致敬。我就想把图往上挪一厘米，整篇文档像多米诺骨牌一样倒下，目录跑到封面上，页码变成罗马数字。我就改了一个逗号啊！

还有一类更硬核，要你写代码，再编译成文档。它的报错特别真诚：“第47行有问题。”我跑到第47行，没毛病。它又说：“我的意思是，第47行附近的某个地方，具体你自己悟。”

用到最后你会明白，排版系统的哲学就一句话：

你以为是你在排版，其实是它在排你。

我发现排版系统分两种。一种叫“所见即所得”，前提是你什么都别碰。你想把一张图往左挪两毫米，整页文字像受惊的鸽子，哗一下全飞到下一页去了。

另一种更高级，得先写代码再编译。它的逻辑是：我不信你的审美，我只信你的语法。你少个括号，它甩你四十行报错，第一行写着“意外的结尾”。我说我也很意外。

最气的是自动编号。它自动，但不对。你删一段，它从3直接跳到7，你问它，它说：“系统自有安排。”

排版，说白了就是跟一个毫无审美、但极有主见的东西合租。

后来我学聪明了：想对齐，就狂按空格；想换页，就狂按回车。

系统不吭声，但我知道，它在记仇。

Nanomaterials: the only industry where "it's really small" counts as a business model. Every press release says the same thing: "This could revolutionize medicine, energy, and computing!" Could. Could is doing more heavy lifting than the material is.

They're always one breakthrough away. Ten years ago, they were going to cure cancer, power your phone for a month, and build an elevator to space. Today they're in a tennis racket and some sunscreen.

And the lab results! "Incredible properties," they say, "at scale of nine atoms, in a vacuum, at minus 270 degrees, in one grad student's hands, on a Tuesday." Scale it up and it behaves like a Tuesday.

Meanwhile, the funding pitch is just "trust us, it's tiny." Tiny isn't a feature. My dignity is tiny. My savings are tiny. Nobody's throwing me a grant.

Nanomaterials, the only industry where "it's incredibly small" is both the science and the sales pitch. Every few years, a press release announces a material that will revolutionize everything: batteries, medicine, space elevators, your sad little phone screen. Then ten years later, it's in a tennis racket.

The lab demo is always stunning. "Behold, a sheet one atom thick, stronger than steel!" Great. Can you make more than a postage stamp of it? "Not without a grant and a miracle." Can it survive contact with air? "We keep it in a vacuum, like a Victorian child."

And the funding pitches! Everything is "game-changing," "paradigm-shifting," and "poised to disrupt." Poised! Like a diver who's been standing on the board since 2004.

Meanwhile, these materials are so tiny that nobody can see them, which makes them the perfect product: impossible to verify, easy to promise, and somehow always "five to ten years away."

现在只要名字前面加“纳米”俩字，价格立马翻十倍。纳米是啥？十亿分之一米。也就是说，他们卖你的核心卖点是：小。

销售还特严肃地跟我说：“这是实验室里刚出来的高科技。”对，实验室里刚出来，所以到我家就出不来了。

你看这个转化链条：论文里，它能导电、能自洁、能改变世界；到了商品页，它能让你的袜子不臭。从“改变世界”到“改变脚气”，我只能说，路径很清晰，就是缩水。

不过它确实厉害。我买完之后，钱真变成纳米级的了，肉眼根本看不见。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm the future" like a device that makes you look like a scuba diver who got lost on the way to a meeting.

Ten pounds of technology strapped to your face, and what do you get? A sweaty forehead, a red mark that makes you look like you lost a fight with a pair of ski goggles, and the unshakable feeling that everyone in the room is silently judging you.

They promised a revolution. We got a $500 way to be rude at dinner. "Sorry, I'm not ignoring you, I'm just watching a virtual screen that's floating in front of your face."

And the battery life? Two hours. So you spend your whole life tethered to a wall like a dog on a leash, looking like a cyborg who's mid-charge.

The best part is the early adopters. They'll tell you it's "life-changing" while walking directly into a glass door.

Head-worn computers: finally, a way to make a laptop feel like a good idea.

现在只要前面加“纳米”两个字，啥东西都能涨价。纳米袜子、纳米牙膏、纳米床垫，听着像要上火星。你知道纳米是什么意思吗？就是小。小！我小时候也特别小，没人说我是高科技啊。

而且这类材料有个规律：在论文里，能导电、能导热、能治病、能拯救世界；一到超市，变成一双袜子。从实验室到货架，中间就差两样东西：量产，和“你信我”。

我真买过一双纳米抗菌袜，穿三天，臭了。我去找店员，他特别淡定：“我们抗的是纳米级的细菌，您这是厘米级的脚。”

我当场就服了。人家不是骗你，人家是精确地没有帮上忙。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm living in the future" like a forty-pound-feeling brick strapped to your face that leaves a red mark you'll explain to coworkers all afternoon.

They promised us the metaverse. We got a guy named Kyle waving his arms at nothing in a living room, punching a coffee table he can't see.

The battery lasts ninety minutes, which is also how long before you get motion sickness and discover your lunch's second act.

Every one of them says "immersive experience," which is marketing for "you will walk into a wall."

And the glasses versions? You pay a thousand dollars to look like a nerd and get less information than a wristwatch.

Meanwhile your phone, a device that fits in your pocket, sits there like, "I do all of this, and I don't need a head brace."

Head computers: the only technology where the demo is amazing and the owner's closet is a graveyard.

现在只要产品名前面加俩字“纳米”，价格立马翻十倍。我就想不通，纳米是什么？就是小。小到什么程度？小到你看不见。所以它宣传的功效你也看不见，这不是巧了吗？

新闻里说，这类材料强度是钢的一百倍，导电性超强，将来能造太空电梯。好家伙，等了十年，我家小区电梯还天天坏。

在实验室里，它是未来科技。到了超市，就成了“添加0.001%纳米成分”的袜子。这含量，袜子自己都不知道自己有。

最离谱的是，每年都说“即将量产，改变世界”。这话我特别熟，跟我说“下个月开始减肥”是一个级别的。它没改变世界，它就改变了我的钱包。

现在只要产品名字里带“纳米”俩字，价格立马翻三倍。你问它有啥用，商家说：“太小了，肉眼看不见。”那我也看不见效果啊，这逻辑闭环了！

我去过一个发布会，PPT上写着“颠覆整个行业”，我当场就热血沸腾。我问啥时候能量产？对方很诚恳：“预计十年。”十年！我家楼下烧烤摊说“马上好”，都没让我等这么久。

这类材料特别像相亲简历：强度第一，导电第一，导热第一，样样满分。一见面，三分钟就崩了：成本太高，没法量产，咱俩不合适。

最惨的是我们普通人，只能买双“纳米袜子”。穿上以后，脚还是那个味儿，只是现在臭得特别先进。

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "the future" like strapping a laptop to your face and walking into a coffee table.

These things promise to merge the digital and physical worlds, and they do. Physically, you're in a living room. Digitally, you're a cartoon with no legs. Everyone wins except your dignity.

The battery life is perfect for a short movie, provided that movie is a trailer. The headset weighs about as much as a bowling ball, so after twenty minutes you've got the neck of a medieval peasant.

And the sweat! Nobody mentions the sweat. You'll finish a "virtual workout" looking like you were baptized by a rival church.

Then there's the wearer in public, nodding at nothing, pinching the air like a mime at a very specific farmers market.

The ads show people laughing joyfully. In real life, you're alone, clammy, and fighting with a software update while the dog watches in silence, deeply concerned.

Head-worn computers: because nothing says "I'm living in the future" like a four-pound brick strapped to your face. You paid a thousand dollars to feel like a deep-sea diver trapped in your own living room.

The pitch is "escape reality." The reality is you're a grown adult punching at invisible buttons while your dog watches with concern. Your neighbors can see you through the window, swinging at a dragon that isn't there. You look like a mime having a stroke.

And the battery! Two hours of life, then it dies and you're back in your beige apartment, sweaty, with a red rectangle imprinted on your forehead like you lost a fight with a window.

Motion sickness is a feature, apparently. "Immersive nausea."

Every few years someone declares this is the next big thing. It's the Loch Ness Monster of technology: lots of sightings, everyone's excited, and nobody's actually bringing one to dinner.

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "thirty years away" has been a stable business model for sixty years. Every one of them is a revolution that's just about to happen, like a guy at a bar telling you he's finishing his screenplay.

The press release always says "breakthrough." The fine print says "in a laboratory, for four seconds, at a cost of the entire GDP of Portugal."

And the renderings! Gleaming facility, blue sky, two models in hard hats pointing at nothing. Never a parking lot. Never a permitting delay. Never the guy named Gary who says the grid connection is backed up until 2041.

They promise unlimited clean power, and what they deliver is a funding round.

Meanwhile, the old technologies just sit there, ugly and boring, keeping the lights on, while the future ones give TED Talks about how the lights are about to be amazing.

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "thirty years away" has been thirty years away for sixty years. That's not a timeline, that's a hostage situation.

Every few months there's a breakthrough. "Scientists achieve record efficiency!" Record for what? For three nanoseconds, in a basement, at a temperature that would vaporize the basement? Great. My toaster also works for three nanoseconds if you don't care about the toast.

And the headlines! "Could power the world." Could. My cat could also run for office. Doesn't mean I'm buying yard signs.

These technologies are like that guy at a party who says he's about to launch something huge. Ten years later he's still about to, he's just got better slides.

Meanwhile I'm still charging my phone from a wall like a caveman, waiting for the future to finally pick up.

现在流行一种头戴式电脑，说是能让你沉浸在另一个世界。我现实世界都沉浸不进去，周一早上能睁开眼就算很努力了。

戴上以后，你在客厅里又挥手又下蹲，嘴里还喊着"我抓到了！"。旁边的猫看你的眼神，就像看一个刚被公司优化的人。

而且这玩意儿死沉，戴半小时，脖子就开始罢工。你以为你在探索宇宙，其实是在给自己的颈椎办追悼会。

最离谱的是广告，人家戴着它在咖啡馆办公。哥们儿，你脸上绑着一块砖，咖啡馆没报警，不是因为他们宽容，是以为你在cos。

现在流行一种头戴式电脑，说白了就是往脸上扣块砖，然后告诉你：这是未来。

我就不懂了，电脑发展这么多年，从一个房间那么大，缩到手机这么小，大家都夸这是进步。结果现在说，来，咱倒回去，挂脸上。

戴上以后，你就成了全家最孤独的人。你在里面开会、看电影、逛什么虚拟办公室，外面你老婆看你：一个大男人站在客厅中间，对着空气比划，跟鬼谈判似的。

而且这玩意儿沉。戴半小时，脖子开始抗议。你以为你进入了新世界，其实你在做颈椎极限挑战。

最绝的是摘下来那一下，脑门上一道红印，像被未来盖了个章：“此人已体验。”

厂家还跟我说，它能解放你的双手。对，手是解放了，脖子被绑架了。

现在有种东西叫头戴式电脑，广告说能让你“沉浸在另一个世界”。我现在这个世界都没混明白，你让我去哪个新世界？

戴上以后，你自己觉得很高科技，在别人眼里，就是一个脸上扣了块砖的人，站在客厅中间对着空气打太极。你老婆一进门，看见你“啊！啊！”地乱挥手，她不会觉得你在体验未来，她在想要不要给你家人打电话。

还说是电脑。以前笔记本烫腿，现在好了，进化了，烫脸。戴半小时摘下来，脑门上一道红印，像被盖了个章：此人已阅，无药可救。

最气人的是它说“解放双手”。我手是解放了，可我天天在空中点来点去，像在给一个看不见的菩萨上香。

科技的尽头，就是花一大笔钱，把自己关进一个只有你能看见的房间。这不叫未来，这叫更贵的躲起来。

现在有种东西叫头戴式电脑，就是把电脑戴脸上。人类科技几十年，一直在让电脑变小：从一个房间，到一张桌子，到一个口袋。结果有人说，太方便了，咱绑回脑袋上去。

广告里的人戴着它，在客厅里挥手，笑得特别开心。可现实里看，就是一个人蒙着眼，在家里打太极，打着打着撞上茶几。

这东西还沉，戴半小时，脖子开始跟你商量要不要辞职。摘下来，脸上一圈印子，像刚潜完水，还是在客厅潜的。

最扎心的是价格，贵得像二手车。买回来第一周天天戴，第二周放柜顶，第三周落灰。第四周我上二手平台一看，一百个同款，全写着："几乎全新，只用过三次。"

这哪是电脑，这是一群人的集体谎话。

Future energy technologies are the only industry where "twenty years away" has been the official timeline for sixty years. It's like a guy who's been "almost done" with his basement since 1987.

Every one of them has a documentary. Every one has a guy with a TED Talk, a turtleneck, and a prototype the size of a microwave that powered a single lightbulb for four seconds. And the headline says "Breakthrough!" Sir, that's not a breakthrough, that's a very expensive nightlight.

They always say it'll be "clean, limitless, and cheap." Pick one. Maybe two on a good day. Nobody's ever gotten all three, which is why the press release has more energy than the product.

Meanwhile, I can't get my phone to last until dinner, and you're telling me we're going to power civilization with a miracle? My phone can't even survive me watching a video of the miracle.

Still, keep going. We believe in you. We just don't believe in your schedule.

Future energy technologies are the most confident group of overachievers I've ever met. They've been "ten years away" for fifty years. That's not a timeline, that's a hostage note.

Every one of them has a breakthrough announced weekly. "Scientists achieve record efficiency!" Of what? "For eleven nanoseconds, in a lab, in Switzerland, at a cost of four million dollars." Great. My toaster also works in a lab in Switzerland.

And the renderings! Always a gleaming facility in a meadow, with a lone deer staring at it, and a family of four in matching sweaters walking by like it's a spa. Meanwhile, the real thing is a parking lot, a lawsuit, and a guy named Doug asking for more funding.

They're the friend who says, "I'm about to blow up, just wait." Brother, we have been waiting. The lights stayed on thanks to the boring ones.

你们发现没有，未来能源这类技术，永远活在"未来"里。我小时候就听说"再过三十年就能用上"，现在我三十多了，新闻还是"再过三十年"。这玩意儿跟我谈恋爱似的，我往前走一步，它往后退两步。

而且每次都是"重大突破"。突破什么了？实验时间从零点一秒延长到零点三秒。我手机充电线接触不良，都能撑三秒好吗！

还有发布会，PPT做得那叫一个好，一个小太阳，一圈绿箭头，写着"清洁、无限、零排放"。对，零排放，因为它到现在连电都没发出来过。

所以我现在看这类新闻就一个态度：你先让我家电费账单少一块钱，再来拯救地球。

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at seven thousand existing languages and says, "Yes, but what if it had a hobby-based grammar?"

Every one of them was created to unite humanity, and every one has united roughly forty people in a Discord server arguing about verb tenses. The founder promised world peace. The community delivered a schism over whether the subjunctive needs a subjunctive.

The vocabulary is always a thrilling mix of "regular and logical" and "I needed a word for dragon at 2 a.m." And the sample sentence is always "The cat drinks milk," because nobody has ever been able to say anything else in them.

Learners spend years mastering fluency, only to discover the only native speaker is the creator's kid, who's now in therapy.

It's the only hobby where you build an entire civilization's grammar but still can't order a sandwich.

我特别爱看未来能源的新闻。每年都是"重大突破"，每年都"即将改变世界"。我就问，这个"即将"是多久？科学家说：三十年。我小时候他们就说三十年，现在我都三十了，他们还是说三十年。这个三十年就像手机里那个1%的电量，永远亮在那儿，但你永远用不完。

而且这些技术在实验室里都特别牛。实验室里成功，就跟相亲照片一样，本人一出来你就懂了。

最离谱的是发布会。灯光、直播、空调、自助餐，开三天，耗的电比这技术一年发的都多。

所以我觉得，未来能源已经实现了真正的永动：不是发电，是融资。

我特别爱看"未来能源"的新闻，标题永远是"重大突破！"。点进去一看：实验室里，三个博士，零下两百度，成功点亮一个小灯泡，持续0.8秒。这叫突破？我小时候舔电池，亮得都比它久。

而且这类技术有个共同点：永远"还有三十年"。我小时候专家说三十年后实现，现在我三十了，专家说：还有三十年。这跟我相亲对象一模一样，永远"在路上了"，永远"快了快了"，永远"你再等等"。

最离谱的是，它们张口闭口都是"解决人类能源危机"。可我的手机下午四点就报警了，你先让我出门不用找充电宝，再来拯救地球行不行？

我特别爱看那种新闻：“未来能源技术取得重大突破！”点进去，激动。往下拉：“预计三十年后可商用。”我爸二十年前看的新闻，也是三十年后。这个“三十年”就是个固定汇率，跟朋友说的“下次一定”一样，永远在前面等你。

而且人家说的“突破”，仔细一看，是实验室里稳定运行了四秒。四秒！我憋气都比它久。然后全网欢呼：人类告别能源危机了！我家电表听了都笑了，转得更快了。

发布会上还说“清洁、无限、零成本”。零成本？那你们融资要几十亿干嘛？这能源还没造出来，先把投资人的钱烧光了，这才叫永动。

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at seven thousand existing languages and says, "None of these have my vibe."

Every creator promises a language so logical it will unite humanity. Humanity has since declined, politely, like a coworker's multi-level marketing invite.

The whole community has maybe forty fluent speakers, and thirty-nine of them are arguing in the comments about whether a verb tense is "naturalistic." The fortieth is the creator, who is also the only one who knows what the grammar is.

The dictionary is always 90% words for "sword," "betrayal," and "moonlight," and zero words for "parking validation." Great, I can curse a dragon but I can't order a sandwich.

And the learning curve is brutal. You study for two years, finally reach fluency, and your only conversation partner is a guy named Greg who's also just reading from the textbook.

It's the only language where "native speaker" means "child of a very committed hobbyist."

Constructed languages are what happens when someone looks at eight thousand natural languages and says, "None of these have my exact vibe."

Every one of them promises to unite humanity, and every one ends up with forty speakers, thirty-nine of whom are arguing in the comments about a verb tense.

The founder spent twenty years on the grammar and zero minutes on "Where's the bathroom?" But the language has seventeen words for different kinds of moonlight, and that's what really matters at a border crossing.

They say it's "logical and regular," which is a nice way of saying it has no soul. Real languages have irregular verbs because people have trauma. This one has a flowchart.

And the grand reunion? A convention in a Holiday Inn conference room, where everyone says "hello" perfectly and then switches to English to order lunch.

Constructed languages are what happen when someone looks at eight thousand existing languages and says, "Not one of these understands me."

Every one of them promises to unite humanity, and every one of them has a community of about forty people, thirty-nine of whom are arguing about a verb tense in a forum thread from 2009.

The grammar is always "perfectly logical," which is a bold claim from someone who has never had a conversation that didn't end with "well, actually." Real languages evolved over thousands of years of people yelling across fields. These were invented by a guy named Gary over a long weekend and a bag of pretzels.

And the vocabulary! Half the words are borrowed, and the other half are the creator's cat's name with a vowel on the end.

Their greatest achievement is that you can be fluent and still have no one to talk to. That's not a language. That's a very elaborate way of being alone.

我特别佩服发明人造语言的人。花十年，语法严密，没有一个不规则动词，逻辑完美。发明完他说：这下全人类可以无障碍沟通了。结果呢？全人类没来。

你想啊，真正的语言是怎么来的？是吵架吵出来的，是骂街骂出来的，是妈妈喊孩子全名喊出来的。人造语言有什么？有语法书。没有脏话，你让我怎么吵架？吵到一半还得翻词典：“你……你这个……（翻页）……不符合逻辑的人！”对方都听笑了，这架还怎么吵？

而且学会了去哪用？全世界会的人凑一块儿，聊的第一个话题永远是：“你为什么学这个？”第二个话题是：“这个语言该怎么改进？”

你看，一个为了沟通发明的语言，最大的用途是讨论这个语言本身。这不是语言，这是个永远在开会的会议室。

有人嫌世界上语言太多，沟通不方便，决定自己发明一门，统一全人类。结果呢，世界上的语言从七千种，变成了七千零一种。

而且这种语言特别讲道理：语法没有例外，三个月上手。我就想问，你见过哪个活人说话讲道理的？真正的语言，是几千年来人们吵架吵出来的，这个是一个人在书房里憋出来的。

学成之后你想找人聊聊，全球一搜，会说的人加起来，一个体育场都坐不满，还有一半在群里为一个词尾吵架。

你学外语是为了认识新朋友，学这个是为了认识教你的那个人，然后你俩互相夸对方说得好。

这不叫语言，这叫两个人的暗号。

我特别佩服发明语言的人。我们普通人连自己母语的错别字都改不完，人家直接从零造了一门。动机还特别崇高：让全世界沟通无障碍。结果呢？全世界会说的人凑一块儿，还不够开个像样的同学会。

他们还主打"简单易学，没有例外"。我一听，行，学！学完发现确实没有例外，因为我连个能跟我说话的人都没有，想例外都没机会。

最离谱的是电影里那种外星语，有语法，有词典，还有粉丝。粉丝还能用它吵架。哥们，母语吵架没吵够吗？还要专门换个语种吵，这叫什么，国际化内耗？

而且你发现没，这个圈子里最流利的一句话，永远是："你这个语法不对。"

人造语言这类东西，发明的人都特别有理想：现在世界上语言太多，沟通不方便，我来造一个，大家都用，世界就和平了。结果呢？世界上本来有七千种语言，他一出手，七千零一种。这不叫统一，这叫给联合国多加了个翻译席位。

而且语言是人类几千年吵架吵出来的，每个词背后都有人骂过街。人造的呢，语法规整，没有例外，没有脏话。你堵车的时候怎么用？只能很礼貌地说："前方的先生，您的行为在逻辑上不太合理。"

最惨的是母语者，全世界就那么几个，还都是发明者的孩子。孩子十六岁，爸爸用这门语言说"吃饭了"，孩子用英语回："别烦我。"

这是一门语言第一次被自己的母语者抛弃，而且理由是：太像爸爸了。
